With the belongsToKeyFromRelation flag, the default comes from the field name: author gives author_id.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, 'user', as the relation name.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. Comments of the same user get the same User object:

List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
print(comments.first.user?.name);

The relation is then in toJson(), with the field name in snake_case as the key.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field. It runs one query each time, so use preload() for a list:

await comment.$getRelation('user');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the related row. It does not set the field:

User? activeUser = await comment
    .related<User>('user')
    ?.where('status', 'active')
    .getFirst();

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model:

@BelongsTo(User, eager: true)
User? user;

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text:
associate() sets the foreign key to the key of a saved model. dissociate() sets it to null. Call save() after them:

await comment.associate('user', user).save();
await comment.dissociate('user').save();

The relation field does not change.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas() keeps the comments of a user that matches:

List<Comment> comments = await Comment().whereHas('user',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('name', 'Ann');
}).get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it:

@BelongsTo(User, onQuery: onlyActive)
User? activeUser;

static QueryBuilder<User> onlyActive(User q) {
  return q.where('status', 'active');
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HasMany: the other side of the relation.
  • Serializer: set the JSON shape of a model.
  • Query by relations: filter by the related rows.

docs.title: HasMany
docs.text:
Use HasMany when one row of this table has many rows in another table.

For example, a user has many posts. The other table keeps the foreign key: post.user_id.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add a list field with @HasMany() to the model, and start it as an empty list. The related model has the foreign key column:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
}

@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? title;
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relation.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Set the keys when your columns have other names:

@HasMany(Book, foreignKey: 'author_code', localKey: 'code')
List<Book> books = <Book>[];
Option Default What it is foreignKey {this model}_id, like user_id The column in the related table that points to this model. localKey the primary key of this model The column in this table that foreignKey points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

The default foreign key comes from the class name, also when the table is users.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, 'posts', as the relation name.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. A user with no posts gets an empty list:

List<User> users = await User().preload('posts').get();
print(users.first.posts.length);

The relation is then in toJson(), with the field name in snake_case as the key.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field:

await user.$getRelation('posts');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field:

List<Post> drafts = await user
        .related<Post>('posts')
        ?.where('status', 'draft')
        .get() ??
    <Post>[];

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model:

@HasMany(Post, eager: true)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text:
createRelated(), saveRelated() and saveManyRelated() save related models and set their foreign key:

Post post = await user.createRelated<Post>('posts',
    <String, dynamic>{'title': 'Hello'});
await user.saveRelated('posts', Post()..title = 'Hello');
await user.saveManyRelated('posts', <Post>[first, second]);

Save the user first, because a model with no key throws a StateError.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas() keeps the users that have a post. whereDoesntHave() keeps the users with no post, and has() counts the posts:

List<User> writers = await User().whereHas('posts').get();
List<User> noPosts = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts').get();
List<User> busy = await User().has('posts', '>=', 10).get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it. Two fields can use the same model with other queries:

@HasMany(Post)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

@HasMany(Post, onQuery: onlyActive)
List<Post> activePosts = <Post>[];

static QueryBuilder<Post> onlyActive(Post q) {
  return q.where('status', 'active').orderBy('id', 'desc');
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• BelongsTo: the other side of the relation.
  • Counting relations: count the related rows.
  • Query by relations: filter by the related rows.

docs.title: HasOne
docs.text:
Use HasOne when one row of this table has one row in another table.

For example, a user has one user info row. The other table keeps the foreign key: user_info.user_id.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add a nullable field with @HasOne() to the model. The related model has the foreign key column:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasOne(UserInfo)
  UserInfo? userInfo;
}

@DoxModel()
class UserInfo extends UserInfoGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? address;
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relation.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Set the keys when your columns have other names:

@HasOne(UserInfo, foreignKey: 'owner_id', localKey: 'id')
UserInfo? userInfo;
Option Default What it is foreignKey {this model}_id, like user_id The column in the related table that points to this model. localKey the primary key of this model The column in this table that foreignKey points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

The default foreign key comes from the class name, also when the table is users.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, 'userInfo', as the relation name.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query:

User? user = await User().preload('userInfo').find(1);
print(user?.userInfo?.address);

The relation is then in toJson(), with the field name in snake_case as the key.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field:

await user.$getRelation('userInfo');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the related row. It does not set the field:

UserInfo? info = await user
    .related<UserInfo>('userInfo')
    ?.where('address', '!=', '')
    .getFirst();

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model:

@HasOne(UserInfo, eager: true)
UserInfo? userInfo;

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text:
createRelated() and saveRelated() save the related model and set its foreign key:

await user.createRelated<UserInfo>('userInfo',
    <String, dynamic>{'address': 'Paris'});
await user.saveRelated('userInfo', UserInfo()..address = 'Paris');

Save the user first, because a model with no key throws a StateError.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas() keeps the users that have a user info row. whereDoesntHave() keeps the users without one:

List<User> inParis = await User().whereHas('userInfo',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('address', 'Paris');
}).get();

List<User> noInfo = await User().whereDoesntHave('userInfo').get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it:

@HasOne(UserInfo, onQuery: byId)
UserInfo? userInfo;

static QueryBuilder<UserInfo> byId(UserInfo q) {
  return q.orderBy('id');
}

When there are many related rows, the relation keeps the last row of the query. So this example keeps the row with the highest id.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HasMany: one row with many related rows.
  • BelongsTo: the other side of the relation.
  • Counting relations: count the related rows.

docs.title: ManyToMany
docs.text:
Use ManyToMany when rows on both sides can have many rows on the other side.

For example, an artist has many songs, and a song has many artists. A third table, the pivot table, keeps the links. It has one foreign key to each side.

docs.title: Tables
Defining the relation
docs.text:
Add a list field with @ManyToMany() to each model that needs it, and start it as an empty list:

lib/app/models/artist/artist.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class Artist extends ArtistGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Song)
  List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
}

@DoxModel()
class Song extends SongGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Artist)
  List<Artist> artists = <Artist>[];
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relation.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Set the names when your pivot table or columns have other names:

@ManyToMany(
  Song,
  pivotTable: 'artist_song',
  pivotForeignKey: 'artist_id',
  pivotRelatedForeignKey: 'song_id',
)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

The examples are for @ManyToMany(Song) in the Artist model:

Option Default What it is pivotTable the two class names in A-Z order, like artist_song The pivot table. pivotForeignKey {this model}_id, like artist_id The pivot column that points to this model. pivotRelatedForeignKey {related model}_id, like song_id The pivot column that points to the related model. localKey the primary key of this model The column in artist that pivotForeignKey points to. relatedKey the primary key of the related model The column in song that pivotRelatedForeignKey points to. withPivot none More pivot columns to read, like ['role']. withTimestamps false Read and set created_at and updated_at in the pivot table. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, 'songs', as the relation name.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. A model with no links gets an empty list:

Artist? artist = await Artist().preload('songs').find(1);
print(artist?.songs.length);

The relation is then in toJson(), with the field name in snake_case as the key.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field:

await artist.$getRelation('songs');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field. The query joins the pivot table, so write table.column:

List<Song> songs = await artist
        .related<Song>('songs')
        ?.orderBy('song.title')
        .get() ??
    <Song>[];

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model. Do not set it on both sides, because each side then loads the other side again and again:

@ManyToMany(Song, eager: true)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

docs.title: Reading pivot columns
docs.text:
List the pivot columns in withPivot, then read them with pivot on each related model:

@ManyToMany(Song, withPivot: <String>['role'])
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

for (Song song in artist.songs) {
  print(song.pivot['role']);
}

pivot is empty on a model that the relation did not load. toJson() has a pivot key. Put 'pivot' in hidden to leave it out.

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text:
These methods add and remove pivot rows. Save the model first, because a model with no key throws a StateError.

The ids can be one id, a model, a list of ids or models, or a map of id => pivot values. Each id is used once.

docs.title: Attaching
docs.text:
attach() adds a pivot row for each id. The third argument has the pivot values for each new row:

await artist.attach('songs', 1);
await artist.attach('songs', <int>[2, 3],
    <String, dynamic>{'role': 'singer'});
await artist.attach('songs', <int, Map<String, dynamic>>{
  4: <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'},
});

attach() does not check for a row that is already there. Use sync() or syncWithoutDetaching() when it can be there.

docs.title: Detaching
docs.text:
detach() deletes the pivot rows of the ids and returns the number of deleted rows. With no ids, it deletes every pivot row of the model:

await artist.detach('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
await artist.detach('songs');

docs.title: Syncing
docs.text:
sync() makes the pivot rows match the ids. It returns a PivotSyncResult with the ids of each change:

PivotSyncResult result = await artist.sync('songs', <int>[1, 2, 3]);
print(result.attached); // ids that got a new row
print(result.detached); // ids whose row was deleted
print(result.updated);  // ids whose pivot values changed

A null id or an unsaved model in the list makes sync() throw an ArgumentError, because it would delete every other link. A null list deletes every link.

syncWithoutDetaching() adds links and never deletes:

await artist.syncWithoutDetaching('songs', <int>[4]);

docs.title: Toggling
docs.text:
toggle() adds a row for each id that has none, and deletes the row of each id that has one:

await artist.toggle('songs', <int>[1, 2]);

docs.title: Updating pivot values
docs.text:
updateExistingPivot() sets pivot values on the rows of one id or a list of ids. It returns the number of changed rows:

await artist.updateExistingPivot('songs', 1,
    <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'});

With withTimestamps, attach(), sync() and toggle() set the pivot timestamps, and updateExistingPivot() sets updated_at.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas() keeps the artists that have a song. It checks the pivot table for you:

List<Artist> artists = await Artist().whereHas('songs',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('title', 'Yesterday');
}).get();

List<Artist> noSongs = await Artist().whereDoesntHave('songs').get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it. Write table.column, because the query joins the pivot table:

@ManyToMany(Song, onQuery: onlyPublished)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

static QueryBuilder<Song> onlyPublished(Song q) {
  return q.where('song.status', 'published');
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HasMany: a relation with no pivot table.
  • Schema: make the pivot table.
  • Counting relations: count the related rows.

docs.title: Polymorphic
docs.text:
Use a polymorphic relation when one model can belong to more than one other model.

For example, a comment can belong to a photo or to a video. The comment table keeps the id in commentable_id and the type, like photo, in commentable_type. commentable is the morph name, and you pick it.

docs.title: Tables
The morph map
docs.text:
The morph map gives each model the type name that goes in the type column. Set it in the setup() of a provider, so it runs in every isolate:

class MorphMapProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Model.morphMap(<String, Model<dynamic> Function()>{
      'photo': Photo.new,
      'video': Video.new,
    });
  }
}

@MorphTo throws without the map. Without it, the other relations store the class name, which changes when you rename the class or build with --obfuscate. Do not change a type name later, because then the old rows do not match.

A queue worker or a CLI command that reads these relations must set the map too. merge: false removes the names you set before.

docs.title: Defining the relation
docs.text:
A photo has many comments. Use @MorphMany, with the morph name as the second argument:

lib/app/models/photo/photo.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class Photo extends PhotoGenerator {
  @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
}

For one row, use @MorphOne. When there are many rows, it keeps the last row of the query:

@MorphOne(Image, 'imageable')
Image? cover;

A comment belongs to a photo or a video. Use @MorphTo on a Model<dynamic>? field. The id and type columns must be @Column fields:

lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? commentableId;

  @Column()
  String? commentableType;

  @MorphTo()
  Model<dynamic>? commentable;
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relation.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The examples are for @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable') in the Photo model. @MorphOne has the same options:

Option Default What it is name (2nd argument) required The morph name, like commentable. typeColumn {name}_type The type column in comment. idColumn {name}_id The id column in comment. localKey the primary key of this model The column in photo that idColumn points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

The options of @MorphTo:

Option Default What it is name the field name in snake_case The morph name. typeColumn {name}_type The type column in this table. idColumn {name}_id The id column in this table. ownerKey the primary key of the related model The column in the related table that idColumn points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query of each type. eager false Load the relation on every query.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, like 'comments' or 'commentable', as the relation name.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query. A @MorphTo runs one query for each type:

List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('commentable').get();
for (Comment c in comments) {
  if (c.commentable is Photo) print((c.commentable as Photo).title);
}

A type that is not in the morph map throws a StateError. No type, or an empty type, gives null.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field:

await photo.$getRelation('comments');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field:

List<Comment> recent = await photo
        .related<Comment>('comments')
        ?.orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .get() ??
    <Comment>[];

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model:

@MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable', eager: true)
List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text:
createRelated(), saveRelated() and saveManyRelated() work with @MorphMany and @MorphOne. They set the id and the type column:

await photo.createRelated<Comment>('comments',
    <String, dynamic>{'body': 'Nice'});

A @MorphTo has no associate(). Set the two columns yourself, and get the type with Model.morphTypeOf():

Comment comment = Comment()
  ..body = 'Nice'
  ..commentableId = photo.id
  ..commentableType = Model.morphTypeOf(photo);
await comment.save();

Model.morphModel('video') gives a new model of a type name.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas(), whereDoesntHave() and withCount() work with @MorphMany and @MorphOne. A @MorphTo throws an UnsupportedError:

List<Photo> photos = await Photo().whereHas('comments').get();
List<Video> videos = await Video().withCount('comments').get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. For @MorphTo, it runs for the query of each type, so it takes and returns Model<dynamic>:

@MorphTo(onQuery: notHidden)
Model<dynamic>? commentable;

static Model<dynamic> notHidden(Model<dynamic> q) {
  q.whereNull('hidden_at');
  return q;
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HasMany: a relation to one model.
  • Providers: set the morph map.

docs.title: HasManyThrough
docs.text:
Use HasManyThrough to read rows that are two steps away, through a model in the middle. HasOneThrough is the same, but it gives one row.

For example, a country has many users, and a user has many posts. So a country has many posts through its users.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: Table Columns country id, name user id, country_id post id, user_id, title

docs.title: Defining the relation
docs.text:
Add the field to the first model. The through option is the model in the middle:

lib/app/models/country/country.model.dart
@DoxModel()
class Country extends CountryGenerator {
  @HasManyThrough(Post, through: User)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

  @HasOneThrough(Post, through: User)
  Post? post;
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relation.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Set the four keys when your columns have other names:

@HasManyThrough(
  Post,
  through: User,
  foreignKey: 'home_country_id', // on user, points to the country
  localKey: 'id', // on country
  throughForeignKey: 'author_id', // on post, points to the user
  throughLocalKey: 'id', // on user
)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
Option Default What it is through required The model in the middle. foreignKey {this model}_id, like country_id The column in the middle table that points to this model. localKey the primary key of this model The column in this table that foreignKey points to. throughForeignKey {middle model}_id, like user_id The column in the far table that points to the middle model. throughLocalKey the primary key of the middle model The column in the middle table that throughForeignKey points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

docs.title: Loading the relation
docs.text: The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, 'posts', as the relation name. Soft deleted rows of the middle and the far table are left out.

docs.title: Preloading
docs.text:
preload() loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query:

Country? country = await Country().preload('posts').find(1);
print(country?.posts.length);

The relation is then in toJson(), with the field name in snake_case as the key.

docs.title: Loading on a model you have
docs.text:
$getRelation() loads the relation into the field:

await country.$getRelation('posts');

docs.title: Querying the relation
docs.text:
related() gives a query for the far rows. It does not set the field:

List<Post> posts = await country
        .related<Post>('posts')
        ?.where('post.title', 'Hello')
        .get() ??
    <Post>[];

docs.title: Always loading the relation
docs.text:
Set eager: true to load the relation on every query of the model:

@HasManyThrough(Post, through: User, eager: true)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

docs.title: Saving related models
docs.text: A through relation only reads. Save the middle and the far models with their own relations, like HasMany.

docs.title: Filtering by the relation
docs.text:
whereHas(), whereDoesntHave(), has() and withCount() work too. The query joins two tables, so write the table in front of the column:

List<Country> countries = await Country().whereHas('posts',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('post.title', 'Hello');
}).get();

See Query by relations and Counting relations.

docs.title: Changing the relation query
docs.text:
Give onQuery a static function of the model. Write the table in front of the column:

@HasOneThrough(Post, through: User, onQuery: newest)
Post? latestPost;

static Model<Post> newest(Post q) {
  q.orderBy('post.id');
  return q;
}

With HasOneThrough, the last row of the query wins. So this example keeps the post with the highest id.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HasMany: the direct relation.
  • ManyToMany: a relation with a pivot table.

docs.title: Broadcasting
docs.text:
Broadcasting sends server events to browsers and apps over Socket.IO, on public, private and presence channels.

A client subscribes to a channel. Your code sends an event to the channel, and every client in it gets the event. Broadcasting is part of the dox_socketio package. It is off by default.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Do the Socket.IO setup first. Then turn on broadcasting in the config:

lib/config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  broadcasting: true,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);

Broadcasting works on the / namespace. To use another namespace, call Broadcast.listen(nsp) with it. Broadcast.event sends through the last namespace it got.

docs.title: Channel rules
docs.text:
Private and presence channels need a rule for who can join. Each isolate keeps its own rules, so add them in a provider:

lib/providers/broadcast_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class BroadcastProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Broadcast.channel('orders.{id}', (Object? user, String id) {
      return (user as User).id.toString() == id;
    });
  }
}

Run dart run build_runner build, so the container finds the provider. Without a rule, every private subscribe gets Forbidden. See Authorizing channels.

docs.title: The auth route
docs.text:
A client gets a channel token from the auth route. Add the route with your auth middleware:

lib/routes/api.dart
@override
void register() {
  // POST /api/broadcasting/auth
  Broadcast.routes(middleware: <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()]);
}

The router prefix goes in front of the path. Give path: to use another path. The route answers {"auth": "<token>"}, or 403 when the rule refuses. The token is signed with a key from APP_KEY, and it works for one socket, one channel and one minute.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Broadcast.maxChannelLength 200 the longest channel name a client can subscribe to Broadcast.maxChannelsPerSocket 100 the most channels for one socket Broadcast.tokenLifetime 1 minute how long a token from the auth route works Broadcast.presenceTimeout 2 seconds how long a presence join or leave waits for other servers Broadcast.maxWhisperSize 10 KB the biggest data of a client event, in bytes of JSON

docs.title: Channel types
docs.text: Channel Name Who can subscribe Channel('news') news any client PrivateChannel('orders.5') private-orders.5 a client that passes the rule PresenceChannel('chat.lobby') presence-chat.lobby a client that passes the rule. Members see each other

docs.title: Defining broadcast events
docs.text:
An event is a class with the ShouldBroadcast mixin:

class OrderShipped with ShouldBroadcast {
  OrderShipped(this.order);
  final Order order;

  @override
  List<Channel> broadcastOn() =>
      <Channel>[PrivateChannel('orders.${order.id}')];

  @override
  String broadcastAs() => 'order.shipped'; // default: the class name

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> broadcastWith() =>
      <String, Object?>{'id': order.id};
}

broadcastOn gives the channels. broadcastWith gives the JSON payload, an empty map by default. Do not start an event name with client-, because that prefix is for client events.

docs.title: Authorizing channels
docs.text:
Broadcast.channel(pattern, rule) adds a rule. The pattern has no private- or presence- prefix, and a {name} part matches any text with no dot. The rule gets the user, then one string for each {name} part. It can be async.

  • A private rule returns true to allow.
  • A presence rule returns a map of member info, with an id.
  • Any other result, or an error, refuses.

This presence rule lets any logged in user join a chat room:

Broadcast.channel('chat.{room}', (Object? user, String room) {
  User u = user as User;
  return <String, Object?>{'id': u.id, 'name': u.name};
});

One rule serves both kinds, so orders.{id} checks private-orders.1 and presence-orders.1. When more patterns match, the first rule wins.

docs.title: Your own auth endpoint
docs.text:
To write the auth route yourself, run the rule with Broadcast.authorize, and make the token with Broadcast.authToken:

Object? result = await Broadcast.authorize(user, 'private-orders.5');
if (result == null) throw ForbiddenHttpException();
String token = Broadcast.authToken(socketId, 'private-orders.5');

authorize gives null when the rule refuses. For a presence channel, it gives the member map. Give that map as the third argument of authToken.

docs.title: Broadcasting events
docs.text:
Use broadcast to send an event. Broadcast.event does the same:

await broadcast(OrderShipped(order));
await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order)); // the same

docs.title: Only to others
docs.text:
Use toOthers to skip the socket of the user who made the change. Broadcast.socketId(req) reads the socket id from the X-Socket-ID header:

await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order),
    toOthers: Broadcast.socketId(req));

docs.title: Receiving broadcasts
docs.text:
On the client, use socket.io-client. Subscribe in the connect handler, because after a reconnect the socket has no channels:

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('https://app.example.com', { transports: ['websocket'] });

socket.on('order.shipped',
  (channel, payload) => console.log(channel, payload));
socket.on('connect', () => {
  socket.emit('subscribe', { channel: 'news' }, (ack) => console.log(ack));
});

Events come as (channel, payload), with the name from broadcastAs.

docs.title: Private and presence channels
docs.text:
Get a token from the auth route, then send it as a string in auth. A token works for one socket id, so get a new one in the connect handler:

socket.on('connect', async () => {
  const res = await fetch('/api/broadcasting/auth', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      authorization: `Bearer ${apiToken}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      socket_id: socket.id,
      channel_name: 'private-orders.5',
    }),
  });
  const { auth } = await res.json();
  socket.emit('subscribe', { channel: 'private-orders.5', auth },
    (ack) => console.log(ack));
});

A socket logged in with SocketAuth needs no token. The rule then gets socket.user.

docs.title: Leaving a channel
docs.text:
Send unsubscribe with the channel name:

socket.emit('unsubscribe', { channel: 'news' }, (ack) => console.log(ack));

docs.title: Subscribe errors
docs.text:
The ack of subscribe and unsubscribe is {ok: true} or {ok: false, error}:

error Why channel is missing no channel name channel name is too long over Broadcast.maxChannelLength too many channels over Broadcast.maxChannelsPerSocket already subscribing the server still checks the same channel Forbidden the rule refused, or the token is missing, wrong or old unsubscribed an unsubscribe came during the subscribe presence is not available another server did not answer in time

docs.title: Presence channels
docs.text:
A presence channel tells its members who else is in it. The client gets three events:

Event Arguments When presence:subscribed (channel, members) to the new socket, with all members presence:joining (channel, member) to the others, when a member joins presence:leaving (channel, member) to the others, when a member leaves

A member is {user_id, user_info}, and user_info is the map from the rule:

socket.on('presence:subscribed',
  (channel, members) => console.log(members));
socket.on('presence:joining',
  (channel, member) => console.log(member.user_info.name));
socket.on('presence:leaving',
  (channel, member) => console.log(member.user_id));

A user with two sockets is one member. The member list covers all isolates and servers that share the adapter.

docs.title: Queued broadcasting
docs.text: A queued broadcast goes through your queue, so the request does not wait. Connect the two packages with a hook and a small job.

docs.title: 1. Mark the event
docs.text:
Use ShouldBroadcastQueued in place of ShouldBroadcast:

class OrderShipped with ShouldBroadcastQueued {
  OrderShipped(this.order);
  final Order order;

  @override
  List<Channel> broadcastOn() =>
      <Channel>[PrivateChannel('orders.${order.id}')];

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> broadcastWith() =>
      <String, Object?>{'id': order.id};
}

await broadcast(OrderShipped(order)); // goes to the queue

docs.title: 2. Write the job
docs.text:
The worker runs this job, and it sends the broadcast to the clients:

lib/app/jobs/broadcast.job.dart
import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

@Job()
class BroadcastJob extends DoxJob {
  BroadcastJob({required this.payload});

  final Map<String, dynamic> payload;

  @override
  Future<void> handle() async {
    await Broadcast.deliver(BroadcastPayload.fromJson(payload));
  }
}

Run dart run build_runner build to add the job to the job registry. See queue setup and configuration.

docs.title: 3. Set the hook
docs.text:
Add the hook to setup() of the BroadcastProvider from Channel rules:

lib/providers/broadcast_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

import '../app/jobs/broadcast.job.dart';

class BroadcastProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Broadcast.channel('orders.{id}', (Object? user, String id) {
      return (user as User).id.toString() == id;
    });

    // puts ShouldBroadcastQueued events on the queue
    Broadcast.useQueue(queueBroadcast);
  }

  static Future<void> queueBroadcast(BroadcastPayload payload) async {
    await Queue.dispatch(BroadcastJob(payload: payload.toJson()));
  }
}

With no hook, a ShouldBroadcastQueued event is sent at once.

docs.title: 4. Use the Redis adapter
docs.text: The worker is its own process, so it reaches the clients of the web server through Redis. Set the Redis adapter in SocketIoConfig. The web server and the worker share this config.

docs.title: 5. Run the worker
docs.text:
dart run bin/queue.dart

Deploy the worker with the web app. See run the worker.

docs.title: Broadcasting from other processes
docs.text:
A command has no Socket.IO server. Set an emitter, so Broadcast.event sends through Redis:

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
Broadcast.emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order));

The servers must use the Redis adapter. For a namespace other than /, use SocketIoEmitter(redis).of('/chat'). With no server and no emitter, Broadcast.event throws a StateError.

docs.title: Client events
docs.text:
A client event (a whisper) goes from one client to the other members of a private or presence channel, like "is typing". The server only passes it on. It is off by default, because clients can then send messages to each other:

SocketIoConfig(broadcasting: true, whisper: true);

The client sends client event with {channel, event, data}. The event name must start with client-. The other sockets in the channel get (channel, data):

socket.emit('client event', {
  channel: 'presence-chat.lobby',
  event: 'client-typing',
  data: { name: 'Alice' },
}, (ack) => console.log(ack)); // the ack is optional

socket.on('client-typing', (channel, data) => console.log(channel, data));

Only a subscribed socket can whisper. The sender does not get its own whisper. A refused whisper gets {ok: false, error}, like not subscribed.

The names match the Echo client. Echo sends auth as headers, so log its socket in with SocketAuth for private channels.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Broadcast.fake() keeps the events and sends nothing:

test('shipping an order broadcasts', () async {
  BroadcastFake fake = Broadcast.fake();

  await shipOrder(order);

  fake.assertBroadcasted<OrderShipped>();
  fake.assertBroadcastedOn<OrderShipped>('private-orders.${order.id}');
  fake.assertBroadcastedTimes<OrderShipped>(1);
});
Method Passes when assertBroadcasted<T>([test]) an event of type T was sent. With test, one of them passes it assertBroadcastedOn<T>(name) T was sent on the channel name, with its prefix assertBroadcastedTimes<T>(n) T was sent n times assertQueued<T>([test]) T was sent as a queued event assertNotBroadcasted<T>() no T was sent assertNothingBroadcasted() no event was sent

fake.eventsOf<T>() gives the events, fake.delivered gives the payloads of deliver, and fake.clear() removes them. Broadcast.restore() turns the fake off. Call Broadcast.reset() in tearDown to remove the rules, the emitter and the fake.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Socket.IO: namespaces, rooms and the Redis adapter.
  • Queue: run the worker for queued broadcasts.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
Cache() keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.

A driver is the place where the data is kept, like files, memory or Redis. A store is a driver with a name and its settings.

The cache is in the dox_cache package, which is built into dox_core. You can also use it without Dox.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: A new project already has lib/config/cache.dart, with a file store and a memory store. The CACHE_STORE key in .env picks the default store.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
In an app that has no cache config, run this command:

dox add cache

To pick another default store, add --store=redis (or memory, database). The database option needs dox add orm first.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
A store uses one driver:

Driver Where the data is Shared between isolates file files in a folder (default storage/cache) yes, on the same machine memory a map inside the isolate no redis a Redis server yes, also between machines database a table in your database. See Database store yes, also between machines null nowhere. It stores nothing -

Each isolate has its own memory store. If all isolates and servers must see the same data, use Redis or the database.

Use the memory store for local development and tests only. In production, use the file store on one server, or use Redis or the database.

docs.title: Adding a Redis store
docs.text:
Add a store in the config file. This example adds a Redis store:

lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);

Add the two env keys to lib/config/env.dart, then run dart run build_runner build:

lib/config/env.dart
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;

docs.title: Store options
docs.text:
Driver Options file path (default storage/cache), prefix, encrypt, prune_every and fsync. See Pruning the file store memory max_size: the most items. When it is full, the item used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Also prefix. redis host (default 127.0.0.1), port (default 6379), username, password, db (default 0), tls, pool_size (default 10), max_value_bytes (no limit by default), prefix, encrypt database table, connection, prefix, encrypt, prune_interval. See Database store

A Redis store with no prefix gets <app name>_cache: from APP_NAME. The other drivers use dox_cache:.

docs.title: Redis options
docs.text:
To set another Redis option, like a command timeout, give the store a RedisOptions:

lib/config/cache.dart
'redis': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'redis',
  'options': RedisOptions(
    host: env.redisHost,
    port: env.redisPort,
    commandTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 2),
  ),
},

Do not set host, port, username, password, db, tls or pool_size next to it. That throws an ArgumentError.

Sessions and the rate limit use the same store, so they get these options too.

docs.title: Retrieving items
docs.text:
Read a value with get. The second argument is the default for a missing key:

await Cache().get('foo');            // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default'); // 'default' when missing

docs.title: Checking if an item exists
docs.text:
Check if a key is in the cache:

if (await Cache().has('foo')) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Retrieving many items
docs.text:
Read many keys at once:

await Cache().many(<String>['a', 'b', 'c']); // {a: 1, b: 2, c: null}

docs.title: Retrieve and store
docs.text:
Read a value, or make it and store it when it is missing:

List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);

The value is stored as JSON, so return maps, lists, strings and numbers, not models. For no expiry, use rememberForever.

remember has two options:

  • decode turns the stored JSON back into your type, like decode: (j) => (j as List).cast<String>().
  • lock: true lets only one caller, on all isolates and servers, run the function. The others wait for its value.

docs.title: Serving stale values
docs.text:
Serve an old value while a new one is made in the background. The flexible method takes two durations:

  • For the first duration, the value is fresh. Callers get it as it is.
  • For the second duration, the value is stale. Callers still get it at once, and the function runs one time in the background.
Map<String, dynamic> stats = await Cache().flexible(
  'stats', Duration(minutes: 1), Duration(minutes: 5), loadStats,
);

Pass null as the second duration to keep the old value until a refresh replaces it:

Map<String, dynamic> rates = await Cache().flexible(
  'rates', Duration(minutes: 10), null, fetchRates,
);

docs.title: Retrieve and delete
docs.text:
Read a value and remove it in one step:

dynamic code = await Cache().pull('login_code');

docs.title: Retrieving raw JSON
docs.text:
Get the stored JSON text as it is, to send it back with no decode:

String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}

docs.title: Storing items
docs.text:
Store a value with put. With no duration, the value stays forever:

await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');

A value must be a JSON type. For a model, store model.toJson().

docs.title: Storing an item forever
docs.text:
Store a value with no expiry:

await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});

docs.title: Storing if not present
docs.text:
Store a value only when the key is missing. It returns true when the value was stored:

bool stored = await Cache()
    .add('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

docs.title: Storing many items
docs.text:
Store many values at once:

await Cache().putMany(<String, Object?>{'a': 1, 'b': 2});

docs.title: Incrementing and decrementing
docs.text:
Change an integer. A missing key starts at 0:

await Cache().increment('visits');
await Cache().decrement('stock', 5);

docs.title: Changing the expiry
docs.text:
Give a key a new expiry:

await Cache().touch('foo', duration: Duration(hours: 1));

docs.title: Removing items
docs.text:
Remove one key with forget, or all items of the store with flush:

await Cache().forget('foo');

await Cache().flush();

On Redis, flush deletes only the keys with the store prefix.

docs.title: Using another store
docs.text:
Cache() uses the default store. Call store to use another one:

await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');

docs.title: Cache tags
docs.text:
A tag puts items in a group, so you can remove only that group:

await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag

For many tags, call tags(['a', 'b']).

docs.title: Atomic locks
docs.text:
A lock lets only one request, or one server, run some code at a time:

CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis')
    .lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

The lock is freed after its time, 30 seconds here, also when you never call release().

A memory lock works in one isolate only, and a file lock on one machine only. For many servers, use Redis or the database.

docs.title: Waiting for a lock
docs.text:
Wait for a lock with block. It gives false when the time is over:

if (await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5))) {
  // ...
}

Pass a callback, and block runs it with the lock and then frees the lock. It throws a LockTimeoutException when the time is over:

await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5), buildReport);

To free a lock that another owner holds, use forceRelease().

docs.title: Encrypting the cache
docs.text:
By default the cache keeps plain JSON. To hide the values, add 'encrypt': true to a file or Redis store:

'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'encrypt': true},

The values are encrypted with your app key. When the key changes, old entries read as a miss.

Cache keys and tag names are not encrypted. Someone who can write to the store can copy an encrypted value to another key.

docs.title: Database store
docs.text:
The dox_cache_database package keeps the cache in a table of your database, so all servers share it with no Redis.

Install it and make the table:

dart pub add dox_cache_database
dox cache:table
dox migrate

Give --table=<name> to cache:table for another table name.

Register the driver when the app starts:

import 'package:dox_cache_database/dox_cache_database.dart';

Dox().cache.extend(
  'database',
  DatabaseCacheDriverFactory(Dox().cache.config.encrypter),
);

Then add a store to the config file:

'database': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'database',
  'table': 'cache', // optional, default `cache`
  'connection': 'cache', // optional, default the default connection
  'prefix': 'app:', // optional
  'encrypt': true, // optional
},

Cache calls inside a transaction on the same connection roll back with it. To avoid this, give the store its own connection.

docs.title: Deleting expired rows
docs.text:
Expired rows stay in the table. To delete them in the background, set prune_interval on the store, in seconds:

'database': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'database', 'prune_interval': 3600},

Or call prune() yourself, for example in a schedule:

int deleted = await (store.driver as DatabaseCacheDriver).prune();

docs.title: Pruning the file store
docs.text:
The file store deletes expired files by itself, one time per hour at most.

To clean up more often, call prune() yourself, for example in a schedule:

int deleted = await (store.driver as FileDriver).prune();

Or set prune_every on the store to prune one time in that many writes:

'file': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'file',
  'path': 'storage/cache',
  'prune_every': 1000,
},

docs.title: Faster writes
docs.text:
Each write syncs the file to the disk, which is slow. Turn the sync off with fsync:

'file': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'file',
  'path': 'storage/cache',
  'fsync': false,
},

With the sync off, a power cut can lose the last writes. Keep it on for a store that holds sessions.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: To use a memory store in tests, see Testing.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_cache also works on its own:

dart pub add dox_cache

Make a CacheManager with your stores:

import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': '127.0.0.1',
      'prefix': 'app:',
    },
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store

A CacheStore has the same methods as Cache(), but the duration is a normal argument:

await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));

docs.title: Encryption without Dox
docs.text:
A CacheManager you build yourself needs an encrypter for stores with 'encrypt': true:

class MyEncrypter implements CacheEncrypter {
  @override
  String encrypt(String text) => myEncrypt(text);

  @override
  String decrypt(String text) => myDecrypt(text); // throw on bad input
}

CacheConfig(defaultStore: 'file', stores: stores, encrypter: MyEncrypter());

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
Write a factory and register it with extend. Or add a ready driver with addStore:

class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver());

Your driver extends CacheDriver. It must implement prefix, get, put, add, increment, forget and flush. Override lock to support locks.

docs.title: Closing the cache
docs.text: Call cache.close() to close the connections of every store, like the Redis connections.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Session: keep sessions in a cache store.
  • Rate limiting: the counts live in the default cache store.
  • Testing: a memory store for each test.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
This page shows how to build a Dox app for production and run it safely.

You build the app into a native binary, copy it to a server or a Docker image, and put a proxy in front of it for HTTPS.

Never run production with dart run

dart run and dox serve use the JIT compiler, which is for development. It uses about 25x more memory at start (around 390 MB instead of 16 MB) and starts slower. Always build an AOT binary for production.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
dox build builds your app for production into build/bundle/:

dox build
File What it is build/bundle/bin/server the native binary. It needs no Dart SDK build/bundle/bin/queue the queue worker, when bin/queue.dart exists build/bundle/bin/schedule the scheduler, when bin/schedule.dart exists build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (like SQLite) build/bundle/db/ your db/ folder, with no SQLite database files build/bundle/.env.example copy it to build/bundle/.env, or use env variables

Keep bin/ and lib/ together, because the binary loads the native libraries from ../lib. Do not use dart compile exe: it does not run build hooks, so the app has no native libraries.

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text:
Start the binary from the bundle folder. It reads .env and db/ from the folder you start it in:

cd build/bundle
./bin/server

A real environment variable wins over the .env file. A new Dox app runs the migrations in bin/server.dart, before the server starts.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
A new Dox app has this multi-stage Dockerfile. The final image is FROM scratch: only the Dart AOT runtime, the bundle and an empty /tmp.

FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# `dox build` runs build_runner, then builds bin/server.dart,
# bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart into build/bundle.
RUN dart pub global activate dox
RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# The final file tree: /app/bin, /app/lib, /app/db, /app/storage and
# a writable /tmp (uploads bigger than 1 MB go to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/

# The AOT runtime files of the dart image plus the bundle.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

The image has no .env file, so secrets stay out of it. Pass the config as environment variables:

docker build -t my-app .
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env -e DB_HOST=... my-app

docs.title: Docker compose
docs.text:
A new app also has a docker-compose.yml. It runs the app, a queue worker and Postgres:

docker compose up -d --build
  • The compose services set DB_CONNECTION=postgres and DB_NAME=dox. To use this Postgres with dox s, set the same two values in .env.
  • A new app skips the Postgres driver in pubspec.yaml. Remove the dox_postgres_native skip lines first. See Skip unused drivers.

See Docker for a health check in the image.

docs.title: Running the queue worker and scheduler
docs.text:
One build has three binaries. Run each one as its own process:

Process Command web server /app/bin/server (the default CMD) queue worker /app/bin/queue work scheduler /app/bin/schedule work

The image has no shell, so start the other binaries with --entrypoint:

docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env my-app
docker run -d --env-file .env --entrypoint /app/bin/queue my-app work
docker run -d --env-file .env --entrypoint /app/bin/schedule my-app work

In compose, use command: ["/app/bin/queue", "work"]. With no Docker, run ./bin/queue work and ./bin/schedule work in build/bundle. Only the server runs the migrations, so start the server first.

A small app can run the jobs and the schedule inside the server, with QueueConfig(inProcess: true) and ScheduleConfig(inProcess: true). See Running jobs in the web server.

docs.title: HTTPS: put a proxy in front
docs.text:
Dox serves plain HTTP only. Run it on a private port, and put Caddy or nginx in front of it for TLS and gzip. When the proxy is on the same machine, set APP_HOST=127.0.0.1:

  1. Client
  2. Caddy or nginxTLS and gzip
  3. Doxa private port
  4. Database

docs.title: Trusting the proxy
docs.text:
Tell Dox to trust the proxy, so req.ip() and req.scheme() show the real client:

AppConfig(
  // the IP of the proxy, or a range like '10.0.0.0/8'
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);

req.ip() then reads X-Forwarded-For, and req.scheme() reads X-Forwarded-Proto. The list is empty by default, so Dox ignores these headers. ['*'] trusts any direct client, so use it only when the app port can not be reached from outside.

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
Caddy gets a certificate for you and sets the forwarded headers. WebSockets work with no extra config:

example.com {
  encode gzip
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
upstream dox {
  server 127.0.0.1:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
  default upgrade;
  ''      '';
}

server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  server_name example.com;

  ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

  # match maxMultipartSize in AppConfig
  client_max_body_size 100m;

  gzip on;
  gzip_types application/json text/plain text/css application/javascript;

  location / {
    proxy_pass http://dox;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;

    # websocket upgrade
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;

    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

    # stream uploads to Dox, do not buffer them in nginx first
    proxy_request_buffering off;
  }
}

server {
  listen 80;
  server_name example.com;
  return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

docs.title: HTTP/2 and gRPC
docs.text:
gRPC needs HTTP/2 between the proxy and Dox. Set http2: true in AppConfig (see HTTP/2). Dox speaks h2c, so the proxy keeps the TLS. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 use the same port.

With Caddy, h2c:// sends HTTP/2 with no TLS to the app:

example.com {
  reverse_proxy h2c://127.0.0.1:3000
}

With nginx, use grpc_pass for the gRPC paths and proxy_pass for the other routes:

server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  http2 on;
  server_name example.com;

  ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

  # Normal routes: HTTP/1.1 to the app
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
  }

  # gRPC service paths only
  location /greeter.Greeter/ {
    grpc_pass grpc://127.0.0.1:3000;
  }
}

The nginx grpc_read_timeout and grpc_send_timeout are 60 seconds by default, and a quiet stream stops after that time. Raise them for long streams.

docs.title: Pass the real Host header
docs.text: The proxy must pass the real Host header, like proxy_set_header Host $host; above. If it sends its own host, the WebSocket origin check gives 403, and back() goes to the fallback.

docs.title: Behind a load balancer
docs.text:
Dox closes an idle connection after 30 seconds. Set idleTimeout longer than the idle timeout of the balancer, or clients can get 502. AWS ALB keeps idle connections for 60 seconds, so use 65 seconds:

AppConfig(
  // ...
  idleTimeout: Duration(seconds: 65),
)

docs.title: Keep it running
docs.text:
When the main isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code. See Isolate. Let a supervisor restart it, like restart: unless-stopped in Docker compose or Restart=always in systemd:

# /etc/systemd/system/dox.service
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/app/build/bundle
ExecStart=/srv/app/build/bundle/bin/server
EnvironmentFile=/srv/app/build/bundle/.env
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: Graceful shutdown
docs.text:
On SIGTERM (docker stop, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, systemd) and SIGINT (Ctrl+C), Dox lets open requests finish. In every isolate it:

  1. stops taking new connections,
  2. lets open requests finish, for shutdownTimeout at most (8 seconds by default),
  3. runs shutdown() of every provider (see Providers),
  4. closes the cache stores of Cache(),
  5. exits with code 0.

A second signal stops the process at once. Set the timeout in lib/config/app.dart:

AppConfig(
  shutdownTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
  // ...
)

Keep it shorter than the time your platform waits before it kills the process:

Platform Waits Change it with docker stop 10 seconds docker stop -t 30, or stop_grace_period in compose Kubernetes 30 seconds terminationGracePeriodSeconds Cloud Run 10 seconds can not be changed Fly.io 5 seconds kill_timeout in fly.toml systemd 90 seconds TimeoutStopSec

docs.title: Stopping in code
docs.text:
Dox().stop() does steps 1 to 4, and the process keeps running:

await Dox().stop();

docs.title: Many processes or machines
docs.text:
One Dox process uses every core. Run more processes only for more machines, or to restart one process with no downtime. List them in the proxy:

upstream dox {
  server 10.0.0.11:3000;
  server 10.0.0.12:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

Socket.IO rooms then need a shared adapter, like Redis.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Docker: a full Docker setup.
  • Deploy to a Linux server: your own server with systemd and Caddy.
  • Deploy to Fly.io: Fly.io.
  • Deploy to Google Cloud Run: Google Cloud Run.
  • Production checklist: what to check before you deploy.

docs.title: Dox CLI
docs.text:
The dox CLI creates projects and files, runs the dev server, builds for production and runs migrations.

Run dox help to see all commands, or dox help <command> for one command. The CLI reference has every command and option.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Install the CLI with dart pub:

dart pub global activate dox

If your shell can not find dox, add the pub bin folder to your PATH in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

docs.title: Updating the CLI
docs.text:
dox update installs the newest version with the same major version as your CLI:

dox update

To remove the CLI, run dart pub global deactivate dox.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
dox create copies the dox-sample template and makes .env with a new APP_KEY:

dox create new_blog
cd new_blog
dart pub get
dox serve

To pick a template release, pass --version <release tag>.

docs.title: Running the dev server
docs.text:
dox serve (or dox s) starts your app and runs build_runner watch:

dox serve

A change in lib/app/ hot reloads into the running server. A change in routes, providers, config, bin/, db/ or generated files restarts the server. Hot reload keeps the old value of a changed static or global value until a restart.

The server prints the VM service link. Open it in a browser to get DevTools, the debugger and the profiler.

Turn off hot reload or build_runner watch with these options:

dox s --no-reload             # restart on every change
dox s --ignore-build-runner   # do not run build_runner watch

See dox serve.

docs.title: Building for production
docs.text:
dox build builds a native (AOT) bundle into build/bundle. Run the server from there:

dox build
cd build/bundle
./bin/server

See Deployment.

docs.title: Creating files
docs.text:
The make:* commands write new files with the right names and folders. So BlogPost makes blog_post.controller.dart with the class BlogPostController.

After make:controller or make:dto, run dox build_runner:build, or keep dox serve running.

docs.title: Controllers
docs.text:
make:controller writes a controller in lib/app/http/controllers. Add -r for all resource methods, --api for the resource methods with no create and edit, and --model to use a model:

dox make:controller Blog
dox make:controller Blog -r
dox make:controller Blog --api
dox make:controller Blog --model=Post

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
make:model writes a model. The options also make the files that belong to it:

dox make:model Blog -m      # model and a create_blogs_table migration
dox make:model Blog -mcr    # model, migration, resource controller
dox make:model Blog -a      # all of the files

The options are -m migration, -c controller, -r resource controller, --api API controller, -f factory, -s seeder and -a all. You can join them, like -mfs. The table is the name in plural snake case, so BlogPost gets blog_posts.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
make:migration writes a Dart migration. Add --sql for a .sql file:

dox make:migration create_blogs_table
dox make:migration create_blogs_table --sql

docs.title: Mail and views
docs.text:
make:mail writes a mailable in lib/app/mail and its view. Add --no-view for a plain text body. make:view writes a .dox.html view:

dox make:mail Welcome
dox make:mail Invoice --no-view
dox make:view pages/about       # resources/views/pages/about.dox.html

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
make:test writes a test that starts the app with DoxTestClient. Add --unit for a plain test:

dox make:test Ping              # test/ping_test.dart
dox make:test Math --unit       # test/math_test.dart

docs.title: Other files
docs.text:
dox make:middleware Auth     # lib/app/http/middleware/auth.middleware.dart
dox make:dto CreateBlog      # lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart
dox make:serializer Blog     # lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart
dox make:provider Cache      # lib/providers/cache_provider.dart
dox make:command send_report # run it with dox app:send-report

docs.title: Listing routes
docs.text:
dox route:list prints every route of the app. Add --json for JSON output:

dox route:list

See dox route:list.

docs.title: Running migrations
docs.text:
The migration commands read the database settings from .env and the real environment. A real environment variable wins:

.env
# postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
# for sqlite: the file path
DB_NAME=postgres
DB_USERNAME=admin
DB_PASSWORD=password

DB_CONNECTION is sqlite by default. A DATABASE_URL wins over all the DB_* keys. See the Env reference.

Run new migrations with migration:run (or migrate). migration:status shows which ones ran:

dox migration:run
dox migration:status

A failed migration stops the run with exit code 1. On MySQL, a CREATE, ALTER or DROP statement saves at once, so a migration that fails half way keeps these changes.

docs.title: Rolling back migrations
docs.text:
migration:rollback undoes the last batch. --step undoes the last N migrations, and --batch undoes one batch:

dox migration:rollback
dox migration:rollback --step=2
dox migration:rollback --batch=3

docs.title: Resetting the database
docs.text:
migration:reset undoes all migrations. migration:refresh undoes all, then runs them again. migration:fresh drops all tables, then runs all migrations:

dox migration:reset
dox migration:refresh
dox migration:fresh

Add --seed to migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh to also run the seeders. The migrate:* names also work, like migrate:fresh.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• CLI reference: every command and option.
  • Add a package: dox add.
  • Package commands: commands that come from a package.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Declare your env keys one time, in a typed class, and read them as normal Dart values.

Each machine needs different settings, like the database password. Keep these values in environment variables or in a .env file, not in your code. Dox reads them through a typed class, so a missing key stops the app at startup.

docs.title: Defining env keys
docs.text:
A new project already has lib/config/env.dart. Its keys are in the Env reference. Each getter is one env key:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'env.g.dart';

enum LogLevel { debug, info, error }

@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) {
    return _$AppEnv.load(reader);
  }

  String get appName;                       // APP_NAME, required
  String get appKey;                        // APP_KEY, required
  int get dbPort => 5432;                   // DB_PORT, default 5432
  bool get appDebug => false;               // APP_DEBUG, default false
  LogLevel get logLevel => LogLevel.info;   // LOG_LEVEL=debug
  Duration get cacheTtl =>
      const Duration(minutes: 5);           // CACHE_TTL=5m
  List<String> get corsOrigins =>
      <String>[];                           // CORS_ORIGINS=a.com,b.com

  @EnvKey('AWS_BUCKET')
  String? get s3Bucket;                     // optional, null when not set
}

/// The env of the app. Read and checked one time, on first use.
final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();

Run dart run build_runner build after each change to the class. It writes env.g.dart. The builder reads only the getters of the class itself, not getters of a superclass or a mixin.

docs.title: Key names
docs.text: The key is the getter name in UPPER_SNAKE case. So appName reads APP_NAME, and dbURL reads DB_URL. To use another name, add @EnvKey('X').

docs.title: Default values
docs.text:
The getter body is the default. It runs only when the key is missing. A default can use another getter. Write the getter directly, not env.appPort, or the app stops with a StateError:

String get appUrl => 'http://localhost:$appPort';

docs.title: Required and optional keys
docs.text:
• A getter with no body is required. A missing key stops the app.
  • A nullable getter with no body, like String? get s3Bucket;, is optional. It is null when the key is missing.
  • An empty value, or the text null, counts as missing.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Type Value in .env String any text int, double, num 3000, 0.5 bool true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off (any case) Uri https://dox.dev Duration a number and a unit: 500ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d. A plain number is seconds. an enum the name of a value, any case: debug List<String> comma separated: a, b, c. Empty items are removed.

Any other type is a build error.

docs.title: Missing or bad keys
docs.text:
At startup, AppEnv.load() checks every key. It throws one EnvException with all missing or bad keys:

EnvException: the env is not valid
  - APP_KEY is missing
  - DB_PORT must be an int

The error shows the key name, never the value.

docs.title: Reading env values
docs.text:
Import the config file and use env:

import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(port: env.dbPort /* int */, ...),
  },
);

Keep only plain keys in the env class. For a computed value, use the app config, like appConfig.isDevelopment.

docs.title: Where values come from
docs.text:
Dox reads values from these places. The first one that has the key wins:

  1. Real environment variables (from the shell, Docker or systemd).
  2. In tests only: the .env.testing file. See Testing: a test database.
  3. The .env file in the folder where you start the app. It is optional.

docs.title: The .env file
docs.text:
The .env file has one KEY=value on each line:

.env
APP_NAME=dox
APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>
DB_PORT=5432
  • Quotes around a value are removed: APP_NAME="My app" gives My app.
  • A line that starts with # is a comment. A # after a space also starts a comment: APP_PORT=3000 # dev gives 3000.
  • COLOR=#fff gives #fff, because no space comes before the #.
  • KEY= gives the default value.
  • export KEY=value also works.
  • A value is on one line only. For a PEM key, put the file path in the env, or use \n with envExpand.

docs.title: Use one value in another
docs.text:
Turn on CoreFlags.envExpand to build a value from other values:

.env
HOST=localhost
PORT=3000
APP_URL=http://${HOST}:${PORT}
GREETING="Hello\nWorld"

${OTHER} works in an unquoted value and in a "..." value. A name that Dox cannot find stays as ${OTHER}. In a "..." value, \n, \t, \", \\ and \$ are escapes.

docs.title: Turning on envExpand
docs.text:
The .env file is read before AppConfig exists. So set the flags in AppConfig and in Env.flags, at the top of main():

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

const CoreFlags flags = CoreFlags(envExpand: true);

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  appKey: Env.get('APP_KEY', ''),
  flags: flags,
  // ...
);
bin/server.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

void main() async {
  Env.flags = flags;
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().startServer();
}

A test does not run bin/server.dart. So also set Env.flags = flags; at the top of main() in each test file:

test/http_test.dart
void main() {
  Env.flags = flags;
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });
  // ...
}

If you forget it, ${OTHER} stays as it is, and Dox prints a warning.

docs.title: Generating the env class
docs.text:
Make lib/config/env.dart from your .env.example:

dox env:generate

Digits become an int default, and true or false become a bool default. An empty value becomes an optional String?. Any other value becomes a required String, so a secret in the example never goes into the code. The command does not overwrite an existing file.

docs.title: Checking the env
docs.text:
Print every missing or bad key. The command exits with code 1 when a key is wrong, so you can use it in CI:

dox env:check

docs.title: The app key
docs.text: Dox uses APP_KEY to encrypt and sign data. Make one with dox key:generate. A missing, short or sample key stops Dox().startServer(). In development and test environments, it only logs a warning.

docs.title: Reading a key by name
docs.text:
Use Env.get() when you know the key name only at run time:

Env.get<String>('APP_KEY');               // '' when missing
Env.get('APP_KEY', 'default_value');
Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000);
Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false); // true, 1, yes, on
Env.get<String?>('AWS_BUCKET');           // null when not set

A missing or empty key gives the default. With no default, int, num, double and bool throw an ArgumentError. Env.get() reads the value again on each call, so do not use it on a hot path.

docs.title: The environment name
docs.text:
Env.appEnv gives APP_ENV in lower case. Env.isTesting is true under dart test, or when APP_ENV=testing is a real environment variable:

if (Env.appEnv == 'staging') {
  // ...
}

An empty Env.appEnv means production.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: To give your own values in a test, see Testing.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Environment variables: every env var that Dox reads.
  • Environments: dev, staging and production config.

docs.title: File Storage
docs.text:
Storage() saves and reads files on a disk: a local folder, AWS S3 (and R2, MinIO, Spaces), or memory.

All disks have the same methods. So you can use a local folder in development and S3 in production, with the same code. Storage is in the dox_storage package. You can also use it without Dox.

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
A new project already has storage. In an older project, run this command:

dox add storage

It writes lib/config/storage.dart, the provider, the storage folder and the STORAGE_DISK=local key. It never overwrites a file.

Add --disk=s3 to also add an s3 disk and the AWS_* keys. STORAGE_DISK stays local, so fill in the keys first, then set STORAGE_DISK=s3.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The disks are in lib/config/storage.dart. STORAGE_DISK in .env picks the default disk. This example adds a url to the local disk, an s3 disk and a memory disk:

lib/config/storage.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storageConfig = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      // for signedUrl(). Without it, url() gives /storage/<path>
      'url': 'https://app.test/files',
    },

    /// only when AWS_BUCKET is set
    if (env.awsBucket != null)
      's3': <String, dynamic>{
        'driver': 's3',
        'bucket': env.awsBucket,
        'region': env.awsDefaultRegion,
        'key': env.awsAccessKeyId,
        'secret': env.awsSecretAccessKey,
        'endpoint': env.awsEndpoint, // R2, MinIO, Spaces
      },
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
);
Driver Use for Options local a folder on the server root (default storage), url, app_key (default: your APP_KEY), visibility, atomic_writes, permissions s3 AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS bucket, region, key, secret, token, endpoint, path_style (MinIO), url (CDN), visibility, acl, batch_delete, unsigned_payload memory tests none

Signed upload URLs work only on S3. The memory disk gives fake URLs.

The provider in lib/providers/ sets up these disks in every isolate:

lib/providers/storage_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';

class AppStorageProvider extends StorageProvider {
  AppStorageProvider() : super(storageConfig);
}

docs.title: The S3 disk
docs.text:
Add the S3 keys to lib/config/env.dart, then run dart run build_runner build. The s3 disk is added only when AWS_BUCKET is set:

lib/config/env.dart
  String? get awsBucket;

  String get awsDefaultRegion => 'us-east-1';

  String? get awsAccessKeyId;

  String? get awsSecretAccessKey;

  /// R2, MinIO or Spaces. Null for AWS.
  String? get awsEndpoint;

Without bucket, key or secret, the app stops at start with an ArgumentError. To save CPU on big uploads, set 'unsigned_payload': true. The signature then does not cover the body, so use it only over HTTPS.

docs.title: Atomic writes
docs.text:
A local disk writes a file in place. With atomic_writes, it writes a temp file and renames it, so a failed upload never leaves a partial file:

'local': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'local',
  'root': 'storage',
  'atomic_writes': true,
},

The rename makes a new file, so the file gets the default mode and owner.

docs.title: Using another disk
docs.text:
Storage() uses the default disk. Use disk to pick another one:

await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports/2026.pdf', bytes, exact: true);

docs.title: Storing files
docs.text:
putFile saves a file in a folder with a new uuid name, and returns the path. It takes a RequestFile or bytes. For bytes, give extension:, or Dox finds it from the bytes:

// returns '/images/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().putFile('images', file); // a RequestFile
Uint8List bytes = Uint8List.fromList(<int>[1, 2, 3]);
String path2 =
    await Storage().putFile('images', bytes, extension: 'png');
String path3 =
    await Storage().put('images', bytes, extension: 'png'); // like putFile

When the bytes are a known format, like png, the extension of the bytes wins over the file name. So a png sent as a.html is saved as .png.

docs.title: Storing with your own name
docs.text:
putFileAs uses your file name. It replaces an old file with that name:

String path4 = await Storage().putFileAs('avatars', file, 'user-1.png');

Do not use the file name from the client, because the name is used as it is.

docs.title: Storing at an exact path
docs.text:
put with exact: true writes to an exact path. It takes a string, a List<int> or a Stream<List<int>>:

await Storage().put('notes/a.txt', 'hello', exact: true);

docs.title: Storing uploaded files
docs.text:
An uploaded file can store itself. store works like putFile, and storeAs works like putFileAs:

RequestFile file = req.input('image');
String path = await file.store('images');
String onS3 = await file.store('images', disk: 's3');
String avatar = await file.storeAs('avatars', 'user-1.png');

putRequestFile and putRequestFileAs on Storage() do the same:

String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', file);
String avatar =
    await Storage().putRequestFileAs('avatars', 'user-1.png', file);

On a local disk, the upload temp file is moved, not read into memory.

docs.title: Prepending and appending
docs.text:
Add text to the end or the start of a file. A missing file is made:

await Storage().append('logs/app.log', 'new line');
await Storage().prepend('logs/app.log', 'first line');

A new line goes between the old and the new text. Change it with separator. Two writers at the same time can lose a write.

docs.title: Retrieving files
docs.text:
get gives the bytes of a file, or null when the file is missing:

Uint8List? found = await Storage().get(path);

docs.title: Checking if a file exists
docs.text:
exists checks for a file. missing is the opposite:

bool exists = await Storage().exists(path);
bool gone = await Storage().missing(path);

docs.title: File metadata
docs.text:
