responses takes status codes as integer keys. For a text key like default or 2XX, use namedResponses. It wins when the same key is in both:

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
    },
    namedResponses: <String, ResponseDoc>{
      'default': const ResponseDoc(description: 'Any other error'),
    });

DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes) adds a basic entry for each route with no docs.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• API docs with OpenAPI: a docs page for your API, step by step.
  • DTOs: the classes that become schemas.

docs.title: PDF Library
docs.text:
Create, load and edit PDF files in Dart with dox_pdf_lib, and send them from a Dox controller.

The package draws text, shapes, SVG paths and images, and it does forms, attachments, metadata, custom fonts, and PDF/A and PDF/X. It has the API of the pdf-lib JavaScript library. To fill pdfme templates, see pdfme.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_pdf_lib

The package uses dart:ffi and a small native library. It runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows, not on the web, iOS or Android. The package downloads a ready-built library, so you do not need Rust.

On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer, like Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. On older Linux or on Alpine, build the library with cargo and set its path in your pubspec.yaml:

pubspec.yaml
hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_pdf_lib:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_pdf_lib.so

docs.title: Sending a PDF from a controller
docs.text:
Return a DownloadableFile, and the browser saves the file. Use StreamFile to show the PDF in the browser tab. See Response:

lib/app/http/controllers/report.controller.dart
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

@Inject()
class ReportController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
    PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
    PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
    page.drawText('Monthly report', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 24);

    Uint8List bytes = await doc.save();
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'report.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/report.pdf', (ReportController c) => c.show);

docs.title: Creating and loading a document
docs.text:
Make an empty document with create, or read a file with load:

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();

PDFDocument old = await PDFDocument.load(
    File('in.pdf').readAsBytesSync());

A broken file throws PDFParsingError. An encrypted file throws EncryptedPDFError.

docs.title: Loading an encrypted file
docs.text:
Load it with ignoreEncryption: true. A file with only an owner password is decrypted, and save writes it with no encryption. A file with a user password throws PDFParsingError:

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.load(bytes, ignoreEncryption: true);
print(doc.isEncrypted); // true

docs.title: Keeping the metadata
docs.text:
create and load set the producer and the modification date. They also add a creator and a creation date when the file has none. To keep the metadata as it is, pass updateMetadata: false:

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.load(bytes, updateMetadata: false);

docs.title: Freeing a document
docs.text:
A document is freed when Dart removes the object. To free it now, call dispose:

doc.dispose();

docs.title: Saving a document
docs.text:
save gives the bytes of the file:

Uint8List bytes = await doc.save();

It has three options, all true by default:

Option What it does useObjectStreams Packs objects into object streams, for a smaller file. addDefaultPage Adds one page when the document has none. updateFieldAppearances Draws the form fields again when the form was used.

docs.title: Saving as base64
docs.text:
Get a base64 string, or a data URI with dataUri: true:

String text = await doc.saveAsBase64(dataUri: true);

docs.title: Adding pages
docs.text:
addPage adds a page at the end. Give a size from PageSizes, a width and height in points, or nothing for A4:

PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.Letter);
doc.addPage(<double>[400, 600]);
doc.insertPage(0, PageSizes.A5);
doc.removePage(1);

removePage on a document with no pages throws RemovePageFromEmptyDocumentError.

docs.title: Reading pages
docs.text:
List<PDFPage> pages = doc.getPages();
PDFPage first = doc.getPage(0);
int count = doc.getPageCount();
List<int> indices = doc.getPageIndices(); // [0, 1, 2]

docs.title: Page sizes
docs.text:
PageSizes has the sizes in points, as [width, height]:

Group Names A $4A0, $2A0, A0 to A10 B B0 to B10 C C0 to C10 RA and SRA RA0 to RA4, SRA0 to SRA4 US and other Executive, Folio, Legal, Letter, Tabloid

docs.title: Changing the page size
docs.text:
print(page.getSize()); // (height: 841.89, width: 595.28)
page.setSize(420, 600);
page.setWidth(500);
page.setHeight(700);

getWidth and getHeight read one side. Boxes that had the size of the media box follow the new size.

docs.title: Page boxes
docs.text:
Each box has a get and a set method: media, crop, bleed, trim and art. A box is (x, y, width, height):

page.setCropBox(10, 10, 400, 580);
PDFBox trim = page.getTrimBox();

The page methods are getMediaBox, getCropBox, getBleedBox, getTrimBox and getArtBox, and the same names with set. A missing crop box reads as the media box. A missing bleed, trim or art box reads as the crop box.

docs.title: Rotating a page
docs.text:
The angle must be a multiple of 90 degrees:

page.setRotation(degrees(90));
Degrees angle = page.getRotation();
Function Result degrees(90), radians(1.57) A Degrees or Radians angle. toDegrees(angle), toRadians(angle) The angle as a number. degreesToRadians(90), radiansToDegrees(1.57) A number converted.

docs.title: Moving and scaling the content
docs.text:
page.translateContent(10, 20); // moves what is on the page
page.scaleContent(0.5, 0.5);   // scales what is on the page
page.scaleAnnotations(0.5, 0.5);
page.scale(2, 2);              // page size, content and annotations
page.resetPosition();          // the text position goes back to 0, 0

docs.title: Copying and merging pages
docs.text:
copyPages copies pages of another document. Then add them with addPage or insertPage:

PDFDocument merged = await PDFDocument.create();
for (PDFDocument source in <PDFDocument>[a, b]) {
  List<PDFPage> pages =
      await merged.copyPages(source, source.getPageIndices());
  for (PDFPage page in pages) {
    merged.addPage(page);
  }
}

A page of another document that you did not copy throws ForeignPageError.

docs.title: Placing pages of another PDF
docs.text:
Use a page of another PDF as a background or a template. embedPdf takes bytes, a base64 string or a PDFDocument, and embeds the first page by default:

List<PDFEmbeddedPage> pages = await out.embedPdf(
    File('template.pdf').readAsBytesSync(), <int>[0, 1]);
PDFEmbeddedPage template = pages.first;

PDFPage page = out.addPage(<double>[template.width, template.height]);
page.drawPage(template);
page.drawText('Filled in on top', x: 50, y: 50);

drawPage takes x, y, xScale, yScale, width, height, rotate, xSkew, ySkew, opacity and blendMode. An embedded page has width, height, size() and scale(factor).

docs.title: Embedding loaded pages
docs.text:
embedPage embeds one page. Give a bounding box to clip a part of it, and a matrix [a, b, c, d, e, f] to transform it:

PDFEmbeddedPage part = await out.embedPage(
  source.getPage(0),
  (left: 0, bottom: 400, right: 595, top: 842),
);
List<PDFEmbeddedPage> all = await out.embedPages(source.getPages());

All pages of embedPages must come from one document, or it throws PageEmbeddingMismatchedContextError.

docs.title: Adding text
docs.text:
drawText draws text at a point. A newline starts a new line:

page.drawText(
  'A long line of text that wraps inside 300 points.',
  x: 50,
  y: 700,
  font: bold,
  size: 14,
  color: rgb(0.1, 0.3, 0.8),
  maxWidth: 300,
  lineHeight: 18,
);

The options are color, opacity, blendMode, font, size, rotate, xSkew, ySkew, x, y, lineHeight, maxWidth and wordBreaks. With no font, the page uses Helvetica.

docs.title: Setting the text state
docs.text:
Set the font, size, color, line height and position one time. Then drawText uses them:

page.setFont(font);
page.setFontSize(12);    // default 24
page.setFontColor(grayscale(0.2));
page.setLineHeight(16);  // default 24
page.moveTo(50, 700);
page.drawText('First line');
page.moveDown(16);
page.drawText('Second line');

Also: moveUp, moveLeft, moveRight, getPosition, getX and getY. A font of another document throws an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Word breaks
docs.text:
With maxWidth, a line breaks at a space. Set other break characters for one call with wordBreaks, or for the document with defaultWordBreaks:

doc.defaultWordBreaks = <String>[' ', '-'];
page.drawText(text, maxWidth: 300, wordBreaks: <String>[' ', '/']);

docs.title: Word breaks in Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar
docs.text:
These scripts have no spaces between words. dictionaryWordBreaks gives the index where each word starts:

List<int> breaks = dictionaryWordBreaks('ทุกสองสัปดาห์'); // [3, 6]

The indexes are UTF-16 indexes, like String.substring. The start and the end of the text are not in the list.

docs.title: Standard fonts
docs.text:
The 14 standard PDF fonts need no font file. They have only Latin letters:

PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.timesRoman);
PDFFont same = doc.embedStandardFont(StandardFonts.timesRoman);
Family Values of StandardFonts Courier courier, courierBold, courierOblique, courierBoldOblique Helvetica helvetica, helveticaBold, helveticaOblique, helveticaBoldOblique Times timesRoman, timesRomanBold, timesRomanItalic, timesRomanBoldItalic Symbols symbol, zapfDingbats

fontName gives the PostScript name, like Times-Roman. embedFont also takes that name as a string.

docs.title: Using other fonts
docs.text:
For other languages, embed a TrueType or OpenType font. subset: true puts only the letters you use into the file:

Uint8List bytes = File('NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync();
PDFFont thai = await doc.embedFont(bytes, subset: true);
page.drawText('สวัสดีครับ', x: 50, y: 700, font: thai, size: 20);

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. Use subset: false for a font in a form field that people edit, because a subset has only the letters known at save time.

embedFont also takes a base64 string or a data URI. Font collections (.ttc), WOFF files and CFF2 fonts do not work.

docs.title: Font options
docs.text:
customName replaces the font name in the file. features turns OpenType features on or off:

PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(
  bytes,
  customName: 'BrandFont',
  features: <String, bool>{'liga': false},
);

docs.title: Measuring text
docs.text:
double width = font.widthOfTextAtSize('Hello', 12);
double height = font.heightAtSize(12);
double above = font.heightAtSize(12, descender: false);
double size = font.sizeAtHeight(20);

getCharacterSet gives the code points the font has. encodeText gives the text as a PDFHexString for raw operators. name is the PostScript name of the font.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
Each part is a number from 0 to 1:

Color red = rgb(1, 0, 0);
Color gray = grayscale(0.5);
Color black = cmyk(0, 0, 0, 1);

The functions give an RGB, Grayscale or CMYK object. A part out of range throws a RangeError.

docs.title: Lines
docs.text:
page.drawLine(
  start: (x: 50, y: 650),
  end: (x: 350, y: 650),
  thickness: 2,
  color: grayscale(0.5),
  dashArray: <double>[4, 2],
);

A line also takes opacity, lineCap, dashPhase and blendMode.

docs.title: Rectangles and squares
docs.text:
A rectangle is 150 by 100 by default. With no color and no border color, it is filled black:

page.drawRectangle(
  x: 50,
  y: 500,
  width: 200,
  height: 100,
  color: rgb(1, 0.9, 0.9),
  borderColor: rgb(1, 0, 0),
  borderWidth: 2,
  opacity: 0.8,
);
page.drawSquare(x: 300, y: 500, size: 50);

docs.title: Ellipses and circles
docs.text:
x and y are the center. An ellipse has the radii xScale and yScale, and a circle has the radius size. Both are 100 by default:

page.drawEllipse(x: 200, y: 300, xScale: 80, yScale: 40);
page.drawCircle(x: 350, y: 550, size: 40, color: cmyk(0.5, 0, 0, 0));

docs.title: Shape options
docs.text:
Option What it does color, opacity The fill. borderColor, borderOpacity, borderWidth The border. borderDashArray, borderDashPhase A dashed border. borderLineCap LineCapStyle.butt, round or projecting. rotate, xSkew, ySkew An angle, like degrees(30). Ellipses and circles take only rotate, and circles take none. blendMode One of BlendMode, see below.

BlendMode has normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, colorDodge, colorBurn, hardLight, softLight, difference and exclusion.

docs.title: Drawing SVG paths
docs.text:
drawSvgPath draws the d attribute of an SVG path. Its y axis points down, as in SVG. With no color and no border color, the border is black:

page.drawSvgPath(
  'M 0,20 L 100,160 Q 130,200 150,120 Z',
  x: 50,
  y: 450,
  scale: 0.5,
  color: rgb(0, 0.5, 0),
);

It takes the shape options, without xSkew and ySkew.

docs.title: Adding images
docs.text:
Embed a PNG or a JPEG, then draw it. The default size is the size in pixels:

PDFImage png = await doc.embedPng(File('logo.png').readAsBytesSync());
PDFImage jpg = await doc.embedJpg(File('photo.jpg').readAsBytesSync());

page.drawImage(png, x: 50, y: 700, width: 100, height: 50);

drawImage also takes rotate, xSkew, ySkew, opacity and blendMode. The embed methods also take a base64 string or a data URI.

docs.title: Image sizes
docs.text:
({double width, double height}) fit = jpg.scaleToFit(200, 200);
({double width, double height}) half = jpg.scale(0.5);
({double width, double height}) full = jpg.size();

width and height of a PDFImage are the size in pixels.

docs.title: Raw operators
docs.text:
pushOperators adds PDF operators to the page content:

page.pushOperators(<PDFOperator>[
  pushGraphicsState(),
  setFillingRgbColor(0.9, 0.1, 0.1),
  rectangle(520, 40, 50, 30),
  fill(),
  popGraphicsState(),
]);
Group Functions State pushGraphicsState, popGraphicsState, setGraphicsState, setLineWidth, setLineCap, setLineJoin, setDashPattern, restoreDashPattern Transform concatTransformationMatrix, translate, scale, rotateDegrees, rotateRadians, skewDegrees, skewRadians Path moveTo, lineTo, appendBezierCurve, appendQuadraticCurve, rectangle, square, closePath Paint stroke, fill, fillAndStroke, endPath, clip, clipEvenOdd Text beginText, endText, setFontAndSize, showText, moveText, nextLine, setCharacterSpacing, setWordSpacing, setCharacterSqueeze, setLineHeight, setTextRise, setTextRenderingMode, setTextMatrix, rotateAndSkewTextDegreesAndTranslate, rotateAndSkewTextRadiansAndTranslate Color setFillingColor, setStrokingColor, and the gray, RGB and CMYK forms, like setFillingGrayscaleColor and setStrokingCmykColor Other drawObject, beginMarkedContent, endMarkedContent

LineJoinStyle has miter, round and bevel. TextRenderingMode has fill, outline, fillAndOutline, invisible, fillAndClip, outlineAndClip, fillAndOutlineAndClip and clip. To make your own operator, use PDFOperator(name, args).

docs.title: Filling a form
docs.text:
getForm gives the form of the document. Get a field by its full name, then set its value:

PDFDocument doc =
    await PDFDocument.load(File('form.pdf').readAsBytesSync());
PDFForm form = doc.getForm();
form.getTextField('person.name').setText('Jane Doe');
form.getCheckBox('agree').check();
form.getRadioGroup('color').select('green');
form.getDropdown('country').select('Myanmar');
File('filled.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await doc.save());

getForm removes XFA data. save draws the changed fields again.

docs.title: Finding fields
docs.text:
List<PDFField> fields = form.getFields();
PDFField field = form.getField('person.name');
PDFField? maybe = form.getFieldMaybe('person.age');

The typed getters are getTextField, getCheckBox, getRadioGroup, getDropdown, getOptionList, getButton and getSignature. A missing name throws NoSuchFieldError, and a field of another type throws UnexpectedFieldTypeError.

docs.title: Field flags
docs.text:
Every field has these methods:

Method What it does getName() The full name, like page1.address.city. isReadOnly(), enableReadOnly(), disableReadOnly() Read-only flag. isRequired(), enableRequired(), disableRequired() Required flag. isExported(), enableExporting(), disableExporting() Export flag. needsAppearancesUpdate() True when the field must be drawn again. defaultUpdateAppearances(font) Draws the field again with a font.

docs.title: Text fields
docs.text:
PDFTextField name = form.getTextField('name');
name.setText('Jane');
name.setAlignment(TextAlignment.center);
name.setMaxLength(40);
name.setFontSize(12);
Method What it does getText(), setText(text) The text. Null or an empty string removes it. getAlignment(), setAlignment(a) TextAlignment.left, center or right. getMaxLength(), setMaxLength(n), removeMaxLength() A longer text throws ExceededMaxLengthError. setImage(image) Shows a PDFImage in the field. setFontSize(size) The font size. updateAppearances(font) Draws the field again with a font. isMultiline(), enableMultiline(), disableMultiline() Many lines. isPassword(), enablePassword(), disablePassword() Hidden text. isFileSelector(), enableFileSelection(), disableFileSelection() A file path. isSpellChecked(), enableSpellChecking(), disableSpellChecking() Spell check. isScrollable(), enableScrolling(), disableScrolling() Scrolling. isCombed(), enableCombing(), disableCombing() One cell for each letter. Needs a max length. isRichFormatted(), enableRichFormatting(), disableRichFormatting() Rich text flag.

docs.title: Check boxes
docs.text:
PDFCheckBox agree = form.getCheckBox('agree');
agree.check();
agree.uncheck();
bool on = agree.isChecked();

docs.title: Radio groups
docs.text:
PDFRadioGroup color = form.getRadioGroup('color');
List<String> options = color.getOptions();
color.select('green');
String? picked = color.getSelected();
color.clear();

Also: isOffToggleable, enableOffToggling, disableOffToggling, isMutuallyExclusive, enableMutualExclusion and disableMutualExclusion.

docs.title: Dropdowns and option lists
docs.text:
A PDFDropdown and a PDFOptionList have the same methods. select takes one option or a list. With merge true, the old selection stays:

PDFOptionList country = form.getOptionList('country');
country.setOptions(<String>['Myanmar', 'Thailand']);
country.addOptions('Laos');
country.enableMultiselect();
country.select(<String>['Myanmar', 'Laos'], true);
List<String> picked = country.getSelected();

A list of many options on a field with no multiselect throws MultiSelectValueError.

Method What it does getOptions(), setOptions(list), addOptions(o) The options. getSelected(), select(o, merge), clear() The selection. setFontSize(size), updateAppearances(font) The look. isSorted(), enableSorting(), disableSorting() Sorted options. isMultiselect(), enableMultiselect(), disableMultiselect() Many selected options. isSelectOnClick(), enableSelectOnClick(), disableSelectOnClick() Save the value on click.

A dropdown also has isEditable, enableEditing, disableEditing, isSpellChecked, enableSpellChecking and disableSpellChecking.

docs.title: Buttons and signatures
docs.text:
A button can show an image. A signature field can only be read, flagged and removed:

PDFButton logo = form.getButton('logo');
logo.setImage(png, ImageAlignment.left);
logo.setFontSize(10);

PDFSignature sign = form.getSignature('signature');

docs.title: Flattening a form
docs.text:
flatten draws every field on its page and removes the fields:

form.flatten();

docs.title: Removing a field
docs.text: form.removeField(form.getField('notes'));

docs.title: Drawing fields with your font
docs.text:
Fields use Helvetica by default (getDefaultFont). For other letters, draw the fields again with your font:

form.updateFieldAppearances(font);

docs.title: Marking fields as changed
docs.text:
save draws the changed fields again. Mark a field by its ref:

form.markFieldAsDirty(field.ref);
form.markFieldAsClean(field.ref);
bool dirty = form.fieldIsDirty(field.ref);

docs.title: XFA data
docs.text:
if (form.hasXFA()) {
  form.deleteXFA();
}

docs.title: Widgets of a field
docs.text:
Each field has widgets, the boxes on the pages. Read them through acroField:

for (PDFWidgetAnnotation w in field.acroField.getWidgets()) {
  PDFBox box = w.getRectangle();
  PDFPage? page = doc.findPageForAnnotationRef(w.ref);
}

A widget also has P() (the page ref), getFlags(), getOnValue() and getAppearanceState(). acroField.getFullyQualifiedName() gives the full name.

docs.title: Creating a form
docs.text:
Create a field by name, then add it to a page. A name can have parents, like a.b.name:

PDFForm form = doc.getForm();
PDFTextField name = form.createTextField('name');
name.setText('Jane');
name.addToPage(page, x: 50, y: 700, width: 200, height: 24);

PDFCheckBox agree = form.createCheckBox('agree');
agree.addToPage(page, x: 50, y: 650, width: 16, height: 16);

The create methods are createTextField, createCheckBox, createRadioGroup, createDropdown, createOptionList and createButton. A name that is already used throws FieldAlreadyExistsError.

docs.title: Adding widgets to a page
docs.text:
addToPage takes x, y, width, height, textColor, backgroundColor, borderColor, borderWidth, rotate and hidden. Text fields, dropdowns, option lists and buttons also take font. A radio group adds one button for each option, and a button takes its caption first:

PDFRadioGroup size = form.createRadioGroup('size');
size.addOptionToPage('small', page, x: 50, y: 600);
size.addOptionToPage('large', page, x: 110, y: 600);

form.createButton('send').addToPage('Send', page, x: 50, y: 500);
Field Default size Text field, dropdown 200 by 50 Option list 200 by 100 Check box, radio button 50 by 50 Button 100 by 50, gray, no border

docs.title: Attaching files
docs.text:
attach adds a file to the document. It takes bytes, a base64 string or a data URI:

await doc.attach(
  File('data.csv').readAsBytesSync(),
  'data.csv',
  mimeType: 'text/csv',
  description: 'The raw data',
);

It also takes creationDate, modificationDate and afRelationship.

docs.title: Reading attachments
docs.text:
for (PDFAttachment file in doc.getAttachments()) {
  print('${file.name}: ${file.data.length} bytes');
}

An attachment also has mimeType, description, creationDate, modificationDate and afRelationship.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
doc.setTitle('Invoice 42', showInWindowTitleBar: true);
doc.setAuthor('Jane Doe');
doc.setKeywords(<String>['invoice', 'paid']);
doc.setLanguage('en-US');
doc.setCreationDate(DateTime.now());
print(doc.getTitle());
Value Set Get Title setTitle getTitle Author setAuthor getAuthor Subject setSubject getSubject Keywords setKeywords getKeywords (one string) Creator setCreator getCreator Producer setProducer getProducer Language setLanguage getLanguage Creation date setCreationDate getCreationDate Modification date setModificationDate getModificationDate Trapped setTrapped(Trapped.yes) getTrapped

Trapped has yes, no and unknown. setTrapped(null) removes the value.

docs.title: Custom metadata
docs.text:
Add your own keys to the document info. A standard key, like Title, throws an ArgumentError:

doc.setCustomMetadata('Client', 'Acme');
String? client = doc.getCustomMetadata('Client');
List<String> keys = doc.getCustomMetadataKeys();
doc.removeCustomMetadata('Client');

docs.title: PDF/A and PDF/X
docs.text:
PDF/A is for long-term archives, and PDF/X is for print. setConformance sets up a document for the standard you pick. You give the ICC profile:

Uint8List srgb = File('sRGB2014.icc').readAsBytesSync();

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
doc.setTitle('Annual report');
doc.setConformance(
  PDFStandard.pdfA2b,
  iccProfile: srgb,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'sRGB IEC61966-2.1',
);

// PDF/A needs fonts from a font file. Standard fonts do not work.
PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(
  File('NotoSans-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync(),
  subset: true,
);
doc.addPage().drawText('Kept for a long time', x: 50, y: 750, font: font);

setConformance also takes outputCondition, registryName and info. A bad profile, or one that does not fit the standard, throws a PDFLibError. After load, call setConformance again before you save.

Standard For Transparency Colors Attachments pdfX1a print no CMYK, gray and spot only no pdfX3 print no must match the profile no pdfX4 print yes must match the profile no pdfA1b archive no must match the profile no pdfA2b, pdfA2u archive yes must match the profile PDF/A files only pdfA3b, pdfA3u archive yes must match the profile any file, with afRelationship

The "u" levels also need Unicode text, which fonts from a font file have. RGB colors need an RGB profile, and CMYK colors need a CMYK profile. label gives the name, like PDF/X-4, and isPDFX is true for the print standards.

docs.title: Printing with PDF/X
docs.text:
PDF/X needs a title and a trim box on each page. For PDF/X-1a, give a CMYK color to every draw call:

doc.setTitle('Flyer');
doc.setConformance(
  PDFStandard.pdfX1a,
  iccProfile: coated,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'FOGRA39',
  registryName: 'http://www.color.org',
);
PDFPage page = doc.addPage(<double>[612, 792]);
page.setTrimBox(9, 9, 594, 774);
page.drawText('Printed in CMYK', x: 50, y: 700, font: font,
    color: cmyk(0, 0, 0, 1));

docs.title: Attaching files to PDF/A-3
docs.text:
Give a relationship and a MIME type:

await doc.attach(
  File('invoice.xml').readAsBytesSync(),
  'invoice.xml',
  mimeType: 'text/xml',
  afRelationship: AFRelationship.data,
);

AFRelationship has source, data, alternative, supplement, encryptedPayload, formData, schema and unspecified.

docs.title: Checking a document
docs.text:
checkConformance lists what is still wrong, with the page and a message. It is not a full validator:

for (ConformanceIssue issue in doc.checkConformance(PDFStandard.pdfA2b)) {
  print('${issue.kind.name}: $issue');
}

An issue has kind, pageIndex (null for the whole document) and message. The kinds of ConformanceIssueKind are fontNotEmbedded, fontNoUnicode, transparency, color, pageBox, encryption, embeddedFile, action, fileId, metadata, version, outputIntent, info, annotation and other.

docs.title: Your own XMP metadata
docs.text:
Save makes the XMP again from the document info, so extra XMP fields of a loaded file are lost. To keep them, start from createXmpMetadata, add your fields, and set the result:

String xmp = doc.createXmpMetadata(standard: PDFStandard.pdfA2b);
doc.setXmpMetadata(addMyFields(xmp));
String? current = doc.getXmpMetadata();

docs.title: Adding an output intent
docs.text:
addOutputIntent adds only the output intent, with none of the other steps of setConformance:

doc.addOutputIntent(
  subtype: OutputIntentSubtype.pdfX,
  iccProfile: coated,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'FOGRA39',
);

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors of the package extend PDFLibError, which has a message. Wrong arguments throw an ArgumentError or a RangeError.

Error When PDFParsingError The file is not a PDF that can be read. EncryptedPDFError load got an encrypted file. RemovePageFromEmptyDocumentError removePage on a document with no pages. ForeignPageError addPage or insertPage got a page of another document. InvalidPDFDateStringError A date in the file is not valid. MissingPageContentsEmbeddingError An embedded page has no content. PageEmbeddingMismatchedContextError embedPages got pages of two documents. NoSuchFieldError, UnexpectedFieldTypeError A field name is missing, or the field is of another type. FieldAlreadyExistsError, InvalidFieldNamePartError A new field name is used or not valid. ExceededMaxLengthError, InvalidMaxLengthError A text or max length does not fit. RichTextFieldReadError, CombedTextLayoutError A rich text or combed field can not be read or drawn. MissingDAEntryError, MissingTfOperatorError A field has no font setting. InvalidAcroFieldValueError, MultiSelectValueError A field value is not valid.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
The same code works in any Dart program. Write the bytes to a file:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
  PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
  PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
  page.drawText('Hello, PDF!', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 30);
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await doc.save());
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• pdfme: fill pdfme templates.
  • Response: send files from a controller.
  • dox_pdf_lib on pub.dev: the package.
  • Source on GitHub: the code of the package.

docs.title: pdfme
docs.text:
Make PDF files from pdfme templates in Dart with dox_pdf_me, and send them from a Dox controller.

You design the template in the pdfme designer, then fill it with data on the server. The package reads the same template JSON as pdfme, and the PDF looks the same. It is built on PDF Library.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_pdf_me

It uses the native library of dox_pdf_lib, so it runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows, not on the web, iOS or Android. On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer. For older Linux or Alpine, see PDF Library setup.

docs.title: Filling a template
docs.text:
Read the template JSON with Template.fromJson, and give one map of inputs for each copy of the template. Return a DownloadableFile, or a StreamFile to show the PDF in the browser tab. See Response:

lib/app/http/controllers/invoice.controller.dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

@Inject()
class InvoiceController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    Map<String, Object?> json =
        jsonDecode(File('storage/invoice.template.json').readAsStringSync())
            as Map<String, Object?>;

    Uint8List bytes = await generate(
      template: Template.fromJson(json),
      inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
        <String, String>{'customer': 'Jane Doe', 'total': '120.00'},
      ],
      plugins: builtInPlugins,
    );
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'invoice.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/invoice.pdf', (InvoiceController c) => c.show);

docs.title: Generating a PDF
docs.text:
generate takes a template, the inputs, the options and the plugins, and gives the bytes of the file:

Uint8List pdf = await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  options: GenerateOptions(lang: 'en', title: 'Invoice'),
  plugins: builtInPlugins,
);

With no plugins, only text schemas work. Pass builtInPlugins for all field types.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Each input map makes one copy of the template. The keys are the schema names, and every value is a string:

Schema type Input value text, select, date, time The text, like 'Jane' or '2026-11-23'. table A JSON string of rows, from jsonEncode(rows). multiVariableText A JSON string of values, like '{"name": "Ann"}'. checkbox, radioGroup, circleMark 'true' to turn it on. image, signature A PNG or JPEG data URL or base64. svg The SVG text. barcodes The data of the code.

A schema with required: true and no value makes generate throw.

docs.title: Options
Building a template
docs.text:
A Template has a base PDF and a list of schemas for each page. Sizes and positions are in millimetres, from the top left corner:

Template template = Template(
  basePdf: const BlankPdf(),
  schemas: <List<Schema>>[
    <Schema>[
      const TextSchema(
        name: 'title',
        position: Position(20, 20),
        width: 170,
        height: 15,
        fontSize: 24,
      ),
    ],
  ],
);

docs.title: Reading and writing JSON
docs.text:
Template.fromJson reads both pdfme formats. Each schema becomes its typed class, and a type with no plugin becomes an UnknownSchema. toJson gives the JSON back, with the keys this package does not know:

Template template = Template.fromJson(json);
Map<String, Object?> back = template.toJson();

Every schema, Position and Sides also has fromJson and toJson.

docs.title: Blank pages
docs.text:
BlankPdf makes blank pages. The default is A4, 210 by 297 mm, with a padding of 10 mm:

const BlankPdf(width: 148, height: 210, padding: Sides.all(5));

docs.title: Static schemas
docs.text:
Static schemas are drawn on every page of a blank base PDF, like a header. Read-only text can use {currentPage} and {totalPages}:

BlankPdf(
  staticSchema: <Schema>[
    const TextSchema(
      name: 'footer',
      position: Position(10, 285),
      readOnly: true,
      content: '{currentPage}/{totalPages}',
    ),
  ],
);

Read-only text also takes input names and dotted paths, like {order.id}, and {date} and {dateTime}.

docs.title: A PDF file as the base
docs.text:
With PdfFile, each page of the file is one page of the template. The schemas are drawn on top:

Template template = Template(
  basePdf: PdfFile(File('form.pdf').readAsBytesSync()),
  schemas: schemas,
);

docs.title: Common schema options
docs.text:
Every schema has these options:

Option What it is name The input key. position The top left corner, like Position(20, 40). width, height The size in mm. rotate Degrees, clockwise. opacity 0 (clear) to 1 (solid). readOnly Shows content and takes no input. required generate throws when the input has no value. content The value of a read-only schema.

Colors are hex strings, like #ff0000, #f00 or #ff000080 with alpha. An empty string means no color, and a bad hex value makes generate throw. Sides(top: 1, right: 2, bottom: 1, left: 2) and Sides.all(1) give a size for each side of a box.

docs.title: Adding text
docs.text:
TextSchema draws text in a box. Long text wraps, and Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar text breaks between words:

const TextSchema(
  name: 'note',
  position: Position(20, 60),
  width: 170,
  height: 30,
  fontSize: 11,
  alignment: Alignment.justify,
  verticalAlignment: VerticalAlignment.middle,
  fontColor: '#333333',
  padding: Sides.all(2),
);
Option Default fontName The fallback font. fontSize 13 points. alignment Alignment.left. Also center, right and justify. verticalAlignment VerticalAlignment.top. Also middle and bottom. lineHeight 1, a factor of the font size. characterSpacing 0 points. fontColor #000000. backgroundColor none. borderColor, borderWidth #000000, no width. padding none. underline, strikethrough false. dynamicFontSize none. See below.

TextSchema also has textFormat, overflow, fontVariants and fontVariantFallback. They are kept in the JSON. Inline markdown is drawn as plain text, and TextOverflow.expand is drawn like visible.

docs.title: Fitting text to the box
docs.text:
DynamicFontSize changes the font size between min and max, so the text fits:

const TextSchema(
  name: 'title',
  position: Position(20, 20),
  dynamicFontSize: DynamicFontSize(
    min: 8,
    max: 40,
    fit: DynamicFontSizeFit.horizontal,
  ),
);

The defaults are 4, 72 and DynamicFontSizeFit.vertical.

docs.title: Text with variables
docs.text:
MultiVariableTextSchema has a text with {name} variables. The input is a JSON string with a value for each variable:

const MultiVariableTextSchema(
  name: 'greeting',
  position: Position(20, 20),
  width: 170,
  height: 10,
  text: 'Hello {name}, welcome to {city}!',
  variables: <String>['name', 'city'],
);
// input: {'greeting': '{"name": "Ann", "city": "Paris"}'}

It takes all text options. When a variable is missing, nothing is drawn. For a read-only schema, content is a JSON string of values. With contentSnapshot: true, content is the text to draw.

docs.title: Select
docs.text:
SelectSchema is a text field with a list of options. It takes all text options:

const SelectSchema(
  name: 'size',
  position: Position(20, 80),
  options: <String>['Small', 'Large'],
);

docs.title: Adding dates and times
docs.text:
DateSchema, TimeSchema and DateTimeSchema format the input with date-fns tokens:

const DateSchema(
  name: 'date',
  position: Position(10, 150),
  format: 'MM/dd/yyyy',
);

They also take locale, fontName, alignment, fontSize, characterSpacing, fontColor and backgroundColor. Month and day names are English for every locale, and weeks start on Sunday.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
ImageSchema draws a PNG or JPEG. objectFit is ObjectFit.contain (default) or cover:

const ImageSchema(
  name: 'photo',
  position: Position(70, 10),
  objectFit: ObjectFit.cover,
  objectPosition: ObjectPosition.centerTop,
);

ObjectPosition has leftTop, centerTop, rightTop, leftCenter, centerCenter (default), rightCenter, leftBottom, centerBottom and rightBottom.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
SignatureSchema is drawn like an image. Its default size is 62.5 by 37.5 mm:

const SignatureSchema(name: 'sign', position: Position(20, 250));

docs.title: SVG
docs.text:
SvgSchema draws the SVG text of the input:

const SvgSchema(name: 'logo', position: Position(10, 10));

docs.title: Drawing shapes
docs.text:
LineSchema, RectangleSchema and EllipseSchema are read-only by default:

const LineSchema(
  name: 'rule',
  position: Position(10, 40),
  width: 190,
  color: '#cccccc',
);
const RectangleSchema(
  name: 'box',
  position: Position(40, 70),
  color: '#b3e5fc',
  borderColor: '#0288d1',
  borderWidth: 1,
  radius: 5,
);
const EllipseSchema(name: 'dot', position: Position(10, 70));

A rectangle and an ellipse take color, borderColor and borderWidth. A rectangle also takes radius.

docs.title: Circle marks
docs.text:
CircleMarkSchema draws a circle line around the box when the input is 'true'. borderWidth is the line width in mm:

const CircleMarkSchema(
  name: 'yes',
  position: Position(30, 100),
  color: '#ff0000',
  borderWidth: 0.5,
);

docs.title: Check boxes and radio groups
docs.text:
Both are on when the input is 'true'. The radio buttons of one group work together in the designer:

const CheckboxSchema(name: 'agree', position: Position(25, 115));
const RadioGroupSchema(
  name: 'small',
  position: Position(25, 125),
  group: 'size',
);

Both take color.

docs.title: Adding barcodes
docs.text:
BarcodeSchema draws a barcode or a QR code as vector shapes. Pick the type with barcodeType:

BarcodeSchema(
  name: 'link',
  barcodeType: BarcodeType.qrcode,
  position: const Position(20, 40),
  barColor: '#000000',
);
Option Default width, height The size of the type, like 30 by 30 mm for a QR code. backgroundColor #ffffff. barColor, textColor #000000. includetext true. The text under the bars.

The types of BarcodeType are qrcode, japanpost, ean13, ean8, code39, code128, nw7, itf14, upca, upce, gs1datamatrix and pdf417. Each has its default width and height, and is2D is true for QR code, Data Matrix and PDF417. barcodeTypes is the list of the type names.

A value that the barcode check refuses, like a bad EAN-13 check digit, draws nothing. A value that passes the check but can not be encoded makes generate throw a BarcodeInputException with a message.

docs.title: Adding tables
docs.text:
TableSchema draws a table. The input is a JSON string of rows:

const TableSchema(
  name: 'items',
  position: Position(10, 170),
  head: <String>['Item', 'Qty', 'Price'],
  headWidthPercentages: <double>[50, 20, 30],
  columnStyles: ColumnStyles(
    alignment: <int, Alignment>{1: Alignment.right, 2: Alignment.right},
  ),
);
// input: {'items': jsonEncode([['Pen', '2', '3.00']])}
Option What it does head The head text of each column. headWidthPercentages The width of each column, in percent. By default, each column gets the same width (30, 30, 40 for the default head). showHead Shows the head (true). repeatHead Shows the head again on each new page (false). tableStyles The outer border: TableStyles(borderColor:, borderWidth:). headStyles, bodyStyles The cell styles: CellStyle.head() and CellStyle.body(). columnStyles Styles by column index, from 0.

On a blank base PDF, a table that is taller than its box goes on over new pages. The schemas below it move down. A row with fewer cells than the head throws.

docs.title: Cell styles
docs.text:
CellStyle.head() and CellStyle.body() take the text options fontName, alignment, verticalAlignment, fontSize, lineHeight, characterSpacing, fontColor and backgroundColor. They also take borderColor, borderWidth and padding. A body style has alternateBackgroundColor for every second row:

const CellStyle.body(
  fontSize: 10,
  alternateBackgroundColor: '#f5f5f5',
);

docs.title: Image columns
docs.text:
A column of TableCellType.image shows PNG and JPEG data URLs. ImageHeightMode.fixed makes the image imageHeight mm high, 20 by default. ImageHeightMode.auto follows the image ratio:

const ColumnStyles(
  cellType: <int, TableCellType>{0: TableCellType.image},
  imageHeightMode: <int, ImageHeightMode>{0: ImageHeightMode.fixed},
  imageHeight: <int, double>{0: 15},
);

ColumnStyles also has verticalAlignment.

docs.title: Using other fonts
docs.text:
Text uses Roboto by default. For other languages, give your fonts in GenerateOptions:

Uint8List noto = File('NotoSansJP-Regular.otf').readAsBytesSync();
Uint8List pdf = await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  plugins: builtInPlugins,
  options: GenerateOptions(
    font: <String, FontSource>{
      'Roboto': FontStore.defaultFont,
      'NotoSansJP': FontSource(noto),
    },
  ),
);

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. A schema picks a font with fontName. Letters that are not in the font show as empty boxes.

docs.title: Font options
docs.text:
One font has fallback: true, and schemas with no fontName use it. subset is true by default, so only the used letters go into the file:

FontSource(noto, fallback: true, subset: false);

In the options JSON, the font data can also be a base64 string or a data URI. Font URLs throw an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Each schema type is a plugin. builtInPlugins has all types, and defaultPlugins has only text. Pick only the plugins you need:

await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  plugins: <String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>>{
    'Text': const TextPlugin(),
    'QR Code': const BarcodePlugin(BarcodeType.qrcode),
  },
);
Plugin Schema type TextPlugin, MultiVariableTextPlugin, SelectPlugin text, multiVariableText, select DatePlugin, TimePlugin, DateTimePlugin date, time, dateTime ImagePlugin, SignaturePlugin, SvgPlugin image, signature, svg LinePlugin, RectanglePlugin, EllipsePlugin, CircleMarkPlugin line, rectangle, ellipse, circleMark CheckboxPlugin, RadioGroupPlugin checkbox, radioGroup BarcodePlugin(type) the barcode types TablePlugin table

findPlugin(plugins, 'qrcode') gives the plugin for a type, or null.

docs.title: Your own schema type
docs.text:
A schema extends Schema, and its fromJson constructor calls Schema.fromJson. A plugin extends SchemaPlugin, reads its schema from JSON and draws it in pdf:

class StampSchema extends Schema {
  const StampSchema({
    required super.name,
    required super.position,
    super.width = 30,
    super.height = 10,
    this.label = 'PAID',
  });

  StampSchema.fromJson(super.json)
    : label = json['label'] is String ? json['label']! as String : 'PAID',
      super.fromJson();

  final String label;

  @override
  String get type => 'stamp';

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> toJson() => <String, Object?>{
    ...super.toJson(),
    'label': label,
  };
}

class StampPlugin extends SchemaPlugin<StampSchema> {
  const StampPlugin();

  @override
  String get type => 'stamp';

  @override
  StampSchema fromJson(Map<String, Object?> json) =>
      StampSchema.fromJson(json);

  @override
  Future<void> pdf(RenderProps<StampSchema> props) async {
    PdfLayout box = PdfLayout.of(props.schema, props.page.getHeight());
    props.page.drawRectangle(
      x: box.x,
      y: box.y,
      width: box.width,
      height: box.height,
      color: rgb(1, 0, 0),
    );
  }
}

Give the plugin to Template.fromJson and to generate:

Map<String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>> plugins = <String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>>{
  ...builtInPlugins,
  'Stamp': const StampPlugin(),
};
Template template = Template.fromJson(json, plugins: plugins);
await generate(template: template, inputs: inputs, plugins: plugins);

The package exports the PDF Library API, so you can use all its drawing methods on the page.

docs.title: Render props
docs.text:
RenderProps has the input value, the typed schema, the basePdf, the page, the document doc, the options, the fonts and a cache. Draw with a built-in plugin on a changed schema with withSchema or copyWith:

await const TextPlugin().pdf(
  props.withSchema(
    TextSchema(
      name: props.schema.name,
      position: props.schema.position,
      fontColor: '#ffffff',
    ),
    value: props.schema.label,
  ),
);

docs.title: Fonts and cache in a plugin
docs.text:
fonts.resolve gives the font name, or the fallback name for null. fonts.embed gives the PDFFont. The cache keeps values for the whole document:

String name = props.fonts.resolve(null);
PDFFont font = await props.fonts.embed(name);

PDFImage? logo = props.cache.get<PDFImage>('logo');
props.cache.set<PDFImage>('logo', image);

fonts.sources has all fonts, and fonts.fallbackName is the name of the fallback font.

docs.title: Layout in a plugin
docs.text:
PdfLayout.of turns the box of a schema into PDF points, with the origin at the bottom left. It has x, y, width, height, rotate and opacity. rotatePoint turns a Point around another one:

PdfLayout box = PdfLayout.of(props.schema, props.page.getHeight());
Point corner = rotatePoint(
    (x: box.x, y: box.y), (x: 100, y: 100), 90);

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
The same code works in any Dart program. Write the bytes to a file:

import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Uint8List pdf = await generate(
    template: Template(
      basePdf: const BlankPdf(),
      schemas: <List<Schema>>[
        <Schema>[
          const TextSchema(
              name: 'title',
              position: Position(20, 20),
              width: 170,
              height: 15),
          BarcodeSchema(
              name: 'link',
              barcodeType: BarcodeType.qrcode,
              position: const Position(20, 40)),
        ],
      ],
    ),
    inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
      <String, String>{
        'title': 'Hello, PDF!',
        'link': 'https://dartondox.dev',
      },
    ],
    plugins: builtInPlugins,
  );
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(pdf);
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• PDF Library: draw and edit PDF files.
  • Response: send files from a controller.
  • dox_pdf_me on pub.dev: the package.
  • Source on GitHub: the code of the package.

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
dox_socketio is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart, and it is the way to do realtime in Dox.

The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package. It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling. In a Dox app, it runs on the same port as your HTTP routes, at /socket.io/. For a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol, use Route.websocket of routing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The quick way is the CLI. It adds the package, the provider, the config and the env key (steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 below). It never overwrites a file:

dox add socketio

Then write a namespace (step 4) and connect a client (step 6). Add --broadcasting to also turn on broadcasting. Without the CLI, do all the steps.

docs.title: 1. Add the package
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: 2. The provider
docs.text:
The provider starts Socket.IO in every isolate. Put it in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/socketio_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/socketio.dart';

class AppSocketIoProvider extends SocketIoProvider {
  AppSocketIoProvider() : super(socketIoConfig);
}

docs.title: 3. The config
docs.text:
The config lists the namespaces to serve:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);
SocketIoConfig option Default What it does enabled true serve Socket.IO at options.path options ServerOptions() see Options namespaces [] NamespaceHandler classes to register adapter none makes one adapter in each isolate, see Many isolates

docs.title: 4. A namespace
docs.text:
A namespace handles the events of one path, like /chat:

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.emit('welcome', <String, dynamic>{'id': socket.id});
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    // everyone in lobby but me
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('message', event.data);
    event.ack('sent'); // answer the client callback
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Turn it on
docs.text:
Add a getter for the SOCKETIO_ENABLED key to lib/config/env.dart:

lib/config/env.dart
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
.env
SOCKETIO_ENABLED=true

Then run dart run build_runner build and dox serve.

docs.title: 6. Connect a client
docs.text:
Use transports: ['websocket'], because long-polling does not work with many isolates. See Many isolates:

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('welcome', (data) => console.log(data.id));
socket.emit('message', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'sent'

Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router, so route middleware does not run for them. To log users in, see Log in a socket.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Give ServerOptions as options to SocketIoConfig, or to SocketIoServer without Dox:

SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: <String>['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(
        origins: <String>['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
Option Default What it does path /socket.io/ the URL path pingInterval 25 s how often the server sends a ping pingTimeout 20 s how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone upgradeTimeout 10 s how long an upgrade from polling to websocket can take connectTimeout 45 s how long the client has to join a namespace maxHttpBufferSize 1,000,000 bytes the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection with code 1009 maxAttachments 10 the most binary parts in one packet. More closes the client transports ['polling', 'websocket'] allowed transports allowUpgrades true let polling clients move to websocket cors none CORS headers for polling requests. With a list of origins, it also checks the origin of websockets allowedOrigins none the sites that can connect, see Allowed origins allowRequest none accepts or refuses each request, see Allow requests and limit sessions maxSessions none the most open sessions per isolate. Set it in production maxAttachmentBytes none the most bytes of all binary parts of one packet. A bigger packet closes the client maxAuthSize none the most bytes of the auth payload. A bigger one gets connect_error (auth payload too large) maxWriteBufferSize none the most bytes kept for a client that does not read. Above it, the session closes ackTimeout none the default timeout of emitWithAck. With none, it waits until the client answers or leaves

On a plain dart:io server, the full message is read before the size check, so also set a size limit in your proxy.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
A namespace is a class, so its dependencies come in through the constructor:

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

// in lib/config/socketio.dart
namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],

docs.title: Namespace middleware
docs.text:
A middleware checks a client before it joins. When it throws a SocketIoException, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data:

@override
List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

void checkToken(Socket socket) {
  if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
    throw SocketIoException('unauthorized',
        data: <String, dynamic>{'reason': 'bad token'});
  }
}

Any other error goes to stderr, and the client gets only {"message": "Internal error"}.

docs.title: Sending from a controller or a service
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider.server is the Socket.IO server of this isolate:

await SocketIoProvider.server?.of('/chat').to('lobby').emit('news', data);

From a queue job or another program, use the emitter.

docs.title: Common methods
docs.text:
The API follows the Node.js server. This table shows where Dart is different:

Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r), socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...), socket.except(r) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same io.local.emit(...) the same: only sockets of this server socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address, .url, .secure, .time, .token, .cookie(name), .session() socket.data socket.data (a map). Keep it JSON, because other servers get a copy await io.in(r).fetchSockets() await io.to(r).fetchSockets() (all servers) await io.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await io.timeout(Duration(seconds: 5)).emitWithAck('e', a) io.serverSideEmit('e', a) await io.serverSideEmit('e', [a]) io.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) (from other servers) io.onServerSideEmit('e', (ServerSideEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.ack(x)

To send binary data, send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps. An event with many values uses emitArgs, emitArgsWithAck and e.ackArgs([a, b]). e.hasAck is true when the client waits for an answer.

docs.title: The state of a socket
docs.text:
socket.connected;   // true while connected
socket.transport;   // 'polling' or 'websocket'
socket.rooms;       // the rooms of the socket
socket.waitingAcks; // acks it still waits for

To stop a handler, call socket.off('message', onMessage). With no handler, all handlers of the event go. nsp.offServerSideEmit does the same for server events.

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text:
The disconnecting and disconnect events give the reason in event.data, like transport close. To close a socket from the server, call disconnect. disconnect(true) also closes the connection under it:

socket.on('disconnect', (SocketEvent e) => print(e.data));
socket.disconnect();

docs.title: Log in a socket
docs.text:
Route middleware, like session and auth, does not run for Socket.IO. Use SocketAuth as a namespace middleware. Your function gets the handshake and returns the user, or null:

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware =>
      <Middleware>[SocketAuth(findUser).handle];

  static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
    String? token = handshake.token;
    if (token == null) return null;
    return User().where('api_token', token).getFirst();
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    User user = socket.user! as User;
    socket.join('user:${user.id}');
  }
}

The client sends the token in auth, because browsers can not set headers on a websocket:

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  auth: { token: 'the-user-token' },
});
socket.on('connect_error', (err) => console.log(err.message)); // 'Unauthorized'

A returned user is kept in socket.user, on this server only. When the function returns null, the client gets connect_error with the message Unauthorized, and onConnection does not run. SocketAuth(findUser, message: '...') changes the message.

The handshake has these helpers:

  • handshake.token is auth.token from the client, else the Authorization: Bearer header.
  • handshake.cookie('name') reads a cookie and decrypts it with APP_KEY. Use decrypt: false for a plain cookie.
  • await handshake.session() gives the Dox session of the client. It uses AppConfig.session, or the SessionConfig you give. Changes are not saved.

docs.title: With dox_auth
docs.text:
dox_auth can check a JWT or the web login session:

static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
  // an API client or a mobile app sends a JWT
  String? token = handshake.token;
  if (token != null) return Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);

  // a browser that logged in on a web page sends the session cookie
  Session session = await handshake.session();
  return Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);
}

A bad, expired or revoked token gives null. The session is read one time, when the socket connects, so call socket.disconnect() yourself after a logout. With userCacheTtl in dox_auth, a banned user can connect until the cache time ends, unless forgetUser runs. With the cookie session driver, an old session cookie works after logout until the lifetime ends.

Cookie login needs allowedOrigins

A browser sends its cookies on a websocket from any website. If you log users in with a cookie, set allowedOrigins to your own sites. Else another website can open a socket as your user.

docs.title: Allowed origins
docs.text:
allowedOrigins sets the websites that can open a socket. Set it when you log users in with cookies:

ServerOptions(allowedOrigins: <String>['https://app.example.com']);
  • None (the default): no extra check. Dox logs a warning at start.
  • []: only pages of the same host can connect.
  • A list of sites: the same host and those sites can connect.
  • ['*']: every site can connect.

Other sites get 403. A client with no Origin header (not a browser) can always connect. cors with * in origins, or no cors, allows websockets from any origin. * with credentials: true throws an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Allow requests and limit sessions
docs.text:
allowRequest runs for every handshake and every websocket upgrade. It gets an EngineRequest with the headers, query and address, and returns true or false. maxSessions is the most open sessions:

lib/config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  options: ServerOptions(
    allowRequest: (EngineRequest req) => req.query['key'] == 'secret',
    maxSessions: 10000,
  ),
);

When allowRequest gives false or throws, the client gets 403. At the limit, a new handshake gets 503, and open sessions keep working. The count is per isolate, so with 4 isolates the app allows 4 times maxSessions.

Warning

Without maxSessions, every GET request makes a session that lives about 45 seconds. Set it in production.

docs.title: Many isolates
docs.text:
Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server. With many isolates, the provider uses the IsolateAdapter. It sends each broadcast, socketsJoin, fetchSockets, serverSideEmit and broadcast ack to the other isolates of the process:

Adapter Reaches InMemoryAdapter (one isolate) the clients of this isolate IsolateAdapter (many isolates, the default) the clients of every isolate of this process RedisAdapter the clients of every isolate of every server

Clients must connect with websocket only. Long-polling sends many requests that can reach different isolates. It works only with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.

Add each namespace in the config, so every isolate adds it. A namespace that only one isolate adds with io.of('/x') gets no answer from the others, so fetchSockets and serverSideEmitWithAck wait 5 seconds and throw.

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
With many server processes, or Dox next to Node.js servers, use the Redis adapter. A broadcast on one server then reaches the clients of all servers. Add the ioredis package:

dart pub add ioredis

Make the adapter in each isolate with a factory, because a Redis connection can not go to another isolate:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(),
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate.
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    // 127.0.0.1:6379. Or Redis(RedisOptions(host: ..., port: ...))
    Redis redis = Redis();
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

The subscriber needs its own connection, because a connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.

The adapter uses the format of @socket.io/redis-adapter, so Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox. If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set format: RedisFormat.json. Long-polling with this adapter also needs sticky sessions.

docs.title: Acting on all servers
docs.text:
With the Redis adapter, these methods work on the sockets of all servers:

// sockets of every server. Sockets of this server are `Socket`s.
List<RemoteSocket> sockets = await io.to('room1').fetchSockets();
for (RemoteSocket socket in sockets) {
  socket.emit('hello', socket.data['name']);
}

await io.to('room1').socketsJoin('room2');
await io.to('room2').socketsLeave('room1');
await io.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

A RemoteSocket also has join, leave and disconnect. fetchSockets throws a TimeoutException when a server does not answer in requestsTimeout (5 seconds by default).

To get one ack from each client on all servers, set a timeout:

List<Object?> answers = await io
    .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))
    .emitWithAck('ping', 'are you there?');

docs.title: Events between servers
docs.text:
serverSideEmit sends an event to the other servers, like "reload the config". Clients do not get it:

// on every server
io.onServerSideEmit('reload-config', (ServerSideEvent event) {
  reloadConfig(event.data);
  event.ack('done'); // only when the sender waits for an answer
});

// on one server
await io.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

To wait for one answer from each other server, use serverSideEmitWithAck. When a server does not answer in time, it throws an AckTimeoutException, and its responses holds the answers that came back:

List<Object?> answers =
    await io.serverSideEmitWithAck('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

docs.title: Emit from other programs
docs.text:
An emitter sends an event with no Socket.IO server, for example from a queue worker or a cron job. It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients:

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.emit('news', <String, dynamic>{'title': 'hello'});
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3');
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();
  await emitter.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

  await redis.disconnect();
}

The emitter does not wait for an answer. Its key must be the same as the adapter key. Both default to socket.io.

The emitters of other languages use the same format. For example, Node.js with @socket.io/redis-emitter:

import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');

docs.title: Broadcasting
docs.text: To send events to public, private and presence channels, see Broadcasting.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_socketio also runs with no Dox app:

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.register(ChatNamespace());
  await io.listen(3001);
}
  • io.listen(port) starts a native server on its own port. Run it in its own small program, like bin/socket.dart, behind the same proxy as the HTTP server.
  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a server you already have: a NativeHttpServer or a dart:io one.
  • In your own server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • io.on('connection', (Socket socket) {...}) handles the default namespace / with no class. io.sockets is that namespace.
  • io.use(SocketAuth(findUser).handle) logs users in on the default namespace.
  • await io.close() disconnects everyone and stops the server.

To use the Redis adapter, give it to the server:

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Broadcasting: send server events to channels.
  • Authentication: log users in.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
dox_validation checks input and gives you typed Dart objects.

It has two parts. A DTO is a class with @Dto() and rule annotations, and a generator writes its checks. Use it for almost all input, see DTOs. A fluent schema like v.object(...) is for input whose shape you know only at runtime. Both give all errors at once, and both give a JSON Schema for OpenAPI.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
dox_core exports dox_validation, so you install nothing. Import package:dox_core/dox_core.dart.

  1. Make a DTO with dox make:dto CreateUser. It writes lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart.
  2. Run the generator: dox build_runner:build.

  3. Give the list of DTOs to the app:

    lib/config/app.dart
    import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart
);

Then ask for the DTO in a controller. Dox checks the body before the method runs, and bad input gets 422 with the errors:

lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked and typed
    return <String, dynamic>{'name': body.name};
  }
}

The full guide is Validation, and every rule is in the rules reference. This page is about the package.

docs.title: Defining a DTO
docs.text:
Give each field its rules as annotations:

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

The generator writes a DtoSchema<CreateUser> named $CreateUserDto, with the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema. The schema line lets you use it as CreateUser.schema. The generator also writes lib/generated/dtos.g.dart, with the list dtos of every DTO in lib/.

docs.title: Validating a map
docs.text: A DtoSchema is also a normal Schema. You can use it inside v.object(...) and v.list(...), and with OpenAPI.

docs.title: Validating and throwing
docs.text:
validateMap runs all checks and gives the object. Bad input throws a ValidationException with the errors:

CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(input);

In a controller, this answers 422. dox_core has its own ValidationException and does not export the one of dox_validation.

docs.title: Validating without throwing
docs.text:
safeValidateMap gives a ParseResult, and never throws for bad input:

ParseResult<CreateUser> result =
    await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}

A ParseResult has:

  • success: true when there are no errors.
  • value: the result, or null when success is false.
  • errors: the first message for each field, like {'user.email': '...'}.
  • fieldErrors: all messages for each field.
  • issues: the full list of ValidationIssue objects, with code and path.

Both methods take these options:

  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string, so text is converted to the field type.
  • params are the path params, for @Unique(ignoreParam: ...).
  • messages and locale change the error text for this call. See Messages.

parse, safeParse, parseAsync and safeParseAsync also work on a DtoSchema. parse throws a StateError when the DTO has async rules.

docs.title: Building an object with no checks
docs.text:
fromMap builds the object with no checks. It reads the keys, converts JSON types and fills in defaults. Use it only for data you trust, because a wrong type throws a TypeError:

CreateUser user = CreateUser.schema.fromMap(trustedData);

docs.title: Turning an object back into a map
docs.text:
toMap gives the object as a map with the input keys. A DateTime becomes an ISO 8601 string, and an enum becomes its name:

Map<String, dynamic> data = CreateUser.schema.toMap(user);

docs.title: Getting the JSON Schema
docs.text:
toJsonSchema gives the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the DTO:

CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

For a CreateUser with age and role fields, you get:

{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description. @Describe('...') also sets it, and wins over the comment. A nested DTO goes in $defs with a $ref, and @Dto(strict: true) adds "additionalProperties": false.

docs.title: Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)
docs.text:
When you know the fields only at runtime, use a fluent schema. The output is a map, not a class:

final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

parse gives the data, and throws a ValidationException for bad input. safeParse gives a ParseResult:

Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);

In a controller, use req.validateSchema:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);

Fluent schemas do not use the DTO defaults:

  • A key is required, unless you add optional().
  • An empty string is a value, not "missing".
  • Text is not converted to numbers or booleans, unless you use v.coerce.

docs.title: Available schemas
docs.text:
Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ulid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, json, digits, digitsBetween, dateFormat, hexColor, password, exists, unique, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, between, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf, gtField, gteField, ltField, lteField, exists, unique v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has maxSize, minSize, mimes, mimeTypes, dimensions, image and extensions

gtField, gteField, ltField and lteField fail when the other key is missing.

docs.title: Optional and nullable values
docs.text:
Every schema has these methods:

  • optional(): the key can be missing. Null is still an error.
  • nullable(): the value can be null, but the key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing.
v.string().optional();
v.int().defaultTo(0);

Every schema also has transform, refine, superRefine, use(rule), same(other), different(other), confirmed(), accepted(), declined(), and describe(text) and example(x) for the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Converting text
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are always text. v.coerce turns the text into the type first:

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checking across fields
docs.text:
For a rule on two fields, use refine on the object. path sets the field that gets the error:

final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: More rules
docs.text:
Fluent schemas have the same rules as the DTO annotations, with the same codes and messages:

final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  // needs password_confirmation with the same value
  'password': v.string()
      .password(min: 8, mixedCase: true, numbers: true)
      .confirmed(),
  'email': v.string().email().unique('users', column: 'email'),
  'team_id': v.int().exists('teams'),
  'type': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['person', 'company']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredIf('type', 'company'),
  'phone': v.string().digitsBetween(8, 12).optional(),
  'country_code': v.string().optional().requiredWith(<String>['phone']),
  'birthday': v.string().dateFormat('Y-m-d').optional(),
  'settings': v.string().json().optional(),
  'age': v.int().between(18, 120).optional(),
});

Map<String, dynamic> data = await signUp.parseAsync(input);

There are more presence and compare rules:

final ObjectSchema order = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'email': v.string().optional().requiredWithout(<String>['phone']),
  'phone': v.string().optional(),
  'fax': v.string().optional()
      .requiredWithoutAll(<String>['email', 'phone']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredUnless('type', 'person'),
  'nick': v.string().optional().filled(),
  'note': v.string().optional().present().nullable(),
  'coupon': v.string().optional().prohibitedIf('type', 'guest'),
  'debug': v.any().optional().prohibited(),
  'terms': v.coerce.bool().accepted(),
  'new_password': v.string().different('old_password'),
  'id': v.string().ulid(),
  'min_price': v.int(),
  'max_price': v.int().gtField('min_price'),
});

Each rule is in the rules reference. Keep these points in mind:

  • The required..., prohibited..., filled and present rules come after optional() (or nullish()).
  • exists and unique ask the database, so they are async. Use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync().
  • exists(table, column: 'id'): the column default is id. Use v.int().exists('teams') for a number id, so text like abc fails before a query.
  • unique(table, column: 'email', ignore: id): column is required. ignore skips the row with this id, for updates.
  • A table or column name can have letters, digits, _ and $, with . between parts. Other names throw an ArgumentError.
  • The database decides if two values match. On MySQL, TAKEN@dox.dev is taken when taken@dox.dev is there.
  • accepted() on v.bool() takes only true. For form words like yes and on, use v.coerce.bool().accepted().

docs.title: Stop at the first error
docs.text:
A fluent schema gives one error for each failed rule of a value. Add .bail() to get only the first error. A DTO always does this:

v.string().min(8).email().bail().safeParse('ab');
// one error: min_length. Without bail(): min_length and email.

Put .bail() before .optional(), .nullable() or .transform(), because rules after them belong to the wrapper. Async rules after a failed rule do not run.

docs.title: Skip a field
docs.text:
excludeIf(other, value) and excludeUnless(other, value) skip a field of v.object(). When they match, the field is not checked and its key is not in the output:

final ObjectSchema account = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'vat_number': v.string().min(5).excludeIf('type', 'person'),
  'company': v.string().excludeUnless('type', 'company'),
});

account.parse(<String, dynamic>{'type': 'person', 'vat_number': 'x'});
// {type: person}

other must be a key of the same object. A skipped field never gets its default. When other is missing, excludeIf does not skip, and excludeUnless skips.

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text:
For a check that needs the database, use refineAsync, or superRefineAsync in place of superRefine. Then call parseAsync() or safeParseAsync(), because parse() throws a StateError:

v.string().refineAsync(isFreeName, message: 'The name is taken');

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
A Rule<T> class works as an annotation on a DTO, and with use() in a fluent schema:

v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());

See Custom rules to write one.

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.text:
Every schema and every DtoSchema implements the Standard Schema interface. Code that only validates can take any StandardSchema and call validate:

StandardResult<Object?> result = await schema.validate(input);

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. A message can use placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

To change messages for the whole app, set MessageResolver.global. In a Dox app, use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...):

MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

To add messages to a resolver later, use setMessages:
