MessageResolver.global.setMessages(<String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
});

To change messages for one call, give messages. It replaces the global resolver for that call, and falls back to the built-in text:

createUser.safeParse(input,
    messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
      'email.required': 'We need your email',
    }));

To show a name for {field} in place of the key, give attributes, or call setAttributes:

MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(
  attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
);
// The first name is required

A DTO can give its own names with @Dto(attributes:). For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve(). See Messages.

docs.title: Opt-in flags
docs.text:
ValidationFlags turns on behavior that is off by default. Set it in Validator.flags:

// turn on one flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(unicodeAlpha: true);

// turn on every flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();

Each isolate has its own Validator.flags. In a Dox app, set it in the setup() of a provider, which runs in every isolate:

class ValidationProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
  }
}
Flag What it does when on emptyStringsToNull Fluent schemas change each empty string to null before the check, also in nested maps and lists. For a DTO, use @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true). unicodeAlpha alpha, alphaNumeric and alphaDash accept Unicode letters, like José. shortInMessage The default in message is The selected {field} is invalid, with no list of allowed values. dtoAllErrors A DTO runs the rules of every field with the right type, also when another field is missing or wrong. dtoRejectEmptyList A required List field of a DTO fails required on []. dtoMaybeRejectsEmpty A Maybe<T> field of a DTO fails required when the key has an empty value, like "". laravelMessageKeys A custom message key can also use the short rule name, like name.min for the min_length error. See the list of names.

After you turn on a dto... flag, run dart run build_runner build one time.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_validation works in any Dart program. Add the package, and the builder for DTOs:

dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

Run the DTO generator with dart run build_runner build.

docs.title: Database rules
docs.text:
exists and unique ask a PresenceVerifier. In a Dox app, dox_orm sets one when the database starts. @Unique and @Exists for DTOs are in dox_orm.

With another database layer, write your own. Each isolate has its own value, so set it in code that runs in every isolate:

class MyVerifier extends PresenceVerifier {
  @override
  Future<Set<String>> found(
    String table,
    String column,
    List<Object?> values, {
    String? exceptColumn,
    Object? exceptValue,
    String? connection,
  }) async {
    // Return the values that are in the column, as text.
    // Bind the values as query parameters, never put them into the SQL.
    return <String>{};
  }
}

class VerifierProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    PresenceVerifier.instance = MyVerifier();
  }
}

docs.text:

docs.title: App config
docs.text:
This page lists every field of AppConfig, with its type, its default and what it does.

You give AppConfig to Dox().initialize() in lib/config/app.dart. Each field has a default except appKey. See the full example.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning appKey String required Encrypts cookies and signs local storage URLs. It must be exactly 32 characters. Make one with dox key:generate. In production a bad key stops the app at start, see APP_ENV. previousKeys List<String> [] Old app keys. Dox can still read data that was encrypted with them. New data uses appKey only. See Rotating the key. serverPort int 3000 The port to listen on. When the env has no APP_PORT but has PORT, Dox uses PORT (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). host String? null: APP_HOST, else all interfaces The network interface to listen on, like 127.0.0.1. null reads APP_HOST. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces (::). totalIsolate int? the CPUs the container allows How many isolates serve HTTP, all on the same port. The default is the number of CPUs this process can use, with the container cpuset and CPU quota. A quota rounds up (1.5 CPUs gives 2 isolates). Windows always uses one. computeWorkers int AppConfig.defaultComputeWorkers (4) How many worker isolates run Dox().compute, Hash.makeAsync and Hash.verifyAsync, in one pool for the process. It must be 1 or more. See Heavy CPU work. compress bool false gzip the responses, but not streamed responses. It costs CPU on each response, so let a proxy do it if you have one. maxBodySize int 10 * 1024 * 1024 (10 MB) Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets 413. maxMultipartSize int 100 * 1024 * 1024 (100 MB) Biggest multipart/form-data body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets 413. bodyTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 120) A client that sends no body bytes for this long gets 408. A slow but steady upload is fine. idleTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 30) A keep-alive connection with no new request for this long is closed. Behind a load balancer, set it longer than the balancer's idle timeout. See Behind a load balancer. maxConnections int? null (no limit) The most connections one isolate holds open at once (1 or more). When it is full, new clients wait in the OS queue. The app holds up to maxConnections * totalIsolate, so keep that below ulimit -n. http2 bool false The same port also speaks HTTP/2 over plain TCP (h2c). HTTP/1.1 keeps working. See HTTP/2. maxConcurrentStreams int 250 The most open requests one HTTP/2 connection can have (1 or more). Used only when http2 is true. shutdownTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 8) On SIGTERM or SIGINT, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See Graceful shutdown. trustedProxies List<String> [] IPs or CIDR ranges of your reverse proxies. Dox reads X-Forwarded-For (for req.ip()) and X-Forwarded-Proto (for req.scheme()) only from these. ['*'] trusts any direct client, but only the last hop. Use it only when the app port is not open to the outside. isDevelopment bool (getter) True when APP_ENV is development. It reads the env at each call, so it works before the server starts. Use it in config, like a database debug flag.

docs.title: Routing and request handling
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning container void Function(IocContainer)? null Pass registerContainer from lib/generated/container.g.dart. It fills the container, and also gives the routers, providers and model binders. See Dependency injection. routers List<Router> [] Routers to register first, in this order. Every other Router class comes from container. globalMiddleware List<dynamic> [] Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an IDoxMiddleware. dtos List<DtoSchema<Object>> [] Pass dtos from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart. Dox finds the DTOs of controllers and req.validate<T>() in it. validationMessages MessageResolver? null (English messages) Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. responseHandler ResponseHandlerInterface? null A class with DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res). It sees every response before it is sent. exceptionHandler ExceptionHandler ExceptionHandler() Reports every unhandled error and turns it into a response. The default logs the error and the stack. See Error handling. htmlErrors bool false Sends an HTML error page to a request that does not want JSON. In development or local the page also shows the error and the stack. JSON clients do not change. See An HTML error page. errorPage String Function(int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug) defaultErrorPage Makes the HTML of the page. debug is true in development or local. Escape every value you put in the page. Used only with htmlErrors. providers List<DoxProvider> [] Providers to run first, in this order. Every other DoxProvider class comes from container. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. webSocketAllowedOrigins List<String>? null (no check) Checks the Origin of each Route.websocket route. Only the same host and the listed sites, like https://app.example.com, can open a socket. Others get 403. [] means the same host only. With null, any website can open a socket with the cookies of the user. The allowedOrigins of a route wins.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning cors CORSConfig CORSConfig() CORS headers. See CORSConfig. logger LoggerConfig LoggerConfig() The Logger output. See LoggerConfig. cache CacheConfig file store in storage/cache, plus a memory store Cache stores for Cache(). See CacheConfig. session SessionConfig cookie driver, cookie dox_session, 2 hours Settings for SessionMiddleware. See Session. openApi OpenApiConfig OpenApiConfig() /docs, /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. See OpenApiConfig. strict StrictConfig StrictConfig() (off) Warnings for code that blocks the server, for development. enabled turns it on. blockLimit is how long code can block an isolate before a warning, StrictConfig.defaultBlockLimit (50 ms) by default. See Let Dox warn you. flags CoreFlags CoreFlags() (all off) Opt-in core behaviors. See Core flags.

docs.title: Core flags
docs.text:
CoreFlags turns on extra behaviors. Each flag is off by default:

AppConfig(
  appKey: env.appKey,
  flags: const CoreFlags(onlyPresent: true, cookieDefaults: true),
);

CoreFlags.all() turns on every flag:

AppConfig(appKey: env.appKey, flags: const CoreFlags.all());
Flag When it is on laravelErrors A 422 body is {"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}, with all messages of each field. The OpenAPI docs use this shape too. Off: {"field": "first message"}. onlyPresent req.only([...]) leaves out keys that are not in the input. So model.update(req.only([...])) does not write null for a field the client did not send. Off: a missing key is in the map with null. cookieDefaults A DoxCookie with no path gets Path=/, and one with no sameSite gets SameSite=Lax. A value you set wins. Off: no Path and no SameSite. hasKeyOnly req.has('x') is true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null), like req.exists('x'). Dot keys work. Off: '' and null give false. htmlStrings A string from a controller is sent as text/html. A content type you set wins. Escape user input in the string. Off: text/plain. replaceHeaders res.header(k, v) replaces a value that a middleware set before. Vary and Set-Cookie still get one more value. Off: it adds a second value. Pass replace: to pick for one call. decryptServerError A DecryptException gives a 500 server_error, and the ExceptionHandler reports it. Off: 400 decrypt_failed, not reported. envExpand .env values can use ${OTHER}, and a "..." value reads \n, \t, \", \\ and \$. Also set Env.flags = flags; at the top of main() in bin/server.dart and in your tests, because .env is read before AppConfig exists. See Use one value in another. Off: values are read as written. rateLimitIpv6Prefix The default key of RateLimit counts an IPv6 client by its /64 prefix. One home or server gets a whole /64, so with one count per address a client gets a new count with each new address. Clients in one /64 share a count. A key you give is used as it is. Off: each full ip has its own count. See Rate limiting. cacheCopies Cache().store('x'), .tag() and .tags() give a new Cache, and the first one does not change. Off: they change the same object and give it back.

The cache has its own flag class, CacheFlags, in CacheConfig.

docs.title: CORSConfig
docs.text:
A value can be a string ('*' or a comma list) or a list of strings. A null value sends no header, so set at least origin.

Field Type Default Header enabled bool true Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own cors setting. origin dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Origin. One origin, '*', or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. methods dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Methods headers dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Headers exposeHeaders dynamic null Access-Control-Expose-Headers credentials bool? null Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. Browsers refuse it with origin '*', so list your sites in origin. maxAge num? null Access-Control-Max-Age in seconds

docs.title: LoggerConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning name String '' Written as logger.name in each JSON log line. Left out when empty. enabled bool false Turn the Logger on. When it is off, LogMiddleware logs nothing too. prettyPrint bool false true prints colored text. Each line starts with a tag that says where it comes from, like [request], [server] or [app]. false prints one JSON object per line, for log services. The tag is then in the source field, unless your data already has a source key. level String 'info' The lowest level to print: debug, info, warn or error. success counts as info, and danger as error.

Your own lines get the tag [app]. To use another tag, give it as the third argument of log, info, warn, success or danger:

Logger.info('invoice sent', null, 'billing');

In JSON mode the tag is the source field. Plain warnings on stderr use the same tags.

docs.title: CacheConfig
StorageConfig
docs.text:
StorageProvider of the dox_storage package takes it. See File storage.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultDisk String 'local' The disk Storage() uses when no disk is named. disks Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> {'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}} Disk name to options. Each disk needs a driver option.

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required local, s3 or memory local root String storage Folder of the files. local url String none Base of the public URLs, like http://localhost:3000/files. local app_key String AppConfig.appKey Key that signs the URLs. local visibility String public public or private. local atomic_writes bool false Write to a temp file, then rename it. local permissions bool or Map off Visibility is the file mode. See File storage. s3 bucket String required Bucket name. s3 region String us-east-1 Region. s3 key String required Access key id. s3 secret String required Secret access key. s3 token String none Session token. s3 endpoint String none Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). s3 path_style bool false Use path style URLs. s3 url String none Base of the public URLs. s3 visibility String private public or private. s3 acl bool true The service supports ACLs. s3 batch_delete bool true The service supports batch delete.

docs.title: OpenApiConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool? null Serve the docs routes. null means on only in development or local. info Info Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0') Title and version of the API. servers List<Server> [] Base URLs of the API. securitySchemes Map<String, SecurityScheme> {} Ways to log in, like {'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}. securityByMiddleware Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>> {} Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. It wins over @Security on the class. A middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth when it has no @Security and no entry here. registry OpenApiRegistry OpenApiRegistry() (empty) What dox_builder found in the code. Pass openApiRegistry from lib/generated/openapi.g.dart. ui DocsUi DocsUi.scalar scalar or swagger. scalar ScalarOptions ScalarOptions() Options of the Scalar page. See below. pageTitle String? null (uses info.title) Title of the /docs page. include List<String> [] (all routes) Only routes with these paths are in the docs, like ['/api/*']. A * at the end matches the rest of the path. exclude List<String> [] Routes with these paths are left out. Checked after include.

ScalarOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning theme ScalarTheme ScalarTheme.default_ One of default_, alternate, moon, purple, solarized, bluePlanet, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, elysiajs, fastify, mars, laserwave, none. darkMode bool false Start in dark mode. showDownloadButton bool true Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. proxyUrl String? null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy.

docs.title: SocketIoConfig
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider of the dox_socketio package takes it. See Socket.IO.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool true Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at /socket.io/. options ServerOptions ServerOptions() Engine options. See below. namespaces List<NamespaceHandler> [] Namespaces to register, like ChatNamespace(). adapter SocketAdapterFactory? null (in memory with one isolate, IsolateAdapter with many) Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many servers.

ServerOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning path String /socket.io/ URL path. Must end with /. pingInterval Duration 25 s Time between two server pings. pingTimeout Duration 20 s Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. upgradeTimeout Duration 10 s Time a websocket upgrade may take. connectTimeout Duration 45 s Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. maxHttpBufferSize int 1000000 Biggest message in bytes a client may send. maxAttachments int 10 Most binary attachments in one packet. A packet with more closes that client. transports List<String> ['polling', 'websocket'] Allowed transports. allowUpgrades bool true Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. cors CorsOptions? null (no CORS headers) CORS for the long-polling requests.

CorsOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning origins List<String> ['*'] Allowed origins. credentials bool false Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. methods List<String> ['GET', 'POST'] Allowed methods for preflight. allowedHeaders List<String>? null (the requested headers) Allowed request headers. maxAge Duration? null How long a browser may cache the preflight answer.

docs.title: DatabaseConfig
docs.text:
The database is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig) in its setup().

Field Type Default Meaning connection String required Name of the connection to use. connections Map<String, ConnectionConfig> required Connection name to config.

ConnectionConfig:

Field Type Default Meaning driver Driver required Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql (also MariaDB) or Driver.sqlite. host String 'localhost' Database host. Not used by sqlite. port int 0 Database port. Not used by sqlite. user String '' Database user. Not used by sqlite. password String '' Database password. Not used by sqlite. database String required Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or :memory:. useSSL bool false Use TLS. Postgres: mode require (no certificate check), set extra['sslMode'] to change it. MySQL: the certificate is checked. debug bool required Print every query with printer. printer QueryPrinter? null ConsoleQueryPrinter(), PrettyQueryPrinter(), FileQueryPrinter(file: File('queries.log')) or your own. With buffered: true, call await printer.flush() before exit(), or the last lines are lost. logRedact List<String> [] Names of values to hide in the query log. A value shows as *** when its key ends with one of these names. ['password', 'token'] hides password, users.password and remember_token. Only the log changes. slowQueryMs int? null Log each query that takes longer than this many milliseconds. 0 logs every query. null turns it off. It works with debug off. read List<Map<String, dynamic>>? null Read replica hosts. Each map can change host, port, user, password, database and extra. See Read replicas. write Map<String, dynamic>? null Settings of the write host, in the same form as one read map. Only used with read. sticky bool false With read: after a write, the reads of the same request go to the write host. extra Map<String, dynamic> {} Driver options. See below. driverFactory DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)? null Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting.

Keys of extra:

Driver Key Type Default Meaning postgres, mysql maxConnectionCount int 10 Most open connections, for the whole process. postgres, mysql threads int 1 Rust threads of the native driver. Only the first pool sets it. postgres, mysql requestTimeout Duration 300 s The longest wait for one request (a free connection, the connect and the query). Over it, the request fails. postgres, mysql maxConnectionAge Duration none on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a connection older than this, once it has no query. postgres, mysql idleTimeout Duration no limit on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a free connection that is not used for this long. mysql serverKill bool true Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with KILL. Set false behind a proxy like ProxySQL. mysql, sqlite preparedStatementCacheSize int 100 Prepared statements kept per connection. postgres sslMode String require with useSSL, else disable TLS mode: disable, prefer, require or verify-full. postgres sslRootCert String none Path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for verify-full. sslrootcert in DATABASE_URL. postgres sslWarning bool true false hides the warning Dox prints when TLS mode is require. sslWarning=false in DATABASE_URL works too. postgres timeZone String UTC Session time zone. postgres applicationName String none Name of the app in pg_stat_activity. mysql verifyCertificate bool true false skips the TLS certificate check. Only for a self-signed certificate in development. sqlite busyTimeout int 5000 PRAGMA busy_timeout in milliseconds. sqlite background bool false true runs the queries in a helper isolate, so a slow query does not block the request isolate. ?background=true in DATABASE_URL works too. See SQLite.

A time key takes a Duration, or a number of seconds. See Pool settings.

docs.title: AuthConfig
docs.text:
Auth is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...)) in its setup().

Class Field Type Default Meaning AuthConfig defaultGuard String required The guard Auth() uses when no guard is named. AuthConfig guards Map<String, AuthGuard> {} Guard name to guard. AuthGuard driver AuthDriver required How a token is made and checked, like JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...)). AuthGuard provider AuthProvider required Where users come from. AuthProvider model dynamic Function() required Makes the user model, like () => User(). AuthProvider identifierFields List<String> ['email'] Columns attempt() matches the login with. AuthProvider passwordField String 'password' Column with the bcrypt hash.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
These are the config files of a new project. They read their values from env, the typed env class in lib/config/env.dart (see Env reference).

lib/config/app.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Changing the key makes old cookies and encrypted data unreadable.
  appKey: env.appKey,
  serverPort: env.appPort,
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate,
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  container: registerContainer,

  /// Only in development. Warns when a handler blocks the isolate.
  strict: StrictConfig(enabled: env.appEnv == 'development'),
  cache: cache,
  cors: cors,
  logger: logger,
);
lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
lib/config/logger.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  /// colored text is slow. JSON lines in production.
  // Env.appEnv, not appConfig.isDevelopment: appConfig is built from
  // this logger, so reading appConfig here would loop.
  prettyPrint: Env.appEnv == 'development',
);
lib/config/database.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
bool _debug = appConfig.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,

  /// Only in development. Warns about N+1 relation loads and big results.
  strict: OrmStrict(enabled: appConfig.isDevelopment),
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// One pool for all isolates.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: false,
  // a list: Dox sends back the request origin only when it is in the list
  origin: <String>['http://localhost:3000'],
  methods: <String>['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>[
    'accept',
    'authorization',
    'content-type',
    'x-csrf-token',
    'x-xsrf-token',
    'x-requested-with',
  ],
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 90,
);

Do not use origin: '*' with credentials: true, because the browser refuses that pair.

lib/providers/orm_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Dox finds it by itself and runs it in every isolate.
/// No database? Delete this file.
class ORMProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}

A new project also has lib/config/storage.dart, queue.dart and schedule.dart, with a provider for each in lib/providers/. See File storage, Queue and Scheduler.

A new project has no openapi.dart, socketio.dart or auth provider. See OpenAPI, Socket.IO and Authentication.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Environment variables: the env keys that fill the config.
  • Dependency injection: the container, routers and providers.
  • Deployment: the server settings in production.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: What changed in dox_core, newest first. Each version lists the changes you may notice in your app. The full list, with every detail, is in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Dox().compute(task) runs heavy CPU work (a PDF, an image, a big JSON file) on a worker isolate. The server keeps answering other requests in the meantime. AppConfig.computeWorkers sets the number of workers (default 4).
  • Strict mode for development: AppConfig(strict: StrictConfig(enabled: true)). It warns when a route blocks the isolate too long, or when Hash.make runs in the web server. Off by default.
  • Log lines have a tag that says where they come from: [request], [server], [error] or [app]. Pass your own tag as the third argument: Logger.info('done', null, 'billing').
  • CoreFlags.rateLimitIpv6Prefix counts an IPv6 client by its /64 prefix. Off by default.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Hash.makeAsync and Hash.verifyAsync use the Dox().compute workers. Before, each call started a new isolate.
  • The stderr warnings use the same tags. dox: warning: and [dox] are now [server] or [request].

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Sessions with the cache driver on a memory store were kept per isolate, so users were logged out at random. They are now shared by all isolates.
  • A slow handler could lose its upload temp file when the client left early.
  • An error after a stream started (like server-sent events) wrote Internal Server Error into the stream. Now the stream just ends.
  • A cut multipart upload kept the request open for ever. Now it gets 400.
  • AfterResponse work could start before the handler ended, or never run after a sync throw.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: • The RateLimit counter without Redis now keeps at most 100,000 clients, so many fake IPs can not fill the memory.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • Faster and lighter requests: lazy request body, lazy cookie session, fewer header reads, a smaller JSON buffer, faster route matching and RateLimit on Redis in one round trip.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• AppConfig.isDevelopment is true when APP_ENV is development.
  • Env.appEnv gives APP_ENV in lower case.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Env.get as the first env read of the app did not see .env. Now every env read loads .env first.
  • In .env, KEY=#value was read as empty. Now it keeps #value.
  • A value with only spaces now gives the default.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• An env error no longer prints the bad value, because it may be a secret.
  • The APP_KEY check refuses more public sample keys. If your key is one of them, run dox key:generate.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• The JSON lines of Logger and LogMiddleware use standard log field names (Datadog). level is now status. LogMiddleware also renames source_ip to network.client.ip and request_id to http.request_id.
  • Command, MigrationFile and DoxProvider moved to dox_annotation. dox_core still exports them. Upgrade dox_builder together with dox_core.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• CoreFlags: opt-in behaviors, all off by default. Pass them as AppConfig(flags: ...). CoreFlags.all() turns on every flag. See App config.
  • CoreFlags.envExpand lets .env values use ${OTHER}. export KEY=value lines now work too.
  • RateLimit(sliding: true) uses a sliding window.
  • AppConfig(htmlErrors: true) sends an HTML error page to browsers. Errors stay JSON by default.
  • Providers get a boot() step that runs after every setup().
  • Dox().addGlobalMiddleware() lets a provider add global middleware.
  • Dox().isWebServer is true only in the web server process.
  • Dox().loadRoutes() gives the app routes without a server. dox route:list uses it.
  • Route.resource(..., parameter: 'photo') names the item param.
  • route() and Route.url() take absolute: true, and put unknown params in the query string.
  • A cache store with 'encrypt': true encrypts its values with APP_KEY.
  • ServerTiming middleware adds a Server-Timing header.
  • AfterResponse.run(work) runs work after the response is sent.
  • session.regenerate(keepToken: true) keeps the CSRF token.
  • dox_core exports the JSON helper.
  • An AI agent skill (dox-core-guide). Install it with dart run skills@ get.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Logger writes lines in batches, not one print() per line. Warnings and errors are written at once.
  • LogMiddleware writes through Logger and follows LoggerConfig.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Route.group and the other route scopes now restore their state when the callback throws.
  • Dox().stop() could keep the process alive.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• IsolateBus sends a message to all isolates of the app, with no Redis.
  • Dox().isolateCount gives the number of running isolates.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Uses dox_validation 3.1.2, so @Describe('...') works on DTO fields.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Hash.sha256(value), to store API keys and tokens as a hash. Not for passwords.
  • ValidationException.issues keeps every issue, so you can build your own 422 body.
  • Cache().flexible takes a null stale.
  • RequestBody and BodyKind are exported, to tell invalid JSON from no body.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• Without Redis, RateLimit counts are shared by all isolates. Before, the real limit was max times the number of isolates. Raise max if you relied on that.
  • When two Route.mount prefixes match, the longest one wins. Before, the first one won.
  • Removed the unused middlewareAndControllerHandler and getDoxRequest helpers.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Routes: Route.match, Route.any, Route.redirect, Route.permanentRedirect, Route.fallback and .where(param, regex).
  • Route.staticFiles(prefix, folder) serves CSS, JS and images, with ETag, 304 and Range support.
  • MethodOverride middleware, so an HTML form can send PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
  • Request helpers: input with dot keys and a default, filled, exists, missing, except, boolean, integer, file, hasFile, bearerToken, path, fullUrl, pathIs and routeIs.
  • Crypt.encryptString and Crypt.decryptString, with the APP_KEY.
  • Hash.check, the same as Hash.verify.
  • Cache().many and Cache().putMany.
  • Route.mount(..., middleware: true) runs the global middleware before the raw handler.
  • SessionMiddleware().fromCookie(value) loads a session with no request, for a Socket.IO login.
  • package:dox_core/command.dart lets a package add its own dox commands.
  • AppConfig.idleTimeout and AppConfig.maxConnections.
  • Route.websocket(maxMessageSize:).
  • A warning in development when a middleware returns null.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• res.withHeaders dropped the headers set before it.
  • res.header added a second value instead of replacing one.
  • A mounted handler that threw left the client hanging.
  • Route.mount('/admin') also matched /administrator.
  • Static files added before startServer() worked only in one isolate.
  • Many smaller router, OpenAPI and session fixes.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• .where now checks a param again after % decoding. Before, %2F could slip ../ past it.
  • req.pathIs() now cleans the path like the router does, so /admin// can not skip a guard.
  • back() only follows a Referer of the same host. It was an open redirect.
  • WebSocket routes can check the Origin header: Route.websocket(allowedOrigins: [...]).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • A Redis cache store with no prefix uses <app name>_cache:. Your old cache keys are not found once after the update. Set 'prefix': 'dox_cache:' to keep them.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Middleware: RequestId, ETag, ValidateSignature and RequestTimeout.
  • Signed urls: Route.signedUrl(...).
  • IDoxTerminableMiddleware runs a step after the response is sent.
  • Cache() has flexible and touch.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• A path with routes, but not for the request method, gives 405 with an Allow header. Before, it gave 404.
  • abort(code, [message, headers]) for any status.
  • Bracket keys nest: tags[]=a&tags[]=b gives a list.
  • AppConfig(previousKeys: [...]) reads cookies made with an old APP_KEY, so a new key does not log users out.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Path params are now URL-decoded.
  • 5xx HTTP exceptions now reach ExceptionHandler.report.
  • req.method said GET for a HEAD request.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • Encrypted cookies and sessions are about 100 times faster (AES-GCM in Rust).
The first stable release.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
Code Does Route.get('/blogs', (C c) => c.index) controller C from the container. Also post, put, patch, delete, options Route.get('/blogs', listBlogs) a plain function Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema) body: is for the docs only. It checks nothing. Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show) path param. show(int id) Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list) optional param. list(int? page) Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page) rest of the path, with / Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me]) middleware first, controller last Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', handler) one handler for a list of methods Route.any('/webhook', handler) one handler for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE Route.redirect('/home', '/') / Route.permanentRedirect('/old', '/new') send a path to another URL. 302 by default, 301 for permanentRedirect. Route.get('/users/{id}', c.show).where('id', '[0-9]+') the route matches only when the param fits the regex Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) { ... }) answers a GET or HEAD request that matches no route and no static file. Use it for a 404 page or an SPA. globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()] lets an HTML form reach PUT, PATCH and DELETE routes Route.group('/blogs', () { ... }) prefix. Dox adds the / between parts. Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... }) middleware for a group Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... }) match by Host Route.resource('blogs', BlogController) index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy Route.health('/health') 200 {"status": "ok"}, or 503 when a check fails. See Health check. Route.staticFiles('/', 'public') serve a folder (CSS, JS, images) when no route matches. maxAge: sets Cache-Control Storage.route('files') serve a storage disk. Only signed URLs work, unless signed: false (dox_storage) Route.enabledCors(() { ... }) / Route.disabledCors(...) CORS for some routes Route.websocket('echo', (WebSocket s, DoxRequest req) { ... }) a raw WebSocket. For rooms and acks, use Socket.IO.

Controller parameters, by type: DoxRequest, one @Dto class, a string, integer, double, num or bool for path params (by position), a @DoxModel (loaded by its key), an @Inject() class. Only positional parameters. In the examples, c.index is a method of a controller C from the container.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
    // Hash.equals: constant time, so the time does not leak the key
    String given = req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '';
    if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(given, apiKey)) {
      return response('no').statusCode(401); // stop here
    }
    return req; // go on
  }
}
Middleware Does const RequestId() X-Request-Id header, req.requestId const ETag() ETag header, 304 when If-None-Match matches RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30)) or Route.get(...).timeout(...) 503 when the route is too slow const ServerTiming() Server-Timing header; ServerTiming.add('db', d) adds a time. Development or trusted clients only const ValidateSignature() 403 unless the url is from Route.signedUrl(...) implements IDoxNextMiddleware await next() runs the rest, then you change the response implements IDoxTerminableMiddleware terminate(req, res) runs after the answer is sent

Middleware runs in this order: globalMiddleware, router middleware, group, route.

See Middleware and Signed URLs.

Returns the deleted rows as an int. await blog.increment('views') / decrement change a number in one query await Blog().forceCreate({...}) create with every key, ignore fillable await Model.unguarded(() async { ... }) turn off the fillable check inside the callback await blog.sync('tags', <int>[1, 2]) many to many: make the links exactly these ids await blog.attach('tags', 3) / await blog.detach('tags', 3) add / remove links await blog.forceDelete() / await blog.restore() real delete / undo soft delete Blog().withTrash() include soft deleted rows Blog().onlyTrashed() only soft deleted rows await blog.touch() set updated_at to now, touchQuietly() with no events blog.replicate() a new unsaved copy of the model Blog().preload('comments').get() load a relation, one query Blog().whereHas('comments').get() / whereDoesntHave / has('comments', '>=', 3) filter by a relation await blog.$getRelation('user') load a relation on one model blog.related<Comment>('comments')?.where(...).get() relation query blog.toJson() / blog.toMap() map, hidden left out of toJson() Blog().query() a new, empty query

class CreateBlogsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {

Access tokens (AccessTokenAuthDriver):

Auth auth = req.auth as Auth; // after AuthMiddleware()
User user = auth.user<User>()!;
AccessToken token = await auth.createAccessToken(user,
    abilities: <String>['posts:read']);
bool ok = auth.tokenCan('posts:read');
AccessToken next = await auth.rotateAccessToken(auth.currentAccessToken!,
    grace: const Duration(seconds: 10));
// replaces the whole list
await auth.setAccessTokenAbilities(auth.currentAccessToken!,
    <String>['posts:read']);
await auth.revokeToken(req); // logout

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('chat', onChat);
  }

  void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data);
    event.ack('ok');
  }
}

Log users in at connect time with SocketAuth(findUser).handle in middleware. The user is in socket.user.

Turn it on with a SocketIoProvider (extend it in lib/). With many isolates, clients must use transports: ['websocket']. Broadcasts reach every isolate without Redis, but many servers need the Redis adapter.

See Socket.IO.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
This page lists every dox command, with its options and the files it writes.

Run dox help to list the commands, and dox help <command> to see one. These rules apply to all commands:

  • A name becomes snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. So BlogPost and blog_post give the same result.
  • A make:* command never overwrites a file. If the file exists, it shows <name> already exists and stops.
  • Many make:* commands also have a create:* name, like create:model.
  • Packages and your app can add commands. See Package commands.

docs.title: dox create
docs.text:
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]

Makes a new project from the dox-sample repo.

Option Meaning --version <v> (or --v) A release tag of dox-sample to clone. The default is the newest release with the same major version as the CLI.

It clones the template into a new snake_case folder, puts your project name in the files, and makes a .env with a new random APP_KEY. It needs curl and git.

docs.title: dox add
docs.text:
dox add <package> [--dev] [options]

Adds a Dox package and runs its <package>:install command with your options, like dox add orm --driver=postgres. See Add a package.

docs.title: dox serve
docs.text:
dox serve [--no-reload] [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server

Starts the dev server with hot reload and build_runner watch. To change the port, set APP_PORT, like APP_PORT=9000 dox serve.

Option Meaning --no-reload Turn hot reload off. Every change restarts the server. --ignore-build-runner Do not start dart run build_runner watch. Changed Result A .dart file in lib/app/ (not .g.dart) Hot reload, in approximately 0.1 to 0.2 seconds. A static or global value keeps its old value until a restart. Routes, providers, config, lib/generated/, bin/, db/ or a generated .g.dart file The server restarts. A hot reload that fails, for example a compile error The server restarts.

The server shows a VM service link at start. Open it for DevTools, or attach VS Code with "Dart: Attach to Dart Process".

docs.title: dox build
docs.text:
dox build

Compiles the app to a native binary for production, in build/bundle. It runs build_runner, then dart build cli. Run the app with cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.

Path What build/bundle/bin/server the native binary, no Dart SDK needed build/bundle/bin/queue the queue worker, when bin/queue.dart exists build/bundle/bin/schedule the scheduler, when bin/schedule.dart exists build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, dox_http_native, ...) build/bundle/db/ your migrations and seeders. SQLite files are not copied. build/bundle/.env.example copy it to .env or set real env vars

Do not use dart compile exe, because it cannot build the native libraries.

docs.title: dox build_runner:build and dox build_runner:watch
docs.text:
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch

Run dart run build_runner build one time, or dart run build_runner watch. The build command shows a short output.

docs.title: dox key:generate
docs.text:
dox key:generate [--show] [--force]

Writes a random 32 character key to APP_KEY in the .env file. The file must exist.

Option Meaning --show Print a new key and write nothing. --force Do not ask in production.

A new key logs out all users. So when APP_ENV=production, the command asks first.

docs.title: dox env:generate
docs.text:
dox env:generate

Writes lib/config/env.dart, the typed env class, from .env.example. Run dart run build_runner build after it. The type of each getter comes from the example value:

Value in .env.example Getter a whole number, like 3000 int get x => 3000; true or false bool get x => true; empty String? get x; any other text String get x; (required)

A # comment line above a key becomes its doc comment.

docs.title: dox env:check
docs.text:
dox env:check [--expand]

Checks the real environment and .env with your AppEnv class. It shows The env is valid., or each missing or bad key and exits with code 1. It needs lib/config/env.dart and a name: in pubspec.yaml.

Option Meaning --expand Check with envExpand on. See Use one value in another.

docs.title: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate [dir]

Writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml into dir (default storage/openapi). It runs bin/openapi.dart. If that file is missing, the command shows the code for it. See OpenAPI.

docs.title: dox update
docs.text:
dox update

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version. It needs curl.

docs.title: dox version
docs.text:
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version

Prints the CLI version.

docs.title: dox help
docs.text:
dox help [command]
dox --help
dox -h

Without a command, it lists every command. With a command, it prints its usage, options and aliases.

docs.title: dox make:controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller <name> [-r|--resource] [--api] [--model=<model>]

Writes lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart. A Controller at the end of the name is removed.

Option Meaning -r or --resource A resource controller with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy. --api A resource controller without create and edit, the two form pages. Route.resource makes no route for them. --model=<model> or --model <model> A resource controller that uses the model. index returns all rows, and store creates a row from req.body. The other methods take the model as a parameter, so route model binding loads it.

--api and --model each make a resource controller, also with no -r. Run dart run build_runner build after it, to add the controller to the container.

docs.title: dox make:middleware
docs.text:
dox make:middleware <name>

Writes lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart: a class <Name>Middleware implements IDoxMiddleware with a handle method that returns the request. A Middleware at the end of the name is removed.

docs.title: dox make:dto
docs.text:
dox make:dto <name>

Writes lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart: a @Dto() class with one name field. A Dto at the end of the name is removed. Run dox build_runner:build after it. See DTOs.

docs.title: dox make:serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer <name>

Writes lib/app/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart: a class <Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>> that imports the model. A Serializer at the end of the name is removed.

docs.title: dox make:provider
docs.text:
dox make:provider <name>

Writes lib/providers/<name>_provider.dart: a class <Name>Provider extends DoxProvider with an empty setup() and an optional shutdown(). A Provider at the end of the name is removed. Run dox build_runner:build after it. See Providers.

docs.title: dox make:command
docs.text:
dox make:command <name>

Writes lib/app/commands/<name>_command.dart: a class <Name>Command extends Command. A Command at the end of the name is removed. The command name is app:<name>, with - for _: dox make:command send_report makes app:send-report.

It adds the class to lib/app/commands/commands.dart, and dox: commands: to pubspec.yaml. Then run dart pub get. If a file has a shape that it does not know, it changes nothing and shows what to add. See Package commands.

docs.title: dox make:mail
docs.text:
dox make:mail <name> [--no-view]
Form Writes plain lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart and the view resources/views/emails/<name>.dox.html --no-view lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart only, with a plain text body

The class is <Name>Mail extends Mailable, with the recipient Address in its constructor. A Mail at the end of the name is removed. It tells you when pubspec.yaml needs dox_mailer or dox_view. See Mail.

docs.title: dox make:view
docs.text:
dox make:view <name>

Writes resources/views/<name>.dox.html with a small sample. A / in the name makes a folder: Pages/About gives resources/views/pages/about.dox.html. See Views.

docs.title: dox make:test
docs.text:
dox make:test <name> [--unit]
Form Writes plain test/<name>_test.dart that starts the app with DoxTestClient and checks GET /ping. --unit test/<name>_test.dart with a plain package:test test.

A Test at the end of the name is removed. See Testing.

docs.title: dox make:model
docs.text:
dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
dox create:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]

Writes lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart, a @DoxModel class. The table name is the plural snake_case name, so BlogPost gives blog_posts.

Option Meaning -m or --migration Also make a create_<table>_table migration. -c or --controller Also make a plain controller, <name>.controller.dart. -r or --resource Also make a resource controller that uses the model. --api Also make a resource controller without create and edit, that uses the model. -f or --factory Also make a factory, db/factories/<name>.factory.dart. -s or --seed Also make a seeder, db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. -a or --all Also make the migration, the factory, the seeder and a resource controller.

You can join short options: -mcr is the same as -m -c -r. Each extra file is the same as the file from its own command:

Command Same file as dox make:model Post -m dox make:migration create_posts_table dox make:model Post -c dox make:controller Post dox make:model Post -r dox make:controller Post -r --model=Post dox make:model Post --api dox make:controller Post --api --model=Post dox make:model Post -f dox make:factory Post dox make:model Post -s dox make:seeder Post

If the model file exists, the command makes no file. If an extra file exists, only that file is skipped.

docs.title: dox make:migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
Option Meaning --sql Make a .sql file with -- up and -- down sections in place of a Dart class.

Writes db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart (or .sql). Migrations run in file name order. For a Dart migration, it also updates db/migration/migrations.dart, and makes bin/migrate.dart if it is missing. The code depends on the name:

Name up() down() create_<table>_table schema.create('<table>', ...) with id() and timestamps() schema.dropIfExists('<table>') <x>_to_<table>_table (also from, in, on) schema.table('<table>', ...) schema.table('<table>', ...) anything else a comment a comment

docs.title: dox route:list
docs.text:
dox route:list [--json]

Shows each route of the app: method, path, name, handler and middleware.

METHOD  PATH           NAME  HANDLER             MIDDLEWARE
GET     /api/ping            ApiController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /ping                WebController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /docs                serve
GET     /openapi.json        serve
GET     /openapi.yaml        serve

5 routes
Option Meaning --json Print the same data as one JSON list. 
dox route:list --json

[{"method":"GET","path":"/api/ping","name":null,"handler":"ApiController.pong","middleware":["LogMiddleware"]}]

Providers do not run, so a route that a provider adds, like the Socket.IO mount, is not in the list. A function with no name shows as Closure. A fallback route has the method FALLBACK, and a mount has the method MOUNT.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
These commands run bin/migrate.dart of your app, and make it if it is missing. The CLI runs .sql migrations itself. The database comes from DATABASE_URL, or from the DB_* keys. See Environment variables.

Command Aliases What it does dox migration:run dox migrate Run the migrations that did not run yet. dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] [--batch=<number>] [--force] dox migrate:rollback Undo the last batch, the last <count> migrations, or only batch <number>. Give --step or --batch, not both. dox migration:reset [--force] dox migrate:reset Undo every migration. dox migration:refresh [--seed] [--force] dox migrate:refresh Undo every migration, then run them all again. dox migration:fresh [--seed] [--force] dox migrate:fresh Drop every table, then run all migrations. dox migration:status dox migrate:status Print which migrations ran, and their batch.

--seed runs dox db:seed after the migrations. When APP_ENV=production, the commands that undo or drop ask first, and --force skips the question.

docs.title: Factories and seeders
docs.text: Command Aliases What it does dox make:factory <model> dox create:factory Make db/factories/<model>.factory.dart. It imports the model with the package name of pubspec.yaml. dox make:seeder <name> dox create:seeder Make db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. It updates db/seeders/seeders.dart, and makes bin/seed.dart when it is missing. dox db:seed [--class=<name>] Run the seeders with bin/seed.dart. The default seeder is DatabaseSeeder.

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
These commands run bin/queue.dart of your app. Ctrl+C and SIGTERM go to the worker, so it can finish its job before it stops.

Command Runs What it does dox make:job <name> Make lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart with a @Job() class that extends DoxJob. It makes bin/queue.dart when it is missing. Run dox build_runner:build after it. dox queue:work [flags] bin/queue.dart work [flags] Run the worker. dox queue:failed bin/queue.dart failed List the failed jobs. dox queue:retry <id\|all> bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all> Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. dox queue:forget <id> bin/queue.dart forget <id> Delete one failed job. dox queue:flush bin/queue.dart flush Delete all failed jobs. dox queue:clear [queue] bin/queue.dart clear [queue] Delete the jobs of a queue. The default queue is default. dox queue:restart bin/queue.dart restart Make the running workers stop after their current jobs. The workers must share the cache store. dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N] bin/queue.dart prune-failed [--hours=N] Delete failed jobs older than N hours. The default is 24.

Each queue command takes --connection=NAME for a connection of QueueConfig.connections. Flags of queue:work:

Flag Default Meaning --queue=a,b default The queues to read, the first one first. --concurrency=N 1 How many jobs run at the same time in this process. --once off Run one job, then stop. --tries=N 1 How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. A job can set its own tries. --timeout=S 60 Seconds a job may run. --sleep=S 3 Seconds to wait when the queues are empty. --stop-when-empty off Stop when the queues are empty. --timeout-grace=S none After a timeout, wait up to S seconds for the old run to end before the next try. --backoff=S[,S...] retry at once Seconds to wait before a retry of a job with no backoff. One value for each retry. --max-jobs=N no limit Stop after N jobs. --max-time=S no limit Stop after S seconds. --memory=MB no limit Stop when the process uses more memory. --max-sleep=S off When the queues stay empty, double the sleep up to S seconds.

This is the bin/queue.dart of a new project:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(app: appConfig).run(args);
}

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
These commands run bin/schedule.dart of your app.

Command Runs What it does dox schedule:work bin/schedule.dart work Run the scheduler and keep it running. dox schedule:run bin/schedule.dart run Run the tasks that are due now, once. dox schedule:list bin/schedule.dart list List the scheduled tasks. dox schedule:test <name> bin/schedule.dart test <name> Run one task now. dox schedule:clear-cache bin/schedule.dart clear-cache Remove the withoutOverlapping() locks that a crash left. Do not run it while a task runs.

Add tasks in lib/config/schedule.dart. These are the two files of a new project:

lib/config/schedule.dart
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

void schedule(Schedule s) {
  // s.call('cleanup', cleanup).dailyAt('02:00');
}
bin/schedule.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}

See Scheduler for the task methods, and Queue for jobs.

docs.title: Package commands
docs.text:
A package can add commands to the CLI. They show in dox help when the package is in your pubspec.yaml. See Package commands.

Command Package What it does dox orm:install dox_orm Set up the ORM and migrations. dox add orm runs it. dox auth:install dox_auth Set up access token auth. dox auth:tokens-table dox_auth Make a migration for the auth_access_tokens table. dox cache:install dox_cache Set up the cache stores. dox cache:table dox_cache_database Make a migration for the cache table. dox queue:install dox_queue Set up the queue and bin/queue.dart. dox queue:table dox_queue_database Make a migration for the queue tables. dox scheduler:install dox_scheduler Set up the scheduler and bin/schedule.dart. dox mailer:install dox_mailer Set up mail. dox storage:install dox_storage Set up file storage. dox socketio:install dox_socketio Set up Socket.IO. dox view:install dox_view Set up views. dox inertia:install dox_inertia Set up Inertia. dox inertia:start-ssr dox_inertia Start the Inertia SSR server. dox mcp:install dox_mcp Set up an MCP server. dox grpc:install dox_grpc Set up gRPC. dox graphql:install dox_graphql Set up GraphQL.

Flags of auth:tokens-table:

Flag Meaning --uuid The users have uuid ids. Set uuidIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. --string-ids The users have text ids. Set stringIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. Do not use it with --uuid. --users-table=<table> Add a foreign key from tokenable_id to this table, with cascade delete. --users-key=<column> The column of --users-table for the foreign key. Default: id. It does nothing without --users-table.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: This page lists every env var that Dox and its packages read.

docs.title: Read by the framework
docs.text:
APP_ENV changes how strict Dox is. Set APP_ENV=development in your local .env and in CI:

  • development or local: Dox shows error details in 500 answers and health checks, turns /docs on (when openApi.enabled is null), and turns the view cache off.
  • development, local, test or testing: a bad APP_KEY or a JWT secret under 32 bytes is only a warning.
  • Any other value, or no value: production. A bad key stops the app at start, /docs is off and error details are hidden.
Variable Who reads it Default Meaning Example APP_ENV dox_core, dox_auth, dox_view empty See the list above. A bad APP_KEY is one that is missing, not exactly 32 characters, or a public sample key. testing as a real env var also loads .env.testing. APP_ENV=production APP_NAME dox_core (Cache) not set The default prefix of a redis cache store: My Shop gives my_shop_cache:. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. APP_NAME="My Shop" APP_URL dox_core (Route.signedUrl) not set The scheme and host in front of an absolute signed URL. APP_URL=https://example.com PORT dox_core (DoxServer.portFor()) not set The port to listen on, when APP_PORT is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. PORT=8080 APP_HOST dox_core (DoxServer.hostFor()) not set (all interfaces, ::) The host to listen on. 127.0.0.1 keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. AppConfig.host wins over it. APP_HOST=127.0.0.1 DATABASE_URL dox_orm (DatabaseConfig.url), dox_migration not set A database url. It wins over DB_CONNECTION and the other DB_* keys. The app reads it with the line url: env.databaseUrl in lib/config/database.dart. Without that line, only the shell value is read. See Database url. DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require DB_CONNECTION dox_migration (DbConnection.config()) sqlite sqlite, postgres or mysql. Any other value is an error. DB_CONNECTION=postgres DB_HOST dox_migration localhost Database host. A path that starts with / is a Unix socket: the folder for Postgres, the socket file for MySQL. DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT dox_migration 5432 (postgres), 3306 (mysql) Database port. DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME dox_migration postgres (postgres), root (mysql) Database user. DB_USERNAME=app DB_PASSWORD dox_migration postgres (postgres), empty (mysql) Database password. DB_PASSWORD=secret DB_DATABASE dox_migration falls back to DB_NAME, then dox Database name. For sqlite: the file path. DB_DATABASE=dox DB_NAME dox_migration dox Same as DB_DATABASE. DB_DATABASE wins when both are set. DB_NAME=dox HOME / USERPROFILE build hooks of dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native empty Used to find cargo when a native library must be built from source. set by the OS DART_VM_OPTIONS the Dart VM not set Flags for the Dart VM. The binary from dox build reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See Performance. DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64

docs.title: Read by a new project
docs.text:
A new project reads these keys with its typed env class in lib/config/env.dart. In code, use the getter, like env.appPort.

Variable Getter Type Default Used for APP_NAME appName String dox LoggerConfig.name. APP_ENV appEnv String production development, staging or production. development turns on colored logs and the query log. Any value except production turns on LogMiddleware (one log line per request). The framework reads it too, see above. APP_PORT appPort int 3000 AppConfig.serverPort. When it is not set, Dox uses PORT if the env has it. APP_KEY appKey String required AppConfig.appKey. Exactly 32 characters. Run dox key:generate to make one. APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE appTotalIsolate int? not set: one per CPU the process may use (cpuset and CPU quota) AppConfig.totalIsolate. LOG_LEVEL logLevel String info LoggerConfig.level. CACHE_STORE cacheStore String file CacheConfig.defaultStore. A new project has the stores file and memory. Add a redis store in lib/config/cache.dart before you use it. STORAGE_DISK storageDisk String local StorageConfig.defaultDisk. A new project has the disk local. Add an s3 or memory disk in lib/config/storage.dart before you use it. DB_CONNECTION dbConnection String sqlite DatabaseConfig.connection: sqlite, postgres or mysql. DB_NAME dbName String db/dox.sqlite The database name. For SQLite: the file path. DB_HOST dbHost String localhost Database host. DB_PORT dbPort int? not set: 5432 for Postgres, 3306 for MySQL Database port. DB_USERNAME dbUsername String postgres Database user. DB_PASSWORD dbPassword String empty Database password.

To add a key, add a getter to AppEnv and run dart run build_runner build. See Environments.

The .env.example of a new project:

.env.example
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

docs.title: How .env is parsed
docs.text:
A real environment variable always wins over the .env file. The file is read like this:

  • One KEY=value per line. A line that starts with # is a comment.
  • export KEY=value is read like KEY=value.
  • The value is everything after the first =, so DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b works.
  • A # after a space starts a comment: KEY=abc # note gives abc. KEY=abc#def stays abc#def.
  • Quotes (", ' or `) keep the value as it is, also a #. The quotes are removed.
  • An empty value (KEY=), only spaces, or the text null counts as missing. So Env.get gives the default.
  • In tests (dart test, or APP_ENV=testing as a real env var), Dox also reads .env.testing. Its keys win over .env.
  • With CoreFlags.envExpand, ${OTHER} and "..." escapes work. See Use one value in another.
  • The file is read one time per isolate, from the current folder. Platform.environment has only the real environment.

Migrations use their own simpler parser. It does not remove # note comments, removes all quote characters, has no ${VAR} expansion and does not read .env.testing. So keep comments on their own line.
