docs.title: Error index
docs.text:
This page lists the messages that Dox shows or throws, so you can search for the text you see.

A <...> part changes, like a name or a number. Dart puts a prefix in front of some errors, like Bad state: or Invalid argument(s):.

docs.title: dox_core: start of the app
docs.text: Text When What to do APP_KEY is not set. Rundox key:generateand put the key in .env appKey is empty. The app stops. In development, local, test or testing it is only a warning. Run dox key:generate, or set APP_KEY in the env. APP_KEY must be exactly 32 characters. Rundox key:generate`` The key is shorter or longer. Same rule as above. Run dox key:generate. APP_KEY is a public sample key. Rundox key:generatefor a new one The key is a known sample key. Same rule as above. Run dox key:generate. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>. Fix: ... The native HTTP library is missing or from another version. The app stops at start. Do what the Fix: part says. See Troubleshooting. Server started at http://<host>:<port> with <n> isolate (native) Normal start. <host> is the address it listens on: [::] means all interfaces. Nothing. Windows: the native server runs on one isolate Windows has no SO_REUSEPORT. Nothing. Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ... Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. Use transports: ['websocket'] in the client. [server] isolate <n> error: <error> An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. [server] isolate <n> exited, restarting A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. Look at the error line above it. SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>) (OS Error: errno = <errno>), port = <port> The port is in use. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: routes and controllers
docs.text:
These stop the app at start.

Text When What to do Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, an @Inject class, a @DoxModel, a type from Route.bind, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ... A controller parameter has another type, the DTO is not in AppConfig.dtos, the class is not in the container, or there is no Route.bind<T> for a {param} of the route. Change the type or add the binder. Run dart run build_runner build, and set dtos: dtos and container: registerContainer in AppConfig. Route <where>: the action gives a function. Give it one controller parameter from the container, like (UserController c) => c.index. ... A route action like (c) => c.index where Dox can not find the controller class. Give the parameter its type, and mark the controller class with @Inject(). Bad state: <T> is not in the container. Add @Inject() above the class and rundart run build_runner build. ... Dox needs a class that is not in the container. Do what the text says, and set AppConfig(container: registerContainer). Route name "<name>" is used twice: <method> <path> and <method> <path>. Two routes have the same name. Give one of them another name. Invalid argument (name): No route has this name: "<name>" route() or Route.url() with a name that no route has. Check the name and the group name: prefix. Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) needs the param "<param>". route() without a value for a {param}. Pass it in params:. Invalid argument(s): An absolute url needs a host. ... route() with absolute: true and no APP_URL and no baseUrl:. Set APP_URL, or pass baseUrl:. Bad state: No bound value of type <T> for the route param "<param>". ... req.bound<T>() for a param with no Route.bind, or of another type. Add Route.bind<T>('<param>', ...). Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>). The method asks for more path params than the path has. Add the {param} to the path, or remove the parameter. Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only. Two DTO parameters. Merge them into one DTO. Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>). Named or [optional] parameters. Use positional parameters. Use int? with {id?} for an optional param. Route <where>: a controller can not be generic. The handler has type parameters. Remove them. Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>. Dox can not read the function type of the handler. Use a plain method or function.

docs.title: dox_core: env
docs.text:
Text When What to do EnvException: the env is not valid then - <KEY> is missing AppEnv.load() found a required key with no value. Set the key, or give the getter a default. - <KEY> must be <type> A value does not fit the getter type. Fix the value. Check for a # comment after it. Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default Env.get<int>(), <num>, <double> or <bool> with no value and no default. Set the key, or pass a default. Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type> Env.get<int>() (or another type) got text that is not that type. Fix the value.

See Environment variables.

docs.title: dox_core: requests (what the client gets)
docs.text:
An HTTP exception with a text message answers {"code":"<errorCode>","message":"<text>"}. The table shows the message text.

Status Message When What to do 404 <METHOD> <path> not found No route matches. Check the method, the path and the router prefix. 404 Not Found A typed path param does not fit, like abc for int id, or a Route.bind finds no row. Send a valid value. 400 The body is not valid JSON A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. Send valid JSON. 400 The form body is not valid A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. Fix the client encoding. 415 Unsupported Media Type A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. Send Content-Type: application/json or form data. 413 Payload Too Large The body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize. Send less, or raise the limit. 419 CSRF token mismatch CsrfMiddleware finds no CSRF token, or a wrong one, on a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Send the token. See CSRF. 429 Too Many Requests A RateLimit middleware sees too many requests. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait. Wait, then try again. See Rate limiting. 422 {"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"} Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. Send less nested data. 422 {"<field>":"<message>"} A DTO check failed. The core flag laravelErrors changes the shape. See Validation rules. 431 (no text) Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. Send smaller headers or cookies. 500 Server Error, code server_error. In development or local, the body is the error text. Any error that is not an HTTP exception. It also goes to ExceptionHandler.report. Look at the server log.

docs.title: dox_core: DTOs, storage and config
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: This request has no session. Add SessionMiddleware() to globalMiddleware or to the route. req.session on a route with no SessionMiddleware. Do what the text says. See Session. Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, rundart run build_runner buildand setdtos: dtos(lib/generated/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig. req.validate<T>() can not find T. Do what the text says. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>" A disk in StorageConfig has a driver other than local, s3 or memory. Fix the driver name. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" needs the "<setting>" setting. It is missing or empty. An s3 disk without bucket, key or secret, on its first use. Set AWS_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Invalid argument(s): invalid file Storage().putFile() with bytes and no extension:, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. Pass extension: 'pdf'. 403 invalid or expired signature A Storage.route() URL without a valid signature, or after expires. Make a new link with Storage().signedUrl(). 404 file not found Storage().stream(), download(), copy(), move(), getVisibility(), setVisibility(), size() or lastModified() of a missing file. Check the path. Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>" A bad entry in AppConfig.trustedProxies. Use an IP, a CIDR like 10.0.0.0/8, or *. Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>" orderBy(column, type) with another direction. Use asc or desc. 400 decrypt_failed, The encrypted value is not valid AESEncryptor.decode got changed text or a wrong key. req.cookie() gives null instead. The core flag decryptServerError makes it a reported 500. Check the key. For a cookie, ask the user to log in again.

docs.title: dox_auth
docs.text:
Text When What to do 401 Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Log in again. Invalid argument(s) (password): The password is too long. bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes. Hash.make() or Hash.makeAsync() with a password over 72 bytes. Limit the length in the DTO. See Troubleshooting. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is empty. Set APP_KEY (rundox key:generate). JwtAuthDriver with an empty secret. Set APP_KEY. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is <n> bytes. It must be at least 32 bytes. ... A short secret. In development, local, test and testing it is only a warning. Run dox key:generate. 401 The access token was already rotated. rotateAccessToken on a token that was rotated before. A token can be rotated only once. Use the new token. Bad state: The table 'auth_access_tokens' has no rotated_at column. ... rotateAccessToken on a token table without the rotated_at column. Add the column in a migration. See Authentication.

Hash.verify() gives false for a value that is not a bcrypt hash, and Auth().attempt() gives null for a wrong password. More auth errors are in Authentication: Problems.

docs.title: dox_orm
docs.text: Text When What to do Unsupported operation: dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to Postgres. Fix: ... The native Postgres library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See Postgres native. Unsupported operation: dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to MySQL. Fix: ... The native MySQL library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See MySQL native. PgServerException(<code>): <message> The Postgres server refused the query, for example code 23505 for a unique violation. Read code, detail and constraint on the exception. MysqlException(<code>, <sqlState>): <message> An error from MySQL, for example code 1062 for a duplicate key. Read code and sqlState on the exception. Exception: <name> not found DatabaseConfig.connection (or withConnection()) names a connection that is not in connections. Fix DB_CONNECTION or the map. Exception: Invalid driver or not supported A ConnectionConfig.driver Dox can not open. Use Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql or Driver.sqlite. Invalid argument(s): dox_postgres_native: bad connection config The native driver can not read the connection values. Check host, port, user, database. Invalid argument(s): dox_mysql_native: bad connection config Same, for MySQL. Same. SqliteException with unable to open database file The SQLite folder does not exist. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_orm: schema builder
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: foreign key <name>: call on(table) table.foreign('x').references('id') with no .on('table'). Add .on('table'), or use foreignId('x').constrained(). Unsupported operation: postgres: change() of an auto increment column is not supported change() on an id() or increments() column. Write the ALTER by hand with schema.driver.execute(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not add a primary key to an existing table primary(...) in schema.table() on SQLite. Make the table again with the key in schema.create(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has CHECK constraints A SQLite rebuild (change(), foreign(), dropForeign()) on a table with other CHECKs. Make the new table by hand in the migration. Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has generated columns Same, on a table with generated columns. Same. Bad state: sqlite: table <table> not found A SQLite rebuild of a missing table. Check the table name. Bad state: sqlite: column <table>.<column> not found change() or renameColumn() of a missing column on SQLite. Check the column name. Bad state: sqlite: foreign key <names> not found dropForeign() of a key the table does not have. Check the key name or columns. Bad state: sqlite: rebuild of <table> breaks foreign keys After the rebuild, rows point to missing parent rows. Fix the data first. Unsupported operation: sqlite: change() rebuilds the table, it only runs on a database table.toSql(SqliteGrammar()) with change(). Run it on a database, not as text.

docs.title: dox_migration
docs.text:
Text When What to do Migration failed: <name> then the error A migration threw, or the migrator can not reach the database. Read the error below it. For a connection error, check DATABASE_URL or the DB_* values. A real env var wins over .env. Unknown migration command: <cmd> (use run, rollback, reset, refresh, fresh or status) dart run bin/migrate.dart <cmd> with another command. Use one of the six. Invalid argument(s): Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count> rollback with a bad option. Use --step=2. Bad state: Migration <name> is both a Dart and a .sql migration Two files with the same name in db/migration. Rename or delete one. Bad state: foreign key check failed: <table> points to a missing <parent> row SQLite: a migration left a broken foreign key. Fix the data in the migration. Migrating: <name> / Migrated: <name> Normal progress. Nothing. Migrations are already up to date! Nothing to run. Nothing. Nothing to rollback! No batch to undo. Nothing. No migrations found. status with no migrations. Check db/migration. Bad state: Seeder <name> not found. Seeders: <names> dox db:seed --class=<name> with a seeder that is not in db/seeders/seeders.dart. Check the name, or add the seeder to the list. Invalid argument(s): Unknown option <x>, use --class=<name> dox db:seed with another option. Use --class=UserSeeder.

See Migration.

docs.title: dox_cache
docs.text:
Text When What to do Invalid argument(s): Cache store "<name>" is not configured Cache().store('<name>') or defaultStore names a missing store. Add the store to CacheConfig.stores, or fix CACHE_STORE. Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported A store has a driver other than file, memory, redis or null. Fix the driver name. Unsupported operation: <Driver> does not support locks lock() on the file or null store. Use the memory or redis store. Bad state: Cache value of "<key>" is not an integer increment() or decrement() on a value that is not an int. Store an int, or forget() the key. Invalid argument(s): Cache value of "<key>" is bigger than <limit> bytes A Redis value is too big. Store less, or use files or a database. Bad state: RedisDriver.flush needs a prefix. It will not delete the whole database. flush() on a Redis store with an empty prefix. Set a prefix.

See Cache.

docs.title: dox_storage
docs.text:
The text has the form <Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>").

Text When What to do FileNotFoundException: File not found The file is not on the disk. Check the path. Storage() paths start with /, Disk keys do not. PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied The OS (local) or S3 (403) refused it. Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed A key with ... Do not build keys from user input. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed A Disk key that starts with / or a drive letter. Remove the first /. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty An empty key. Storage().deleteDirectory() with '', '/' or '.' also gives it, because the root is refused. Pass a file or folder name. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs signedUrl() on a local disk with no url, or no APP_KEY. Set both. UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days signedUrl() on S3 with a bad expiresIn. Use a time up to 7 days. UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered Storage().disk('<name>') with a missing disk. Add the disk to StorageConfig.disks. DriverException: <S3 error> Any other S3 error (network, 500, wrong bucket). Read the S3 code in the text.

See File storage.

docs.title: dox_validation
docs.text:
Text When What to do Bad state: Schema has async rules. Use parseAsync() instead. schema.parse() on a schema with an async rule. Use await schema.parseAsync(). Bad state: Rule "<name>" is async. Use parseAsync() instead. Same, for one AsyncRule. Same. Bad state: This refine is async. Use parseAsync() instead. refine() with an async function and sync parse. Same. Bad state: DTO <name> has an async validate(). Use parseAsync() instead. A DTO with Future<void> validate() checked with a sync call. Use the async call, like req.validate<T>(). Bad state: No value: the key was missing. Check isPresent. maybe.value on a Maybe<T> that is missing. Check isPresent first.

docs.title: dox_builder (build_runner)
docs.text:
These stop dart run build_runner build.

Text When What to do The @Dto class <Name> has problems: then a - ... list One or more lines below. Fix each line. - The field <Class.field> must be final. A DTO field is not final. Add final. - The field <Class.field> must be athis.parameter of the unnamed constructor. The field is not set by the constructor. Add this.<field> to the constructor. - A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor. Only named constructors. Add const Name({...}). - A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>). The DTO extends a class. Copy the fields in. - A @Dto class can not be generic. The DTO has type parameters. Remove them. - The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them. Field type not supported. Change the type. - @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>. A rule on the wrong type, like @Email() on an int. Move the rule, or change the type. - @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both. @Length() with no limit. Add min: or max:. - The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason> The pattern does not compile. Fix the pattern. - @<Rule> on <where> needs a size like '2MB' (units B, KB, MB, GB), not "<text>". Bad size text on @MaxSize or @MinSize. Use '2MB'. - @Dimensions on <where> needs at least one limit, like minWidth:. @Dimensions() with no limit. Add a limit, like minWidth: 100. - The Maybe field <where> needs the defaultconst Maybe.missing(). A Maybe<T> field without that default. Add it. - <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase. Both on one field. Keep one. - The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors:void validate(DtoErrors errors). Wrong validate signature. Use that signature. Two @Dto classes are named <Name>: in <a> and <b>. Dox finds DTOs by name, so rename one. Two DTOs with the same class name. Rename one. Env getter "<name>" has type <T>. Use String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, an enum or List<String>. A @DoxEnv getter with another type. Change the type. @DoxModel can only be used on a class. / @DoxEnv can only be used on a class. The annotation is on something else. Put it on a class. Conflicting outputs were detected ... build_runner cache is out of date. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Native libraries (build hooks)
docs.text:
These show during dart pub get, dox serve or dox build. <pkg> is dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native or dox_mysql_native. When a library is missing, the app stops with the reason and the fix.

Text When What to do <pkg>: no native library for <os>-<arch>. No ready build for this OS and CPU. Install Rust. <pkg>: download <file>: <status> / <pkg>: download <file> failed: <error> The GitHub download failed. Check the network, then dart pub get again. <pkg>: sha256 of <file> does not match The downloaded file is not the expected one. Delete .dart_tool and try again. <pkg>: cargo build failed The build from source failed. Read the cargo output below it. Bad state: <pkg>: <path> does not exist The lib_path user define points to a missing file. Fix the path in pubspec.yaml. <pkg> did not load: the native library is not in the build (...). The app opens Postgres or MySQL, but pubspec.yaml skips that driver. Remove its skip line. See Skip unused drivers. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native can not detach the socket. Use NativeWebSocket.upgrade for a WebSocket. Code called detachSocket() on a response. Rust owns the socket. For a WebSocket use NativeWebSocket.upgrade(request).

See Native server.

docs.title: dox_socketio
docs.text:
These show on stderr. The connection or the request fails, and the app continues.

Text When What to do dox_socketio: handler error: <error> Your namespace handler threw. The stack follows. Fix the handler. dox_socketio: request error: <error> A Socket.IO HTTP request failed. The client gets 500. Check the client version and transport. dox_socketio: publish failed: <error> The Redis or isolate adapter could not publish. Redis adapter: check Redis. Isolate adapter: it should not happen, so report it as a bug. dox_socketio: bad adapter message: <error> The Redis or isolate adapter got a message it can not read. Check that every app on the channel runs the same version.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Troubleshooting: problems that need a longer fix.
  • HTTP exceptions: the error classes and their status codes.
  • CLI: all commands and their options.

docs.title: HTTP exceptions
docs.text:
An HTTP exception stops a request and sends an error answer with the right status code, like 404 or 403.

Each HTTP exception extends IHttpException, with three fields: the status code, a short errorCode and a message. Throw it, or return it from a middleware or a controller.

docs.title: Throwing an exception
docs.text:
Throw one of the classes below when a request cannot continue:

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

The client gets a JSON body with the error code and the message:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}

docs.title: The classes
docs.text:
Most classes take the named parameters message, errorCode and code. The table shows the defaults.

Class Package code errorCode Default message Dox throws it when BadRequestException dox_core 400 bad_request Bad Request the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid UnAuthorizedException dox_auth 401 unauthorized Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no valid token ForbiddenHttpException dox_core 403 forbidden Forbidden never; it is for your own use NotFoundHttpException dox_core 404 not_found Not Found no route fits (message <METHOD> <path> not found), a typed path param does not fit ({id} is not an int), or route model binding finds no row MethodNotAllowedHttpException dox_core 405 method_not_allowed Method Not Allowed the path has routes, but not for this method. The Allow header lists the methods, like Allow: GET, POST, HEAD. PayloadTooLargeException dox_core 413 payload_too_large Payload Too Large the body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize UnsupportedMediaTypeException dox_core 415 unsupported_media_type Unsupported Media Type a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data TokenMismatchException dox_core 419 csrf_token_mismatch CSRF token mismatch CsrfMiddleware finds no CSRF token, or a wrong one ValidationException dox_core 422 validation_failed {} (a Map) a DTO, req.validate() or schema.parse() of dox_validation finds bad input TooManyRequestsException dox_core 429 too_many_requests Too Many Requests a RateLimit middleware sees too many requests InternalErrorException dox_core 500 server_error Server Error never; it is for your own use QueryException dox_core 500 sql_query_error Error in sql query never; it is for your own use

docs.title: Any status: abort and HttpStatusException
docs.text:
For a status with no class, use abort(code):

if (post.userId != req.auth?.id()) abort(403);

You can also pass a message:

abort(404, 'No post with this id');

abort throws an HttpStatusException. Throw it yourself to send headers too:

throw HttpStatusException(503,
    headers: <String, String>{'retry-after': '60'});

Common codes get a default errorCode and message, like forbidden and Forbidden for 403:

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"code":"forbidden","message":"Forbidden"}

Other codes get http_error and Error.

docs.title: What the client gets
docs.text:
The status is the code of the exception, and the body is JSON. A text message gives {"code": "<errorCode>", "message": "<message>"}. For your own JSON shape, give a map as the message:

throw NotFoundHttpException(
    message: <String, String>{'error': 'not_found'});
// 404 {"error":"not_found"}

A ValidationException always has a map, with one entry per field:

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}

A form post with a session gets a redirect back, with the errors and the old input in the session. See Session.

docs.title: Other errors
docs.text:
Any other error gives 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. When APP_ENV is development or local, the body is the error text.

These errors go to the report method of the exception handler. An HTTP exception with a 5xx code also goes there.

docs.title: Making your own exception
docs.text:
Extend IHttpException and set the three fields in the constructor:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PaymentRequiredException extends IHttpException {
  PaymentRequiredException({
    dynamic message = 'Please pay',
    String errorCode = 'payment_required',
    int code = HttpStatus.paymentRequired,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}

To give each error the same JSON shape, override toResponse(). It returns the body.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Error handling: report and render errors.
  • Response: more error examples.
  • Error index: each message that Dox shows or throws.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
This page lists what to check before you deploy a Dox app.

Go through each table one time before your first deploy. An item marked "Dox limit" is a task that you do outside Dox.

docs.title: Secrets and config
docs.text: Check How Read more APP_KEY is set, 32 characters and secret Run dox key:generate, or set a random value of exactly 32 characters in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from .env.example. Encryption APP_ENV=production Set it, or leave it empty: both mean production. A bad APP_KEY then stops the app at start, /docs is off and error details are hidden. Env reference The env is complete Run dox env:check in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. CLI No secrets in the image or in git Put .env in .dockerignore and .gitignore. Pass values as env vars (docker run -e, env_file:, systemd EnvironmentFile=). dox build copies only .env.example. Docker No comments after values in .env The app strips # note, but migrations keep it in the value. Put comments on their own line. Env reference

docs.title: Auth and passwords
docs.text: Check How Read more JWT tokens expire JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn is 1 hour by default. Pick a time that fits your app, like expiresIn: Duration(hours: 12). Authentication A JWT works until it expires The server keeps no token list by default. To revoke tokens, set revocation: true on JwtAuthDriver, or use AccessTokenAuthDriver (tokens live in a table). To log out everyone, change APP_KEY with no previousKeys. Authentication Passwords are hashed Use user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(input) (bcrypt, on another isolate). Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hashing The hash is never sent Add List<String> get hidden => <String>['password']; to the user model. The JWT payload is user.toJson(), and anyone can read it. Authentication Passwords have a max length bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes, and Hash.make throws on longer input. Add @MaxLength(72) to the password field of the DTO. Troubleshooting

docs.title: HTTP and network
docs.text: Check How Read more HTTPS at the proxy Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. Deployment trustedProxies is set behind a proxy Set AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']), or the proxy network, like '172.16.0.0/12'. Without it, req.ip() is the proxy and req.scheme() is http. Do not use ['*'] when the app port is public. App config Body limits are on Keep maxBodySize (10 MB) and maxMultipartSize (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: client_max_body_size 100m; Request CORS has real origins Use CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app'), or a list like <String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app']. CORS No credentials: true with origin: '*' The browser refuses this pair. The new project's cors.dart has credentials: true and a localhost origin. When you turn CORS on, put your real origins in the list. CORS Rate limiting Add RateLimit(...) to login and other busy routes. Use a Redis cache store, so all servers share the counts. You can also limit at the proxy. Rate limiting Security headers Add const SecurityHeaders() to globalMiddleware. Security headers gzip at the proxy Keep compress: false. Turn on gzip in Caddy (encode gzip) or nginx (gzip on;). Performance OpenAPI docs They are off in production. Do not set enabled: true for a private API. OpenAPI

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text: Check How Read more AOT binary, not dart run Run dox build, then build/bundle/bin/server. Keep bin/ and lib/ together. Do not use dart compile exe. Deployment Native server loads The start line says (native). If the library does not load, the app stops and prints the fix. Native server Native database driver loads The database works. If the library does not load, the app stops and prints the fix. Postgres native Isolates = cores Keep the default totalIsolate. It uses the CPUs the container allows (cpuset and CPU quota). Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. With SQLite, 1-2 isolates are enough. Isolate Shared state across isolates Use a redis cache, not memory. For Socket.IO, use transports: ['websocket'] on the client, and a Redis adapter with many servers. Isolate A supervisor restarts the process Use Docker restart: unless-stopped, or systemd Restart=always. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. Deployment Writable temp folder Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A FROM scratch image needs /tmp with mode 1777. Docker Uploads live on a volume or S3 The local disk writes to storage/. Mount it as a volume, or use the s3 disk. File storage

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Check How Read more Postgres or MySQL for a busy app SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate, so use it for small apps only. Give it an absolute file path. Database Migrations run once per deploy The new project runs migrations in bin/server.dart before startServer(). Or run dox migrate once in CI. With many machines, run migrations in one place only, so two machines do not migrate at the same time. Migration Migrations use the right database Migrations also read a .env file, so a key that is only in an old .env is still used. Do not ship a .env next to the binary, or give Migrator(config: ...) your own config. Migration Small MySQL migrations MySQL saves CREATE, ALTER and DROP at once, so a failed migration can leave half the changes. Make one table change per migration. Migration Pool size fits the database Set extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10}. All isolates share one pool, so this is the total for the process. Keep it under the database max_connections. Database Query logging is off debug: true prints every query. The new project turns it on only in development. Database Backups Dox limit: Dox has no backup tool. Use pg_dump, mysqldump, managed snapshots, or sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db". Test a restore.

docs.title: Logs and errors
docs.text: Check How Read more JSON logs Use LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false). The new project does this outside development. App config Log level Set LOG_LEVEL=warn to print only warnings and errors. App config Access logs in one place LogMiddleware logs one line per request. The new project turns it off in production, because the proxy already logs requests. Log lines are written every 20 ms, so a hard kill can lose the last lines. Performance Errors go to your tracker Extend ExceptionHandler and set AppConfig.exceptionHandler. Every error that is not an HTTP exception goes to its report method. Error handling

docs.title: Health and shutdown
docs.text: Check How Read more Health route Add Route.health('/health', checks: ...) with a database check, so the load balancer knows when the app can not serve. Health check Graceful shutdown On SIGTERM or SIGINT, Dox stops taking connections and lets open requests finish. Set shutdownTimeout below the kill timeout of your platform. Close your own connections in the shutdown() of a provider. Deployment Zero downtime deploys Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. Deployment

docs.title: Rate limit at the proxy
docs.text:
You can also limit requests at the proxy, so bad clients never reach the app.

nginx:

# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;

Caddy needs the caddy-ratelimit plugin. Build Caddy with it:

xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit

Then add the limit:

example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

The proxy must see the real client IP. If a load balancer is in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.

docs.text:
• Deployment: build and run the app in production.
  • Environments: config and secrets for each environment.

docs.title: Request and response
docs.text: This page lists the members of DoxRequest, DoxResponse and the response helpers.

docs.title: DoxRequest
docs.text: A controller and an IDoxNextMiddleware get a DoxRequest. An IDoxMiddleware gets an IDoxRequest, with fewer members. The last column shows its members.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest validate<T>({Source? source}) Future<T> The request checked with the DTO T. Bad input gives 422. Throws StateError when T is not in AppConfig.dtos. no validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema) Future<O> Query and body checked with a fluent dox_validation schema. no all() Map<String, dynamic> Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. yes only(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> Only these keys from all(). A missing key gives null. yes input(String key, [dynamic defaultValue]) dynamic One value from all(). A dot key like user.name or items.0.id reads inside maps and lists. You get the default when the key is not there or is null. IDoxRequest has no default value. yes except(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> All values from all(), without these keys. no has(String key) bool true when the key is there and its text is not empty. yes exists(String key) bool true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null). no missing(String key) bool true when the key is not there. no filled(String key) bool true when the key is there and not empty. Dot keys work. no boolean(String key, [bool defaultValue = false]) bool true for true, 1, on and yes. no integer(String key, [int defaultValue = 0]) int The value as an int. The default is used when the key is not there or is not a number. no file(String key) RequestFile? The uploaded file, or null when the field is not a file. no hasFile(String key) bool true when the field holds a file or a list of files. no add(String key, dynamic value) void Adds a value to all() and body. yes merge(Map<String, dynamic> values) void Adds many values to all() and body. yes body Map<String, dynamic> The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are RequestFile. no query Map<String, dynamic> The query string. no param Map<String, dynamic> The route params, like {'id': '5'}. no pathParams Map<String, String> The route params as text. null values are left out. no bound<T>(String param) T The value that Route.bind made for this route param. Throws StateError when there is none. no requestBody RequestBody The body as it was read, for DTOs. no isJson() bool The content type is JSON. yes isFormData() bool The content type is form data (multipart/form-data or urlencoded). yes toJson() Map<String, dynamic> all() with files replaced by their file name. Lets jsonEncode(req) work. yes

docs.title: Headers, cookies and client
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest header(String key) String? One header. null when it is not there. yes headers Map<String, dynamic> Every header. Many values of one name are joined. yes httpHeaders HttpHeaders The dart:io headers object. no contentType ContentType? The parsed Content-Type. yes bearerToken() String? The token of Authorization: Bearer <token>, or null. no cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true}) String? One cookie. Decrypted with appKey unless decrypt: false. yes ip() String The client IP, or unknown. From X-Forwarded-For only behind a trusted proxy. yes scheme() String http or https. From X-Forwarded-Proto only behind a trusted proxy. no isSecure() bool scheme() is https. no clientIp String? The client IP, or null. no userAgent() String The User-Agent header, or unknown. yes host() String The Host header, or unknown. yes origin() String? The Origin header. yes referer() String? The Referer header. yes locale String? The first language of Accept-Language, like th. null when there is none or it is *. no auth IAuth? The auth object set by AuthMiddleware. req.auth?.id() gives the user id. It is null for a guest. yes expectsJson() bool The client wants JSON: an Accept header with json, a JSON body, or X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. An Inertia request is not. no DoxRequest.expectsJsonFor(HttpHeaders headers) bool The same check as expectsJson(), for raw headers. A static method. no requestId String? The id that the RequestId middleware set, or null. no protocolVersion String The HTTP version: 1.0, 1.1 or 2.0. no

docs.title: Session
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest session Session The session of the request. Needs SessionMiddleware. Throws StateError without it. no hasSession bool true when the request has a session. no

docs.title: Route and raw request
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest method String The HTTP method in upper case. yes uri Uri The request URI. yes route RouteData The matched route. no getRouteData() RouteData Same as route. yes path() String The request path, like /admin/users/5. no fullUrl() String The full URL with the query string. no pathIs(String pattern) bool true when the path matches. * matches any text. no routeIs(String pattern) bool true when the route name matches. It is false for a route with no name. no getRouteIdentifier() String A key for the route (base64 of <method>|<domain><path>). Useful for a cache or rate limit key. yes httpRequest HttpRequest The dart:io request. Use it for raw access. yes takeOverResponse() void Your handler sends the response itself on httpRequest.response, and Dox sends nothing more. Your code must close the response. no responseTakenOver bool True after takeOverResponse(). no

docs.title: DoxResponse
docs.text:
Each setter returns the same DoxResponse, so you can chain the calls.

Member Returns What it does DoxResponse(dynamic content) DoxResponse The constructor. content can be a String, number, Map, List, a JSON serializable object, a Stream<List<int>>, a File, a StreamFile or a DownloadableFile. statusCode(int code) DoxResponse Sets the status. Default 200. status int? The status set with statusCode(), or null (which means 200). content(dynamic content) DoxResponse Replaces the content. getContent() dynamic The content as it was given. stream(Stream<List<int>> stream) DoxResponse Sets a byte stream as content. contentType(ContentType type) DoxResponse Sets Content-Type. A File without it gets the type from its extension. header(String key, dynamic value, {bool? replace}) DoxResponse Sets one header. A second call with the same key, in any case, replaces the value. A value that a middleware already put on the response stays, unless replace is true. When replace is null, CoreFlags.replaceHeaders decides. headers Map<String, dynamic> The headers set so far, by name. withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values) DoxResponse Adds these headers. A key replaces the header with the same name, in any case. Other headers stay. cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false}) DoxResponse Adds a Set-Cookie header. setExpire: true sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. cache(Duration duration) DoxResponse Sets Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>.

docs.title: Response helpers
docs.text:
These top level functions give a DoxResponse.

Function What it does response([dynamic content]) Same as DoxResponse(content). redirect(String url, {int status = 302}) A redirect to url. It sets the Location header. back(DoxRequest req, {String fallback = '/'}) A 302 redirect to the Referer header, or to fallback when there is none.

docs.title: How the content is sent
docs.text:
A controller can return a plain value or a DoxResponse:

Content Sent as null an empty body String text, as it is Map, List, number, bool, object with toJson() JSON, Content-Type: application/json DateTime its ISO 8601 text File streamed, with Content-Length, Accept-Ranges and one Range supported StreamFile streamed with its content type. An HTML, XML or JavaScript type is sent as a download, in a sandbox. DownloadableFile streamed with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>" Stream<List<int>> streamed chunk by chunk IHttpException its status and toResponse(), see HTTP exceptions other Exception or Error 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. In development or local, the body is the error text.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists known problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix.

docs.title: The native HTTP library did not load
docs.text:
Symptom: The app stops at start with this error:

Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>.
Fix: install Rust (cargo, see https://rustup.rs), then run the app again ...

At build time (dart pub get, dox serve or dox build) you may also see one of these:

dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Install Rust (cargo) to build it from source.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed

Cause: The package could not find, download or build its native library. Common reasons:

  • There was no internet during dart pub get, or there is no ready build for your OS and CPU. Ready builds exist for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, and Windows x64.
  • Rust is not installed, so the library can not be built from source.
  • You compiled with dart compile exe. It does not run build hooks, so the binary has no native library.
  • The reason is native library ABI <x>, expected <y>: the library on disk is from another version of the package.

Fix: Pick one:

  1. Install Rust with rustup and run dart pub get again. Dox then builds the library with cargo.
  2. If the reason is an ABI mismatch and you set lib_path, rebuild that library: run cargo build --release in the native folder of the dox-http-native repo.

  3. Download the library yourself from the GitHub releases, and point to it in the root pubspec.yaml:

    hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_http_native:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so

  4. Build with dox build, not with dart compile exe.

The native database drivers load their library the same way. When it does not load, the app stops with:

dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>.
dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>.

The fix is the same as above, with the dox-postgres-native or dox-mysql-native repo.

See Native server, Postgres native and MySQL native.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Symptom: At start:

SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>) (OS Error: errno = <errno>), port = 3000

The errno is 48 on macOS and 98 on Linux.

Cause: Another process listens on the port, like an old bin/server.dart or a second copy of the app.

Fix: Find and stop the process, or use another port:

lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>

Or set APP_PORT=3001 in .env.

docs.title: build_runner: conflicting outputs
docs.text:
Symptom: dox build_runner:build, dox serve or dox build stops with a build_runner message that starts with Conflicting outputs were detected, and names files like lib/generated/dtos.g.dart or lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart.

Cause: The generated .g.dart files are on disk, but .dart_tool/build does not know them. This happens after a git clone with committed .g.dart files, after deleting .dart_tool, or after a Dart SDK update.

Fix: Delete the build cache and build again:

rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build

If that is not enough, delete the .g.dart files that the message names, and build again.

docs.title: Ambiguous import: Uuid, Name or Schema
docs.text:
Symptom: The analyzer or the build says a name like Uuid, Name, Range, Image or Schema is an "ambiguous import".

Cause: dox_core exports the validation rules (Uuid, Name, Range, Image, ...) and the Schema class. Another import has a class with the same name, like package:uuid. dox_orm also has a Schema class.

Fix: Hide the name you do not use in that file:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

docs.title: A .env value with #
docs.text:
A # after a space starts a comment. The comment is not part of the value.

APP_PORT=3000 # dev port   -> 3000
DB_PASSWORD=abc#123        -> abc#123 (no space before the #)
DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"    -> abc # 123 (quotes keep the #)

When a value must have # in it (a space, then #), put the value in quotes. The quotes are removed.

docs.title: Hash.make throws on a long password
docs.text:
Symptom: Saving a user, or registering, gives a 500. The log shows:

Invalid argument(s) (password): The password is too long. bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes.

Cause: Hash.make() and Hash.makeAsync() use bcrypt, which takes at most 72 bytes. So Dox throws an ArgumentError for a longer password.

Fix: Refuse long passwords in your DTO, before you hash them:

@MaxLength(72)
final String password;

@MaxLength counts characters, not bytes, so a password with non-ASCII characters can still be over 72 bytes. See Hashing.

docs.title: MySQL 8 login fails
docs.text:
Symptom: The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the mysql client. Often the user was made with the default caching_sha2_password plugin.

Cause: caching_sha2_password needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

Fix: The Dox MySQL driver supports this plugin. Check these settings of the connection in lib/config/database.dart:

Setting What to do Remote host without TLS Turn on useSSL: true. useSSL: true The server must have TLS on. host, port, user, password A wrong value gives the same login error. DB_PORT is 3306 by default for MySQL.

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';

docs.title: SQLite: the database file
docs.text:
Symptom: An SqliteException with unable to open database file, or an empty database after dox build.

Cause: A relative path starts from the folder where you start the app. After dox build you run the app from build/bundle, where the database is a new empty file. Also, SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

Fix:

  • Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
  • Set it with DB_NAME, like DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite.
  • Migrations read DB_DATABASE or DB_NAME as the path too, so use the same value.
  • Do not use :memory: with more than one isolate. Each isolate gets its own empty database.

docs.title: dox: command not found after dart pub global activate
docs.text:
Symptom:

zsh: command not found: dox

right after dart pub global activate dox.

Cause: The dox script is in $HOME/.pub-cache/bin, and that folder is not in your path.

Fix: Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

On Windows the folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin.

docs.text:
