  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}

These types work:

Parameter type Dox gives DoxRequest the request a @Dto class the checked body or query. See Validation. String, int, double, num, bool the path params, in the order of the route the same types with ? an optional path param ({id?}). null when it is not in the URL. a @DoxModel class the model, loaded by the route param. See route model binding. an @Inject() class the instance from the container

The parameters can be in any order. The first path param parameter gets the first {...} in the route. These rules apply:

  • At most one @Dto parameter.
  • Only positional parameters.
  • A catch-all {path*} param is a string.
  • The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.

The server does not start when a parameter type is not in the list, or when the method has more path params than the route.

docs.title: Path param types
docs.text:
Dox changes the text from the URL into the type. Text that does not fit gets 404:

  • int: "42" is 42. "abc" or "4.5" gives 404.
  • double, num: "4.5" is 4.5.
  • bool: true or 1 is true. false or 0 is false. Any other text gives 404.

Dox checks path params before the DTO.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Response: return a string, a map, a model, a file and more.
  • Dependency injection: give services to a controller.
  • Request: read the input.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
The Dox container makes your classes and gives each constructor what it needs, so you never wire classes by hand.

Put @Inject() above a class, and dox_builder adds it to the container. Then any class can ask for it in its constructor.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
The builder writes lib/generated/container.g.dart. Give it to the app one time:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
);

Run the builder again after you add a class:

dart run build_runner build

Do not edit the generated file. Dox finds classes in lib/ only.

docs.title: A full example
docs.text:
A repository reads the database, a service holds the business logic, and a controller answers the route. Each one asks for the one below it:

lib/app/repositories/user.repository.dart
@Inject()
class UserRepository {
  Future<User?> find(int id) => User().find(id);
}
lib/app/services/user.service.dart
@Inject()
class UserService {
  UserService(this.users);

  final UserRepository users;

  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await users.find(id);
    if (user == null) throw NotFoundHttpException();
    return user;
  }
}
lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
@Inject()
class UserController {
  UserController(this.service);

  final UserService service;

  Future<User> show(int id) => service.show(id);
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show);

GET /api/users/5 makes the repository, the service and the controller, and calls show(5).

docs.title: Lifetime
docs.text:
@Inject() makes one instance for each isolate, on first use. For a new instance each time, use singleton: false:

@Inject(singleton: false)
class ReportBuilder {}

Isolates do not share objects. Keep state that all isolates must see in the cache or the database.

docs.title: Constructor parameters
docs.text: Dox finds each constructor parameter by its type. Positional and named parameters both work. If the type is not in the container, an optional parameter keeps its default, and a nullable parameter gets null.

docs.title: Abstract types
docs.text:
A parameter of an abstract type gets the one container class that implements it:

abstract class Mailer {}

@Inject()
class SmtpMailer implements Mailer {}

@Inject()
class SignupService {
  SignupService(this.mailer); // gets the SmtpMailer

  final Mailer mailer;
}

This works for constructor parameters only. get<Mailer>() and handler parameters need the class itself.

docs.title: Routes to controller methods
docs.text:
Pass a function that picks the method. Dox finds the controller by the parameter type, one time for each isolate at start:

Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
Route.resource('posts', PostController);

See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Handler parameters
docs.text:
A controller method or a route function can ask for any class of the container:

Route.get('/stats', (StatsService stats) => stats.today());

Dox reads a singleton one time, at start, and makes a singleton: false class on each request.

docs.title: Route model binding
docs.text:
Every @DoxModel class gets a binder. A handler parameter of a model type gets the model, loaded by its primary key:

Route.get('/posts/{post}', (PostController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class PostController {
  Post show(Post post) => post;
}

Dox uses the route param with the name of the model, like {post} for Post or {blogPost} for BlogPost. Else it uses the next route param, like {id}. A missing row gives 404.

A binder from Route.bind wins. See Routing: route model binding.

docs.title: Routers and providers
docs.text:
Dox finds every class that extends Router or DoxProvider, with no @Inject(). It registers the routes and runs setup() of each provider at start, in every isolate. Their constructors also get parameters from the container.

They run in the order of their file path. To pick the order, list them in AppConfig. The others follow:

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  providers: <DoxProvider>[ORMProvider()], // runs first
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter()],          // registered first
);

A provider can add global middleware. See Middleware.

docs.title: Using the container in code
docs.text:
Dox().ioc is the container of the current isolate. Get a class:

UserService users = Dox().ioc.get<UserService>();

get throws when the class is not in the container. Check first with has:

if (Dox().ioc.has<UserService>()) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Adding classes by hand
docs.text:
singleton makes one instance on first use, factory makes a new one on each get, and instance uses the value you give:

Dox().ioc.singleton<Clock>((IocContainer c) => Clock());
Dox().ioc.factory<Report>((IocContainer c) => Report());
Dox().ioc.instance<MailConfig>(mailConfig);

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Put a fake in place of a real class with override, before the app starts. Remove it with clearOverrides:

setUpAll(() async {
  Dox().ioc.override<UserRepository>(FakeUserRepository());
  client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
});

tearDownAll(() async {
  await client.close();
  Dox().ioc.clearOverrides();
});

docs.title: Build errors
docs.text:
The build stops with the file and line when:

  • a required parameter has a type that is not in the container,
  • two or more container classes implement the abstract type of a parameter,
  • classes need each other in a circle, like A -> B -> C -> A,
  • @Inject() is on an abstract class or a generic class,
  • a class has no unnamed constructor.

A private class (like _AdminRouter) is not put in the container, and the build shows a warning. Two classes with the same name can not be handler parameters.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Controller: get services in a controller.
  • Providers: run code when the app starts.

docs.title: DTOs
docs.text:
A DTO is a typed Dart class that describes the input of a request, so your controller gets checked data instead of a raw map.

A DTO (data transfer object) is a class with @Dto(). Each field has a Dart type and some rules. When the input is wrong, the client gets 422, and your method does not run.

docs.title: Creating a DTO
docs.text:
Make a DTO with the CLI. It writes lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart:

dox make:dto CreateUser

Then run the generator. It writes a .dto.g.dart file next to the DTO. dox serve and dox build_runner:watch run it on every save:

dox build_runner:build

docs.title: Defining fields
docs.text:
Each field is a final field and a parameter of the constructor. Put rules on a field as annotations:

lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable, so optional

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

Keep the part line and the schema line. They connect the class to its generated code.

A field that is not nullable and has no default is required. See Required and optional fields.

docs.title: Field types
docs.text:
These field types work:

Dart type JSON Query and form data String, int, double, num, bool the same JSON type text, converted DateTime an ISO 8601 string the same an enum the name, like "admin" the same RequestFile not allowed a file part a @Dto class an object bracket keys: address[city] List<T> an array tags=a&tags=b or tags[]=a Map<String, T> an object bracket keys: meta[color]

JSON is strict: "18" is not an integer. See Types in detail.

docs.title: Numbers as text in JSON
docs.text:
Read numbers and bools that a client sends as text in JSON:

@Dto(coerce: true)
class UpdateStock {
  final int count; // {"count": "18"} gives 18
  final bool active; // {"active": 1} gives true

  const UpdateStock({required this.count, required this.active});
}

docs.title: Nested objects and lists
docs.text:
A field can be another @Dto class, or a list of them:

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}

An error in a nested value has a path key, like items.1.quantity.

docs.title: Input keys
docs.text:
The input key is the field name in snake case, so firstName reads first_name. Use @Name to pick another key:

final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress

@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) uses the field names as they are. Unknown keys are dropped, and @Dto(strict: true) makes them an error. All options are in Keys and DTO options.

docs.title: Registering DTOs
docs.text:
The generator writes the list of all DTOs to lib/generated/dtos.g.dart. Give it to the app config one time. A new app already has this line:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos,
);

docs.title: Using a DTO in a controller
docs.text:
Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs:

@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}

A method can have one DTO parameter, next to others like DoxRequest and path params. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Validating inside the method
docs.text:
Check the input later in the method. It gives the object, or throws the 422 error:

CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();

docs.title: Body and query string
docs.text:
Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body:

Request Dox reads GET, HEAD, DELETE the query string POST, PUT, PATCH the body (JSON, form or multipart)

Set source to pick the source, on the DTO or on one call:

@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call

Path params are not part of a DTO. See the Pagination guide for a full query DTO.

docs.title: Uploaded files
docs.text:
A RequestFile field reads a file from a multipart request. Add file rules to check its type and size:

@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. To save the file, see Request: form data.

docs.title: When validation fails
docs.text:
Dox answers 422 with one message for each field:

{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email"
}

On a form post with a session, Dox redirects back with the errors. To change the messages, see Validation.

docs.title: Converting a DTO
docs.text:
Build a DTO from trusted data with no checks, or turn it into a map with the input keys:

CreateUser user = CreateUser.schema.fromMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'Ann',
  'email': 'ann@dox.dev',
});
Map<String, dynamic> map = CreateUser.schema.toMap(user);

Get the JSON Schema of the DTO:

Map<String, dynamic> json = CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

docs.title: Using a DTO in other places
docs.text:
• OpenAPI docs: each DTO becomes a schema. A /// comment or @Describe('...') on a field becomes its description.
  • MCP tools: extend McpDtoTool<T> to get the checked object.
  • Flutter: import dox_validation in a shared package, and check a form before you send it.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Make a DTO directly to skip the checks:

CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');

Test the checks with safeValidateMap. It never throws:

ParseResult<CreateUser> result =
    await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');

validateMap gives the object or throws. Pass source: Source.query to read the map like a query string, and params: to give path params. @Unique and @Exists need a test database.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Validation: rules, messages and custom checks.
  • Validation rules: every rule and option.
  • Request: raw input and files.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Every error that a route throws goes to one exception handler, which logs it and sends an answer to the client.

The handler has two methods. report(error, stackTrace) logs the error, and render(error, req) decides what the client gets. The default handler works with no setup.

docs.title: The default answer
docs.text:
This is what the client gets with the default handler:

Error Status Body an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException its code {"code": "not_found", "message": "Not Found"} a ValidationException (bad input) 422 the field errors, like {"name": "The name is required"} a ValidationException on a form post with a session 302 a redirect back, with the errors and the old input in the session a URL with no route 404 {"code": "not_found", "message": "GET /x not found"} any other error 500 {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}

For a 500, the client gets the error text only when APP_ENV is development or local. See HTTP exceptions for the exception classes.

report runs for every error, except an IHttpException with a 4xx code. It also runs for errors outside a request, like a future that nobody awaits.

docs.title: An HTML error page
docs.text:
Send browsers an HTML page in place of JSON. A JSON client and a validation error get the same answer as before:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  htmlErrors: true,
);

The page shows the status and its title, like "404 Not Found". In development or local, it also shows the error text and the stack trace.

docs.title: Your own error page
docs.text:
Set errorPage. debug is true when APP_ENV is development or local:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  htmlErrors: true,
  errorPage: (int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug) =>
      '<h1>Sorry, error $status</h1>',
);

Warning

Escape every value you put in the page.

Call defaultErrorPage with the same arguments for the statuses you do not handle.

docs.title: Your own handler
docs.text:
Extend ExceptionHandler, for example to send errors to an error tracker. Override one method or both:

lib/app/exception_handler.dart
class PaymentRequiredException implements Exception {}

class AppExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
  const AppExceptionHandler();

  @override
  void report(Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
    print('ERROR $error\n$stackTrace'); // send it to your error tracker
  }

  @override
  dynamic render(Object error, HttpRequest req) {
    if (error is PaymentRequiredException) {
      return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Please pay'})
          .statusCode(402);
    }
    return super.render(error, req); // the default answer
  }
}

Then set it in AppConfig:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler(),
);

render can return anything a controller can return. Return the error itself for the default answer. req is the raw HttpRequest, so read headers with req.headers.value('accept'). See Custom errors.

docs.title: The request id in a report
docs.text:
Read the id from RequestId at the start of report, before any await:

sentry.captureException(error, hint: ExceptionHandler.requestId);

docs.title: Errors of one route
docs.text:
Send the errors of one route to your own function, for example for gRPC. It also gets the errors of the middleware and of the body:

DoxResponse? rpcError(Object error, DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'error': 'failed'}).statusCode(500);
}

Route.post('/rpc', (RpcController c) => c.call)
    .renderErrorsWith(rpcError);

Return null to get the answer of your ExceptionHandler. The error is still reported. The function must be a top-level or static function, because Dox sends routes to every isolate.

docs.title: Show error text only in development
docs.text:
Decide if the client can see the error text in an answer you send yourself. It is true when APP_ENV is development or local:

String message = showErrors() ? '$error' : 'Server Error';

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• HTTP exceptions: the exception classes and their status codes.
  • Custom errors: your own exceptions and one JSON shape.
  • Error index: every message Dox prints or throws.

docs.title: Inertia
docs.text:
Inertia lets you build a single page app with React, Vue or Svelte, and keep routes and controllers in Dox.

A controller gives a page name and its props, and Inertia shows the page in the browser. The first visit gets a full HTML page. After that, links and forms get only JSON. The dox_inertia package is the server side. Use it with Vite and the Inertia 3 client (@inertiajs/react, @inertiajs/vue3 or @inertiajs/svelte).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add the package with the CLI. It does steps 1 to 3 below, and prints the steps you do yourself:

dox add inertia

docs.title: Set it up by hand
docs.text:
Add the package:

dart pub add dox_inertia

docs.title: 1. Root view
docs.text:
The root view is the HTML page of the first visit. Dox puts the script and style tags in place of @vite, and the page in place of @inertia:

resources/views/app.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>My app</title>
    @vite
  </head>
  <body>
    @inertia
  </body>
</html>

docs.title: 2. Config
docs.text:
Tell Dox where your Vite files are:

lib/config/inertia.dart
import 'package:dox_inertia/dox_inertia.dart';

InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  devServerUrl: 'http://localhost:5173',
  reactRefresh: true,
);
Option Default What it does rootView resources/views/app.html the HTML page of the first visit entryPoints ['resources/js/app.js'] the Vite entry files publicPath public the folder of public files buildDirectory build the folder in publicPath where vite build writes its files devServerUrl null the URL of the Vite dev server. See Vite. reactRefresh false add the React Fast Refresh code in dev mode version hash of the manifest the asset version. See Asset version. encryptHistory false encrypt the browser history of every page. See History encryption. ssr null server side rendering. See SSR.

Paths are from the project root.

docs.title: 3. Provider
docs.text:
The provider sets up Inertia in every isolate. Put it in lib/:

lib/providers/inertia_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_inertia/dox_inertia.dart';

import '../config/inertia.dart';

class AppInertiaProvider extends InertiaProvider {
  AppInertiaProvider() : super(inertiaConfig);
}

With no provider, Dox uses the defaults. Inertia.configure(config) sets the config with no provider, and Inertia.config reads it.

docs.title: 4. Vite
docs.text:
Set up Vite so it writes a manifest into public/build:

vite.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  plugins: [react()],
  // public/ holds the Dox public files, so Vite must not copy it
  publicDir: false,
  base: command === 'build' ? '/build/' : '/',
  server: { origin: 'http://localhost:5173' },
  build: {
    manifest: true,
    outDir: 'public/build',
    rollupOptions: { input: 'resources/js/app.jsx' },
  },
}))

Then start the Inertia app in your entry file:

resources/js/app.jsx
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

createInertiaApp({
  resolve: (name) => {
    const pages = import.meta.glob('./Pages/**/*.jsx', { eager: true })
    return pages[`./Pages/${name}.jsx`]
  },
  setup({ el, App, props }) {
    createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />)
  },
})

docs.title: 5. Serve the built files
docs.text:
In production the browser loads /build/assets/.... Add a route for them, or let your proxy serve public/build:

lib/routes/web.dart
Route.get('/build/{path*}', (String path) {
  if (path.contains('..')) throw NotFoundHttpException();
  // the file names have a hash, so the browser can keep them for a year
  return response(File('public/build/$path'))
      .cache(const Duration(days: 365));
});

docs.title: 6. Middleware
docs.text:
Add three middleware to globalMiddleware, in this order:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(),
    HandleInertiaRequests(),
  ],
);
  • SessionMiddleware keeps the validation errors and the flash data. See Session.
  • CsrfMiddleware sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, and the Inertia client sends it back. See CSRF.
  • HandleInertiaRequests is your InertiaMiddleware. See Shared props. With no props to share, use const InertiaMiddleware().

You can also add them to a router, in the same order.

docs.title: Rendering pages
docs.text:
Give the request, the page name and the props. The page name is the file in resources/js/Pages, with no extension:

lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<DoxResponse> index(DoxRequest req) {
    return inertia(req, 'Users/Index', <String, dynamic>{
      'title': 'Users',
      'users': () => User().query().all(),
    });
  }
}

A function prop, like users, runs only when the prop is sent. It can give a Future. Props become JSON, so a model works. Inertia.render(req, ...) is the same as inertia(req, ...).

A Dart integer above 2^53 loses precision in JavaScript, so send such a number as a string.

docs.title: Is it an Inertia request
docs.text:
Check if the request came from the Inertia client:

if (Inertia.isInertia(req)) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Shared props
docs.text:
Share props with every page, like the signed in user. Extend InertiaMiddleware and return them from share. It can be async:

lib/app/http/middleware/handle_inertia_requests.dart
class HandleInertiaRequests extends InertiaMiddleware {
  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> share(DoxRequest req) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'appName': 'My app',
      'auth': () => req.auth?.toJson(),
    };
  }
}

A page prop with the same name wins. Share from any middleware or controller with Inertia.share(req, {...}), and read all shared props with Inertia.shared(req).

docs.title: Global values
docs.text:
Share one value with the full app. Call it in the setup() of your provider:

@override
void setup() {
  super.setup();
  Inertia.shareGlobal('appName', 'Dox');
}

Warning

All users get a global value. Put data of one user, like the signed in user, in share.

docs.title: Partial reloads
docs.text:
The client can ask for some props only, with router.reload({ only: ['users'] }). Dox then sends only those props. Ask for a top level prop, like auth, not auth.user.

These helpers change when a prop is sent:

Helper First visit Partial reload plain value or function sent sent when asked Inertia.optional not sent sent when asked Inertia.always sent always sent Inertia.defer not sent, loaded right after sent when asked Inertia.merge sent sent when asked

docs.title: Optional props
docs.text:
Send the prop only when a partial reload asks for it. Inertia.lazy is the same:

'stats': Inertia.optional(() => Stats.load()),

docs.title: Always props
docs.text:
Send the prop on every request:

'notices': Inertia.always(notices),

docs.title: Deferred props
docs.text:
Leave a slow prop out of the first visit. The page loads it right after. Props of the same group load in one request:

'comments': Inertia.defer(() => Comment().query().all()),
'likes': Inertia.defer(() => Like().query().count(), group: 'side'),

docs.title: Merging props
docs.text:
Add the new items to the old ones, for infinite scroll:

'posts': Inertia.merge(posts),
'feed': Inertia.defer(() => Post().query().all()).merge(),

docs.title: Forms and validation errors
docs.text:
A form post needs no extra code for errors. When validation fails, Dox flashes the errors and redirects back. The page gets them in the errors prop:

Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
  await req.validateSchema(
    v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
      'name': v.string().min(2),
      'email': v.string().email(),
    }),
  );
  // ... save the user
  return redirect('/users');
}

const { data, setData, post, errors } = useForm({ name: '', email: '' })
// errors.email holds the message, or is undefined

docs.title: Error bags
docs.text:
Keep the errors of two forms on one page apart. Pass errorBag in the post, and the errors are under the bag name, like errors.login.email:

router.post(url, data, { errorBag: 'login' })

docs.title: Redirects
docs.text:
Redirect with redirect(url) or back(req). After PUT, PATCH or DELETE, InertiaMiddleware changes a 302 into 303, so the browser follows with GET:

return redirect('/users');

A controller that returns nothing to an Inertia request sends the browser back, like back(req).

docs.title: External redirects
docs.text:
Go to an outside site, or a page that is not an Inertia page, with a full page load:

return Inertia.location(req, 'https://checkout.example.com/pay/1');

docs.title: Flash data
docs.text:
Give the next page a short message, like "User saved". It needs SessionMiddleware:

Inertia.flash(req, 'message', 'User saved');
return redirect('/users');

The next page gets it in page.flash, one time:

const { flash } = usePage()
// flash.message is 'User saved'

docs.title: Vite
docs.text:
In dev mode, @vite loads the entry files from the Vite dev server, with hot reload. In production, Dox reads public/build/.vite/manifest.json.

Dox is in dev mode when devServerUrl is set, or when public/hot exists. So set devServerUrl from the env:

lib/config/inertia.dart
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  devServerUrl: Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'development'
      ? 'http://localhost:5173'
      : null,
);

When APP_ENV is production, Dox ignores public/hot and prints a warning.

docs.title: Asset version
docs.text:
When the asset version changes, the next link click loads the full page again, with the new files. The default is a hash of the Vite manifest, read one time for each isolate. So restart the server after vite build.

Set your own version, for example the git commit:

InertiaConfig(version: Env.get<String>('GIT_SHA'));

Inertia.version gives the current version.

docs.title: Root view data
docs.text:
Give the root view a value, like the title. Write {{ key }} in the root view:

<head>
  <meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ csrfToken }}">
  <title>{{ title }}</title>
  @vite
</head>

Set the values in a controller or a middleware. More calls merge the data:

Inertia.withViewData(req, <String, Object?>{'title': 'Users'});
return inertia(req, 'Users/Index');
  • Dox fills {{ csrfToken }} with the CSRF token of the session.
  • A key that you did not set stays as it is, so set every key of the root view.
  • Each value is HTML escaped. Put it only in text or in a quoted attribute.
  • Later visits do not load the root view again. So set the title in the <Head> component of the client too.

docs.title: Another root view for some pages
docs.text:
Use another HTML file for one request, like an admin area:

Inertia.setRootView(req, 'resources/views/admin.html');
return inertia(req, 'Admin/Dashboard');

For every page of a router, use RootViewMiddleware:

@override
List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[
  const RootViewMiddleware('resources/views/admin.html'),
];

Warning

Use a fixed path. A path from the request could show any file of the server.

docs.title: History encryption
docs.text:
The browser keeps the props of each page in its history. After a logout, the back button can show private data. With history encryption, the browser encrypts the page data, and a cleared history can not be read. It works only on HTTPS and on localhost.

Turn it on for all pages:

lib/config/inertia.dart
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(encryptHistory: true);

Or for one page. Pass false to turn it off for one page:

Inertia.encryptHistory(req);
return inertia(req, 'Account/Show', props);

Or for all pages of a router:

@override
List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[const EncryptHistoryMiddleware()];

Clear the history, for example at logout. It needs SessionMiddleware:

Inertia.clearHistory(req);
return redirect('/login');

docs.title: Server side rendering (SSR)
docs.text: With SSR, the first visit gets the full HTML of the page, so search engines can read it. The Inertia SSR server renders it. It is a Bun or Node process next to your Dox app. Links and forms never use it.

docs.title: 1. The SSR entry file
docs.text:
dox inertia:install --ssr writes the entry file and adds a build:ssr script to package.json:

package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build:ssr": "vite build && vite build --ssr resources/js/ssr.jsx --outDir bootstrap/ssr"
  }
}

The entry file looks like this:

resources/js/ssr.jsx
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'
import createServer from '@inertiajs/react/server'
import ReactDOMServer from 'react-dom/server'

createServer(
  (page) =>
    createInertiaApp({
      page,
      render: ReactDOMServer.renderToString,
      resolve: (name) => {
        const pages = import.meta.glob('./Pages/**/*.jsx', { eager: true })
        return pages[`./Pages/${name}.jsx`]
      },
      setup: ({ App, props }) => <App {...props} />,
    }),
  { host: '127.0.0.1' },
)

Vue and Svelte have the same createServer, in @inertiajs/vue3/server and @inertiajs/svelte/server. Keep host at 127.0.0.1, so only your own machine can reach the server.

docs.title: 2. Hydrate in the browser
docs.text:
Reuse the HTML from the server. Change setup in your app file:

resources/js/app.jsx
setup({ el, App, props }) {
  if (el.hasAttribute('data-server-rendered')) {
    hydrateRoot(el, <App {...props} />)
  } else {
    createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />)
  }
},

docs.title: 3. Build and run
docs.text:
Build the files, then start the SSR server with Bun. Add --node for Node:

bun run build:ssr
dox inertia:start-ssr

It runs bootstrap/ssr/ssr.js (or ssr.mjs) in the foreground. Run it under Docker, pm2 or systemd, and keep node_modules on the server.

docs.title: 4. Turn it on
docs.text:
Set ssr in the config:

lib/config/inertia.dart
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  ssr: Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'production' ? InertiaSsr() : null,
);
Option Default What it does url http://127.0.0.1:13714/render the render URL of the SSR server timeout 2 seconds how long Dox waits for the answer

The head tags of the page go before </head>. So when your pages set a title with <Head>, remove the title from the root view.

When the SSR server is down or slow, the visitor gets the normal page, and Dox prints one warning.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Views: server templates with no front-end framework.
  • Session: errors and flash data.
  • Static files and SPA: serve the built front-end files.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text: Middleware is code that runs before the controller, and if you want, after it too.

docs.title: Making a middleware
docs.text:
Make a middleware with the CLI:

dox make:middleware Logger

It writes lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart. Write your code in handle:

lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on to the next middleware
  }
}

handle can be async. Return the request to go on. Return any other value to send it as the response, or throw an exception to send an error. Then the controller does not run.

Warning

Do not forget return req. A middleware that returns null ends the request with an empty 200.

docs.title: Function middleware
docs.text:
A function that takes a DoxRequest also works as middleware:

lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart
dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
  String given = req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '';
  if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(given, apiKey)) {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'})
        .statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}

Compare secrets with Hash.equals, not ==, so the time does not tell an attacker how much of the key was right.

docs.title: On a route
docs.text:
Put the middleware in a list before the controller. They run from left to right:

Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  (WebController c) => c.pong, // the controller is always last
]);

docs.title: On a group of routes
docs.text:
Run a middleware for many routes:

Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
  Route.post('/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
});

docs.title: On a router
docs.text:
Run a middleware for all routes of one router:

lib/routes/api.dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}

docs.title: Global middleware
docs.text:
Run a middleware for all routes:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
);

docs.title: Global middleware from a package
docs.text:
A package adds a global middleware in the setup() of its provider. It runs before the global middleware of the app:

class AuditProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    Dox().addGlobalMiddleware(AuditMiddleware());
  }
}

A second add of the same middleware is skipped, so use a top-level function or a const instance.

docs.title: Skip a middleware on one route
docs.text:
Take every middleware of a type out of one route, also a global one:

Route.post('/events', (EventController c) => c.stream)
    .withoutMiddleware<RequestTimeout>();

It also takes out the subtypes of the type, so use a specific type.

docs.title: The order
docs.text:
Middleware runs in this order. If one returns a value or throws, the rest do not run:

  1. Packagefrom a provider
  2. Globalall routes
  3. Routerone router
  4. Groupa route group
  5. Routeone route
  6. Controllerhandles the request

docs.title: Run code after the controller
docs.text:
Implement IDoxNextMiddleware to change the response. await next() runs the rest of the middleware and the controller:

lib/app/http/middleware/see_other.middleware.dart
class SeeOtherMiddleware implements IDoxNextMiddleware {
  @override
  Future<DoxResponse> handle(DoxRequest req, Next next) async {
    DoxResponse res = await next();
    if (res.status == 302 && req.httpRequest.method != 'GET') {
      res.statusCode(303);
    }
    return res;
  }
}

If the controller throws, next() gives the error response from the ExceptionHandler, so the code after it always runs.

A function works too:

Future<DoxResponse> timerMiddleware(DoxRequest req, Next next) async {
  Stopwatch watch = Stopwatch()..start();
  DoxResponse res = await next();
  return res.header('X-Time', '${watch.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
}

docs.title: Run code after the answer is sent
docs.text:
Implement IDoxTerminableMiddleware for work that must not make the client wait, like logs or metrics:

lib/app/http/middleware/metrics.middleware.dart
class MetricsMiddleware
    implements IDoxMiddleware, IDoxTerminableMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) => req;

  @override
  void terminate(DoxRequest req, DoxResponse res) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path} ${res.status}');
  }
}

An error in terminate goes to ExceptionHandler.report. It never changes the answer.

docs.title: From any code
docs.text:
AfterResponse adds work after the answer from a controller, a service or a package. Turn it on in the setup() of a provider:

lib/providers/app_provider.dart
@override
void setup() {
  AfterResponse.enable();
}

Then add work anywhere in the request. The work runs in the order you add it:

AfterResponse.run(() => mailer.sendWelcome(user));

Work that did not run yet is lost when the server stops. For work that must run, use a queue.

AfterResponse.disable() turns it off again, for tests. AfterResponse.enabled tells if it is on.

docs.title: Request id
docs.text:
RequestId gives each request an id. It is sent in the X-Request-Id header, and you read it as req.requestId:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const RequestId(),
    LogMiddleware(),
  ],
);

Put it before LogMiddleware, so each log line gets the id. Dox keeps a safe id from the client. RequestId(trustClient: false) always makes a new one.

To make an id yourself, call RequestId.make(). It gives 32 hex characters.

docs.title: ETag and 304 Not Modified
docs.text:
ETag answers 304 with no body when the client already has the same data:

Route.get('/posts',
    <dynamic>[const ETag(), (PostController c) => c.index]);

It works on 200 answers with a body in memory. The controller still runs, so it saves bandwidth, not server time.

To make a weak ETag yourself, use ETag.of(bytes). ETag.matches(ifNoneMatch, tag) tells if the header of the client has the tag.

docs.title: Request timeout
docs.text:
Answer 503 when the route takes too long:

Route.get('/report', (ReportController c) => c.show)
    .timeout(Duration(seconds: 30));

For every route, add the RequestTimeout middleware to globalMiddleware:

RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30))

Dart can not stop a running Future, so the controller keeps running and its late result is dropped. A global timeout also ends long streams. See Skip a middleware on one route.

docs.title: Server timing
docs.text:
ServerTiming adds a Server-Timing header. The browser dev tools show it in the Network tab:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    if (Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'development') const ServerTiming(),
  ],
);

Development or trusted clients only

The header tells every client how long your code takes. An attacker can use it, for example to guess if an email has an account.

It sends the time in the controller as handler and the full time as total. Add your own time to the current request:

ServerTiming.add('db', Duration(milliseconds: 4));

Run a function and add the time it took:

String html = await ServerTiming.measure('render', () => view.render());

The header then looks like this. A name you add again adds up, with a count:

Server-Timing: db;dur=4.10;desc="3 calls", handler;dur=12.34, total;dur=13.02

docs.title: Timing database queries
docs.text:
Add the time of every query in the setup() of a provider:

lib/providers/query_timing_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

void onQuery(QueryEvent event) {
  ServerTiming.add('db', event.time);
}

class QueryTimingProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    SqlQueryBuilder().listen(onQuery);
  }
}

See Listen to queries.

docs.title: Log requests
docs.text:
LogMiddleware logs one line for each request. It follows the logger config. These are its options:

Option What it does enabled false turns the request logs off. Not set: follow the logger. withHeader true also logs the headers. redact Fields and headers whose name has one of these words are logged as [REDACTED]. Default: LogMiddleware.defaultRedact (password, secret, token, cookie and more). filter A function that changes the line before it is logged. 
LogMiddleware(withHeader: true, redact: <String>['password', 'pin'])

docs.title: More middleware
docs.text:
Other pages have more middleware:

  • AuthMiddleware and GuestMiddleware check the login. See Authentication.
  • RateLimit answers 429 for too many requests. See Rate limiting.
  • SecurityHeaders adds safe headers. See Security headers.
  • SessionMiddleware gives each request a session. See Session.
  • CsrfMiddleware stops cross site request forgery. See CSRF protection.
  • ValidateSignature checks signed URLs. See Signed URLs.
  • MethodOverride lets HTML forms send PUT, PATCH and DELETE. See Routing.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Routing: add middleware to routes and groups.
  • Rate limiting: limit the requests of a client.
  • CORS: let other origins call your API.

docs.title: Request
docs.text: The request gives you the input, files, headers and cookies that the client sent.

docs.title: Typed input
docs.text:
Ask for a DTO in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET, HEAD and DELETE), checks it, and gives you a typed object:

Route.put('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User?> update(int id, UpdateUser input) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See Validation.

docs.title: Checking in the controller
docs.text:
To check the input at a later point, call validate with the DTO type:

CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();

For input you know only at runtime, use a fluent schema. See Fluent schemas:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(
    <String, Schema<Object?>>{'email': v.string().email()}));

docs.title: Raw input
docs.text: Add a DoxRequest parameter to read the raw values. Dox does not check these values.

docs.title: Retrieving an input value
docs.text:
Read one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key:

String? name = req.input('name');
String name = req.input('name', 'guest'); // default for a missing key

Use a dot key to read inside a map or a list:

req.input('user.name');
req.input('items.0.id'); // the id of the first item

A key that is in the input as it is, like 'a.b', wins over a dot key.

docs.title: Retrieving all input
docs.text:
Get all values of the query string and the body:

Map<String, dynamic> data = req.all();

Get only the body or only the query string:

req.body;  // JSON or form data
req.query; // the query string

docs.title: Retrieving a part of the input
docs.text:
Get some keys, or all keys but some:

req.only(<String>['name', 'email']);
req.except(<String>['password']);

docs.title: Checking if a value exists
docs.text:
filled gives true when the key is there and not empty. Only spaces, an empty list and an empty map count as empty:

if (req.filled('name')) {
  // ...
}

exists gives true for a key with any value, also an empty string or null. missing is the opposite:

req.exists('name');
req.missing('name');

has gives true when the key is there and not empty. It does not read dot keys.

docs.title: Reading booleans and numbers
docs.text:
boolean gives true for true, 1, on and yes, so it works for checkboxes:

bool remember = req.boolean('remember');

integer gives the default when the key is missing or not a number:

int page = req.integer('page', 1);

docs.title: Adding input
docs.text:
Add one value, or a map of values, for example in a middleware:

req.add('key', value);
req.merge(<String, dynamic>{'key': value});

docs.title: Lists and maps in forms
docs.text:
Form and query keys with brackets give lists and maps:

Input req.input(...) gives tags[]=a&tags[]=b req.input('tags') is ['a', 'b'] address[city]=Yangon req.input('address') is {'city': 'Yangon'} items[0][name]=x req.input('items') is [{'name': 'x'}] name=a&name=b (no brackets) req.input('name') is 'b', the last value

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
Ask for a path param as a typed parameter, like int id above. See Controller: parameters.

The URL-decoded text values are also in req.param:

String? id = req.param['id'];
Map<String, String> params = req.pathParams; // {'id': '5'}

A value from route model binding comes from bound:

User user = req.bound<User>('user');

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. The request must be multipart/form-data. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

lib/app/dtos/upload_image/upload_image.dto.dart
@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}

Then store it. store comes from the dox_storage package:

Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
  String path = await input.image.store('images');
  return <String, String>{'filename': path};
}

Save the file before you return

Dox deletes the temp file of a big upload when the response is sent. Call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Files without a DTO
docs.text:
Get a file, or null when the field is not a file. Dox does not check it:

RequestFile? image = req.file('image');

hasFile gives true when the field holds a file or a list of files. For a field with many files, use req.input('images'):

if (req.hasFile('image')) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Reading and saving a file
docs.text:
A RequestFile tells you about the file:

file.filename;  // name from the client
file.filetype;  // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension; // mp4
file.length;    // size in bytes
await file.size; // size in KB
file.head;      // the first bytes, to find the real file type

Save it to storage, or move it:

await file.store('videos');              // gives the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // gives the new File

Read it in chunks with stream. bytes loads the full file in memory, so do not use it for big files:

file.stream();
await file.bytes;

file.file is the temp file on disk, or null when the upload is in memory. An upload up to 1 MB stays in memory.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413. Change the limits in AppConfig:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,       // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024, // uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
Read one header, or all of them. A repeated header is joined with ', ':

String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers;

There are short methods for common headers:

req.userAgent();   // User-Agent header
req.host();        // Host header
req.origin();      // Origin header, or null
req.referer();     // Referer header, or null
req.locale;        // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null
req.bearerToken(); // the token of 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', or null

docs.title: Body type
docs.text:
Check the body type, or if the client wants a JSON answer:

req.isJson();      // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData();  // true for multipart/form-data
req.expectsJson(); // true for a JSON Accept header, JSON body or XHR

docs.title: Method, path and URL
docs.text:
Read the method and the URL of the request:

req.method;          // 'GET'
req.path();          // '/admin/users/5'
req.fullUrl();       // 'https://example.com/admin/users/5?tab=info'
req.uri;             // the Uri
req.protocolVersion; // '1.1', or '2.0' for HTTP/2

Check where the request goes. * matches any text, and a route with no name never matches routeIs:

req.pathIs('admin/*');        // a path pattern
req.routeIs('admin.users.*'); // a route name

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
Read a cookie. Dox encrypts cookies by default, so you get the decrypted value:

String? token = req.cookie('token');
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false); // value as sent

See Response to set a cookie.

docs.title: Client IP and scheme
docs.text:
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https

Behind a proxy, set trustedProxies in AppConfig, or req.ip() gives the proxy. See Deployment.

docs.title: Other request data
docs.text:
These come from middleware:

req.requestId; // from RequestId, see Middleware
req.session;   // from SessionMiddleware, see Session
req.hasSession; // true when the route has a session
req.auth;      // the logged in user, see Authentication

See Middleware, Session and Authentication.

docs.title: Send the response yourself
docs.text:
Write the response on req.httpRequest.response. After takeOverResponse, Dox sends nothing more for the request:

Future<void> handle(DoxRequest req) async {
  req.takeOverResponse();
  HttpResponse res = req.httpRequest.response;
  res.write('done');
  await res.close();
}

Your code must close the response. req.responseTakenOver gives true after the call.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• DTO: typed and checked input.
  • Validation: the rules for input.
  • Response: send an answer.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: A controller returns a value, and Dox turns it into the response for the client.

docs.title: Return a value
docs.text:
Return the value from your controller. Dox sends a string as text, and a map or a model as JSON:

Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

This is what the client gets for each type:

You return The client gets a String the text a Map or a List JSON a model, a list of models, a serializer JSON (from toJson()) a DateTime the ISO 8601 text an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException() its status code and JSON: {"code": ..., "message": ...} a File (from dart:io) the file, streamed a Stream<List<int>> the bytes, streamed a StreamFile or a DownloadableFile the file, streamed response(...) full control: status, headers, cookies

The htmlStrings flag sends a string as HTML. See Core flags.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Throw or return an exception to answer with an error:

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

The client gets 404 with {"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}. Each exception takes message: and errorCode:. A map message is sent as it is.

Exception Status BadRequestException() 400 ForbiddenHttpException() 403 NotFoundHttpException() 404 MethodNotAllowedHttpException(allow) 405 PayloadTooLargeException() 413 UnsupportedMediaTypeException() 415 TokenMismatchException() 419 ValidationException() 422 TooManyRequestsException() 429 InternalErrorException() 500 QueryException() 500

See HTTP exceptions for all of them.

docs.title: Any status
docs.text:
Stop the request with any status, an optional message and headers:

if (post.userId != req.auth?.id()) abort(403);
throw HttpStatusException(503,
    headers: <String, String>{'retry-after': '60'});

docs.title: Your own exception
docs.text:
Extend IHttpException:

class PaymentRequiredException extends IHttpException {
  PaymentRequiredException({String message = 'Payment required'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.paymentRequired;
    super.errorCode = 'payment_required';
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Any other error gets 500, and goes to the exception handler.

docs.title: Files and big responses
docs.text:
Return a File or a Stream<List<int>> to send a file. Dox sends it in chunks:

Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

A file gets the right Content-Type and Content-Length. It also answers Range requests with 206, so video players can seek and downloads can resume.

docs.title: A stream with a type
docs.text:
Send a stream with its content type, or as a download with a file name:

return StreamFile(ContentType.parse('image/png'), bytes, length: size);
return DownloadableFile(ContentType.binary, bytes, 'report.pdf');

docs.title: Files from storage
docs.text:
Make the browser save a file from File Storage:

Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}

Show the file in the browser:

Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}

docs.title: The response() helper
docs.text:
Set the status, headers or cookies. All methods return the response, so you can chain them:

DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}

docs.title: Setting the status
docs.text:
Set the status code. The default is 200:

response(data).statusCode(201);

docs.title: Setting headers
docs.text:
Set one header. If a middleware already set it, the new value is added. Pass replace: true to replace it:

response(data).header('X-Key', 'value');
response(data).header('X-Key', 'value', replace: true);

The replaceHeaders flag makes header replace by default. See Core flags.

Set many headers. Each key replaces the header with the same name:

response(data).withHeaders(<String, String>{'X-One': '1', 'X-Two': '2'});

Set the content type. ContentType is from dart:io:

response(html).contentType(ContentType.html);

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Set Cache-Control. Duration(minutes: 5) sends max-age=300:

response(data).cache(Duration(minutes: 5));

docs.title: Changing the body
docs.text:
Change the body, or send a byte stream as the body:

response('').content(value);
response('').stream(byteStream);

docs.title: Reading the response
docs.text:
Read the body, the status and the headers, for example in a middleware. A null status means 200:

res.getContent();
res.status;
res.headers;

docs.title: Redirect
docs.text:
Send the browser to another page. The status is 302 by default:

return redirect('/login');
return redirect('/posts', status: 301);

Send the browser back to the page of the Referer header, for example after a form post. With no Referer, or one of another host, it goes to the fallback:

return back(req);
return back(req, fallback: '/home');

See Session for flash messages with a redirect.

docs.title: Cookie
docs.text:
Make a DoxCookie and add it to the response:

DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);

Set the cookie options:

DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true, // default true: page scripts can not read it
  secure: true,   // default: only when the request came over https
  path: '/',
  sameSite: SameSite.lax, // from dart:io. default: none sent
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);

Delete a cookie:

return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);

Dox encrypts the cookie value with APP_KEY. If the browser or another app must read it, use DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false), and read it with req.cookie(key, decrypt: false). See Request: cookies.

To decrypt a raw cookie value with no request, use DoxCookie.decrypt(name, value).

docs.title: Send the response yourself
docs.text: Write the raw response, for example a stream with trailers. See Request: send the response yourself.

docs.title: Change every response
docs.text:
Change every response in one place, for example to add a header. Set a responseHandler in AppConfig:

lib/app/http/handler.dart
class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
);

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Serializer: set the JSON shape of a response.
  • Error handling: report and render errors.
  • Request: read the input.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
A route connects a URL and an HTTP method to the code that answers it.

The router finds the route of a request by its method, host and path. Then it calls the handler of the route: a function or a controller method.

docs.title: Where routes live
docs.text:
Routes are in the lib/routes folder. Each file has one router class:

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong'); // GET /api/ping
  }
}

The prefix goes in front of every route of the router. Run dart run build_runner build, and Dox finds the router by itself. To set the order of the routers, see Dependency injection.

To see every route of your app, run dox route:list. See the CLI reference.

docs.title: Route methods
docs.text:
There is one method for each HTTP verb:

Route.get('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
Route.post('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);
Route.put('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.patch('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.delete('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.destroy);

A HEAD request runs the GET route of the same path. There are also methods for the less common verbs: Route.options, Route.copy, Route.link, Route.unlink, Route.purge, Route.lock, Route.unlock, Route.propfind and Route.view.

docs.title: More than one method
docs.text:
Answer a list of methods with one handler:

Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact',
    (ContactController c) => c.handle);

Answer GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE:

Route.any('/webhook', (WebhookController c) => c.handle);

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
The handler can be a function:

Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');

Or a controller method:

Route.get('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);

@Inject()
class WebController {
  String pong(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Or a list, with middleware before the controller:

Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  (WebController c) => c.pong,
]);

docs.title: Health check route
docs.text:
Add a route for your load balancer or uptime check:

Route.health('/health');

Add checks and a timeout:

Route.health(
  '/health',
  timeout: Duration(seconds: 2),
  checks: <String, HealthCheckFunction>{
    'database': () => QueryBuilder.query('select 1'),
    'cache': HealthCheck.cache(),
  },
);

A failed check answers 503. See Health check.

docs.title: Redirect routes
docs.text:
Send an old path to a new URL. The status is 302 by default:

Route.redirect('/home', '/');
Route.redirect('/old-blog', '/blog', status: 301);

Or send a 301:

Route.permanentRedirect('/old-pricing', '/pricing'); // 301

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
A route param is a name in braces in the path. Ask for it as a typed parameter:

Route.get('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}

A request to /blogs/abc gets a 404, because the text is not an integer. See Controller.

docs.title: Param in a part with text
docs.text:
Mix text and params in one part of the path:

Route.get('/v{version}/users/{id}', (DoxRequest req) {
  return req.param['version']; // GET /v2/users/5 gives '2'
});

Route.get('/files/{name}-{size}', (DoxRequest req) {
  return req.param['size']; // GET /files/logo-small gives 'small'
});

docs.title: Optional param
docs.text:
Add ? to a param that can be missing:

Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) {
  return 'page ${page ?? 1}'; // GET /posts and GET /posts/2 both match
});

docs.title: Catch-all param
docs.text:
Add * to match the rest of the path, with slashes:

Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) {
  return page; // GET /docs/a/b/c gives 'a/b/c'
});

docs.title: Param rules
docs.text:
Match only some values with where and a regex. When it does not match, the router tries the next route:

Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show)
    .where('id', '[0-9]+');
Route.get('/users/{name}', (UserController c) => c.byName); // gets the rest

The regex must match the whole param. For a group, use (?:...).

docs.title: Group routes
docs.text: A group gives many routes the same prefix, domain or middleware.

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
Add a path in front of every route:

Route.group('/blogs', () {
  Route.get('/', (BlogController c) => c.index); // GET /blogs
  Route.get('/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.show); // GET /blogs/{id}
});

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
Match only requests for one host:

Route.domain('dartondox.com', () {
  Route.get('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);
});

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
Run the same middleware for every route:

Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
  Route.post('/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
});

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
Turn the CORS headers on or off for some routes:

Route.enabledCors(() {
  Route.get('/public/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
});

Route.disabledCors(() {
  Route.post('/webhooks/stripe', (WebhookController c) => c.handle);
});

See CORS.

docs.title: Route options
docs.text: Add these after a route. They change only that route.

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text:
Answer 503 when the route takes too long:

Route.get('/report', (ReportController c) => c.show)
    .timeout(Duration(seconds: 30));

See Request timeout.

docs.title: Skip a middleware
docs.text:
Take one middleware out of the route, also a global one:

Route.post('/events', (EventController c) => c.stream)
    .withoutMiddleware<RequestTimeout>();

See Middleware.

docs.title: Errors of one route
docs.text:
Send the errors of the route to your own function:

DoxResponse? rpcError(Object error, DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'error': 'failed'}).statusCode(500);
}

Route.post('/rpc', (RpcController c) => c.call)
    .renderErrorsWith(rpcError);

See Error handling.

docs.title: Name and param rules
docs.text: The other options are name and where. See Named routes and Param rules.

docs.title: Resource routes
docs.text:
A resource route makes the routes to list, show, create, change and delete, in one line:

Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);

These are the routes it makes:

Method Path Controller method Route name GET /blogs index blogs.index GET /blogs/create create blogs.create POST /blogs store blogs.store GET /blogs/{id} show blogs.show GET /blogs/{id}/edit edit blogs.edit PUT, PATCH /blogs/{id} update blogs.update DELETE /blogs/{id} destroy blogs.destroy

A method that the controller does not have gets no route. To make the controller, see Resource controllers.

Pass name to change the first part of the route names:

Route.resource('blogs', BlogController, name: 'posts'); // posts.index, ...

docs.title: Naming the param
docs.text:
Pass parameter to change {id} to another name:

Route.resource('photos', PhotoController, parameter: 'photo');
// GET /photos/{photo}, PUT /photos/{photo}, ...

docs.title: Forms with PUT, PATCH and DELETE
docs.text:
An HTML form can only send GET or POST. Add MethodOverride to the global middleware:

AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()],
);

Then send the form as POST with a _method field:

<form method="POST" action="/blogs/5">
  <input type="hidden" name="_method" value="DELETE">
</form>

For a client that sends the X-HTTP-Method-Override header, turn it on with header: true:

AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride(header: true)],
);

docs.title: Named routes
docs.text:
A named route lets you build URLs from a name, so the path lives in one place:

Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show).name('users.show');

docs.title: Generating URLs
docs.text:
Build the path with route(). Route.url() does the same:

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5});
// /users/5

Add a query string with query:

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5},
    query: <String, Object>{'tab': 'posts'});
// /users/5?tab=posts

docs.title: Full URL
docs.text:
Pass absolute: true to put APP_URL in front:

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5}, absolute: true);
// https://example.com/users/5   (APP_URL=https://example.com)

Or pass your own baseUrl:

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5},
    absolute: true, baseUrl: 'https://admin.example.com');
// https://admin.example.com/users/5

docs.title: Name prefix in a group
docs.text:
Put a prefix in front of the names in a group:

Route.group('admin', () {
  Route.get('users', (UserController c) => c.index)
      .name('users'); // admin.users
}, name: 'admin.');

docs.title: Signed routes
docs.text:
A signed URL is a link that nobody can change, like an unsubscribe link in an email. Protect the route with ValidateSignature, and make the URL with Route.signedUrl:

Route.get('/unsubscribe/{user}', <dynamic>[
  const ValidateSignature(),
  (UserController c) => c.unsubscribe,
]).name('unsubscribe');

Route.signedUrl('unsubscribe',
    params: <String, Object>{'user': 5}, expires: Duration(days: 7));
// https://example.com/unsubscribe/5?expires=...&signature=...

A changed or expired URL gets 403. See Signed URLs.

docs.title: Route model binding
docs.text:
A binder turns a route param into a model before the controller runs. Add it before the routes that use it:

Route.bind<User>('user', (String id) => User().find(id));

Route.get('/users/{user}', (DoxRequest req, User user) {
  return user;
});

When the binder returns null, the client gets a 404. Other params still work next to it:

Route.get('/users/{user}/posts/{page}', (User user, int page) {
  return user.posts(page);
});

You can also read the model with req.bound<User>('user'). A model class needs no Route.bind. See Dependency injection.

docs.title: Serve static files
docs.text:
Serve the files of a folder, like CSS, JavaScript and images:

Route.staticFiles('/', 'public');

Let the browser keep files that never change, with maxAge:

Route.staticFiles('build', 'public/build', maxAge: Duration(days: 365));

No middleware runs for a file, so a login check does not protect this folder.

Warning

Never save user uploads in this folder. An uploaded html or svg file would run its script on your site. Use File Storage for uploads. It sends such files as downloads.

docs.title: Fallback route
docs.text:
A fallback answers a GET or HEAD request that matches no route and no static file:

lib/routes/web.dart
class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/', (WebController c) => c.home);

    Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) {
      return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Page not found'})
          .statusCode(404);
    });
  }
}

Set the status yourself. Without statusCode(404), the client gets 200.

docs.title: Fallback for other methods
docs.text:
Give when a check to answer other methods too, for example for gRPC clients:

bool isGrpc(HttpRequest req) {
  String type = req.headers.value('content-type') ?? '';
  return req.method == 'POST' && type.startsWith('application/grpc');
}

Route.fallback(grpcNotFound, when: isGrpc);

The check must be a top-level or static function.

docs.title: Serve storage files
docs.text:
Serve the files of a storage disk. By default only signed URLs work:

Storage.route('files');
Storage.route('public', disk: 'local', signed: false);

For user uploads, send every file as a download:

Storage.route('uploads', download: true);

See File Storage.

docs.title: WebSocket routes
docs.text:
Add a raw WebSocket route:

Route.websocket('chat', handler, maxMessageSize: 64 * 1024);

Warning

By default any website can open the socket from a browser, with the cookies of the user. Pass allowedOrigins to the route, or set webSocketAllowedOrigins in AppConfig.

docs.title: Request body for the docs
docs.text:
Give a post, put or patch route a body schema to show the body in the OpenAPI docs. It does not check the request. To check input, use a DTO.

Route.post('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store,
    body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
      'title': v.string().min(3),
    }));

docs.title: Mount a raw handler
docs.text:
A mount sends every request under a path prefix to a raw HttpRequest handler. Socket.IO uses it:

Route.mount('/socket.io/', io.handle);

Warning

By default a mount skips all middleware, also the global middleware (security headers, CSRF, rate limit). Set middleware: true to run the global middleware before the handler. The global CORS config never applies to a mount. The handler must send its own CORS headers.

Route.mount('/admin', admin.handle, middleware: true);

Remove a mount with the same prefix:

Route.unmount('/admin');

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Controller: put the route code in a class.
  • Middleware: run code before and after a route.
  • Request: read the input of a request.

docs.title: Serializer
docs.text:
A serializer sets the JSON shape of a response: which keys the client gets, their names and their values.

It works with any Dart type: a model, a plain class or a map. A controller can also return a model, a map or a list as it is. See Response. To only hide some model fields, use hidden.

docs.title: Create a serializer
docs.text:
Make a serializer with the CLI. It writes lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart, for the model with the same name:

dox make:serializer Blog

docs.title: Writing a serializer
docs.text:
Extend Serializer<T> and write convert. It gets one value and gives one JSON object:

lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

import 'package:my_app/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart';

class BlogSerializer extends Serializer<Blog> {
  BlogSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Blog m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'uid': m.id,
      'title_en': m.title,
    };
  }
}

Return the serializer from a controller, with one model or a list:

lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
class BlogController {
  Future<BlogSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    List<Blog> blogs = await Blog().all();
    return BlogSerializer(blogs); // a list
  }

  Future<BlogSerializer> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
    return BlogSerializer(blog); // one model
  }
}

The response of show:

{
  "uid": 1,
  "title_en": "This is title"
}

This is what the client gets for each input:

You give The client gets one value of type T one JSON object a List<T> a JSON list ([] when the list is empty) null, or any other type null

A List<dynamic>, like a list from jsonDecode, gives null. Call .cast<T>() first. See JSON from another API.

docs.title: Getting the JSON
docs.text:
toJson() gives the map, the list or null, for use in other code:

dynamic json = BlogSerializer(blogs).toJson();

docs.title: Change values
docs.text:
Format dates, join fields and add new keys:

lib/app/serializers/user.serializer.dart
class UserSerializer extends Serializer<User> {
  UserSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(User m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'name': '${m.firstName} ${m.lastName}',
      'is_active': m.status == 'active',
      'joined_at': m.createdAt?.toIso8601String(),
    };
  }
}

docs.title: A serializer inside a serializer
docs.text:
Use the serializer of a relation inside the other one:

lib/app/serializers/comment.serializer.dart
class CommentSerializer extends Serializer<Comment> {
  CommentSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Comment m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'content': m.content,
      'user': UserSerializer(m.user).toJson(), // null when there is no user
    };
  }
}

Load the relation first, with preload:

Future<CommentSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
  return CommentSerializer(comments);
}

docs.title: With pagination
docs.text:
Put the serializer output in place of data of the page:

Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}

See Pagination.

docs.title: A plain Dart class
docs.text:
A serializer for a plain class works the same way:

lib/app/serializers/weather.serializer.dart
class Weather {
  final String city;
  final double celsius;

  Weather(this.city, this.celsius);
}

class WeatherSerializer extends Serializer<Weather> {
  WeatherSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Weather m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'city': m.city,
      'celsius': m.celsius,
      'fahrenheit': m.celsius * 9 / 5 + 32,
    };
  }
}

docs.title: Rows from the query builder
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.table(...) gives rows as maps. Use Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> to pick and rename the keys:

lib/app/serializers/sales_report.serializer.dart
class SalesReportSerializer extends Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> {
  SalesReportSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Map<String, dynamic> m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'product': m['name'],
      'sold': m['total'],
    };
  }
}

Future<SalesReportSerializer> report(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('orders')
      .selectRaw('name, count(*) as total')
      .groupBy('name')
      .get();
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows);
}

docs.title: JSON from another API
docs.text:
Cast the list to the type of the serializer first:

Future<SalesReportSerializer> remote(DoxRequest req) async {
  String body = await fetchReport(); // your HTTP call
  List<dynamic> rows = jsonDecode(body);
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows.cast<Map<String, dynamic>>());
}

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Response: other values a controller can return.
  • CLI: dox make:serializer: the make command.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
A session keeps data for one browser across many requests, like the logged in user or a shopping cart.

Dox gives every browser a session cookie and keeps the data for that cookie. Web pages with forms and logins need a session. An API with tokens does not.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add SessionMiddleware to globalMiddleware. Session forms also need CSRF protection, so add CsrfMiddleware after it:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(except: <String>['/api/*']),
  ],
);

Now every request has req.session. On a route with no session middleware, req.session throws.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set session in the app config. Set only the options you want to change:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  session: const SessionConfig(
    driver: 'cache',
    store: 'redis',
    lifetime: Duration(hours: 2),
  ),
);
Option Default What it does driver cookie cookie or cache. See Drivers. store null The cache store for the cache driver, like redis. null uses the default store. cookie dox_session The name of the session cookie. lifetime 2 hours The session ends after this time with no use. path / The path of the cookie. domain null The domain of the cookie. null means only the host that set it. httpOnly true Page scripts can not read the cookie. secure null null sets Secure when the request came over https. sameSite lax The SameSite of the cookie.

To give one middleware its own config, use SessionMiddleware(SessionConfig(...)).

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
The driver decides where the data is kept:

  • cookie: all data is in the cookie, encrypted with your APP_KEY. A cookie holds about 4 KB, so store an id, not a full object. An old copy of the cookie works until the lifetime ends, also after logout.
  • cache: the cookie holds only a session id, and the data is in a cache store. On logout the data is deleted.

For more than one server, use the cache driver with a shared store like redis or database. The memory store is shared by the isolates of one server only, and it is lost when the server stops.

docs.title: Retrieving data
docs.text:
Read a value. The second argument is the default for a missing key:

String? name = req.session.get('name');
List<dynamic> cart = req.session.get('cart', <int>[]);

docs.title: Retrieving all data
docs.text:
Get a copy of all session data:

Map<String, dynamic> data = req.session.all();

docs.title: Checking if a value exists
docs.text:
has gives true when the key is in the session and its value is not null:

if (req.session.has('cart')) {
  // ...
}

docs.title: Storing data
docs.text:
Store a value. It must be a JSON type: a map, a list, a string, a number, a bool or null:

req.session.put('cart', <int>[1, 2]);

docs.title: Retrieving and deleting a value
docs.text:
Read a value and remove it in one step:

dynamic cart = req.session.pull('cart');

docs.title: Flash data
docs.text:
Flash data stays for the current request and the next one, like a "saved" message after a redirect:

req.session.flash('message', 'The post is saved');
return redirect('/posts');

On the next page, req.session.get('message') gives the text.

docs.title: Keeping flash data
docs.text:
Keep all flash data for one more request, or only some keys:

req.session.reflash();
req.session.keep(<String>['message']);

docs.title: Deleting data
docs.text:
Remove one value, or all data:

req.session.forget('cart');
req.session.flush();

docs.title: Regenerating the session ID
docs.text:
Give the user a new session id at login. This stops a session fixation attack. It also gives a new CSRF token and keeps the data:

req.session.regenerate();

regenerate(keepToken: true) keeps the CSRF token, for forms in other tabs. Do not use it at login.

At logout, remove all data and get a new id:

req.session.invalidate();

Session login from dox_auth does both for you.

docs.title: CSRF token
docs.text:
